When determining whether a feed entity has entered or exited a fence polygon, there are two spatial operations that can be used: Intersects: the feed geometry must intersect the fence polygon. Contains: the feed geometry must be contained by the fence polygon.
These operations determine whether a fence polygon has been entered, and also when it has been exited (the feed geometry no longer intersects or is no longer contained by the fence polygon). Because the contains condition is more strict than intersects (a geometry can intersect another geometry without being contained by it) it tends to result in fewer notifications when the two geometries are nearby. By using different combinations of these rules for enter and exit, you can control the likelihood that notifications will be sent.
Note that when the feed geometry is a RT_PointHandle, there is no difference between intersection and containment, so both options behave the same. When using a RT_LocationGeotriggerFeedHandle, set RT_FenceGeotrigger_getFeedAccuracyMode to RT_FenceGeotriggerFeedAccuracyMode_useGeometryWithAccuracy in order to create a polygon geometry that accounts for the area of uncertainty around a RT_Location_getPosition. Since: 100.13.0

member.name: F:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreFenceEnterExitSpatialRelationship.EnterIntersectsAndExitDoesNotIntersect
member.summary: The fence polygon is entered when it intersects a RT_GeotriggerFeedHandle entity and exited when it no longer intersects.
member.remarks: This option tends to increase the number of notifications as an entity approaches a fence polygon. Use this option when you want to receive all possible notifications - for example, when you want to be warned that you are approaching a hazard. This option has no effect unless the feed entity geometry is a RT_PolygonHandle. Set RT_FenceGeotrigger_getFeedAccuracyMode to RT_FenceGeotriggerFeedAccuracyMode_useGeometryWithAccuracy to create a polygon geometry that accounts for the area of uncertainty around a RT_Location_getPosition. Since: 100.13.0

member.name: F:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreFenceEnterExitSpatialRelationship.EnterContainsAndExitDoesNotContain
member.summary: The fence polygon is entered when it contains the entity from a RT_GeotriggerFeedHandle and exited when the entity is no longer contained.
member.remarks: This option limits notifications to when the entity is fully within the fence polygon. Use this option to be certain you are within a given fence - for example when carrying out work within a specific land parcel. This option has no effect unless the feed entity geometry is a RT_PolygonHandle. Set RT_FenceGeotrigger_getFeedAccuracyMode to RT_FenceGeotriggerFeedAccuracyMode_useGeometryWithAccuracy to create a polygon geometry that accounts for the area of uncertainty around a RT_Location_getPosition. Since: 100.13.0

member.name: F:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreFenceEnterExitSpatialRelationship.EnterContainsAndExitDoesNotIntersect
member.summary: The fence polygon is entered when it contains a RT_GeotriggerFeedHandle entity and exited when it no longer intersects.
member.remarks: This option tends to minimize the number of notifications. The entity must be fully within the fence polygon to enter and must be fully outside to exit. This combination reduces the number of spurious notifications that occur as you move around the border of a fence. Use this option when you want to limit notifications - for example, when driving past properties on your way to a delivery address. This option has no effect unless the feed entity geometry is a RT_PolygonHandle. Set RT_FenceGeotrigger_getFeedAccuracyMode to RT_FenceGeotriggerFeedAccuracyMode_useGeometryWithAccuracy in order to create a polygon geometry that accounts for the area of uncertainty around a RT_Location_getPosition. Since: 100.13.0

member.name: T:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreFenceGeotrigger
member.summary: A RT_GeotriggerHandle that defines regions or fences to be monitored using a RT_GeotriggerMonitorHandle.
member.remarks: You can monitor areas of interest with a RT_FenceGeotriggerHandle, using spatial rules like enter or exit. This type of operation is also known as "Geofencing". Three main components comprise a RT_FenceGeotriggerHandle: The RT_GeotriggerFeedHandle that is monitored for changes - usually the device location read from a RT_LocationDataSourceHandle. The RT_FenceRuleType that describes the check that is performed with the feed and fence data - for example, "enters within 50 meters of". The RT_FenceParametersHandle that the feed data are evaluated against. For example, a set of polygon features representing areas of interest. The RT_FenceParametersHandle can cover many features or graphics that are checked. Since: 100.12.0

member.name: P:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreFenceGeotrigger.FeedAccuracyMode
member.summary: Gets or sets the describes how a RT_FenceGeotriggerHandle uses accuracy information from a RT_GeotriggerFeedHandle.
member.remarks:
This property controls how the accuracy information from a RT_GeotriggerFeedHandle is used to provide the RT_GeometryHandle for checking a RT_GeotriggerHandle condition. In particular, you can choose how to use the RT_Location_getHorizontalAccuracy property to reflect the uncertainty around a fixed RT_Location_getPosition. Due to various factors, GPS positions may be inaccurate, with RT_Location_getHorizontalAccuracy representing a radius that defines the area containing the actual location. Spurious notifications may occur when the RT_Location_getPosition is inaccurate and is incorrectly reported as inside or outside of a fence. You can use the RT_Location_getHorizontalAccuracy to account for that uncertainty. This property is used in conjunction with RT_FenceGeotrigger_getEnterExitSpatialRelationship to affect when notifications are sent. The default value is RT_FenceGeotriggerFeedAccuracyMode_useGeometry.
Note that you can also use an RT_ArcadeExpressionHandle with the RT_LocationGeotriggerFeed_getFilter property to reject RT_LocationHandle objects with a poor accuracy. Since: 100.13.0
member.value: Describes how a RT_FenceGeotriggerHandle uses accuracy information from a RT_GeotriggerFeedHandle.

member.name: T:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreFileRequest
member.summary: *Internal Use* Represents a request to download a file directly to disk.
member.remarks:
RT_FileRequestHandle adds a number of properties and methods to RT_RequestHandle to support performing a download of a file directly to disk. The location to write the completed download is specified by the RT_FileRequest_getFilePath property. Clients respond to a file request in the usual way via a notification from RT_Requestable_setRequestRequiredCallback. A file request has the RT_Request_getObjectType to RT_RequestType_fileRequest. Guidelines for implementation are: Avoid reading the file into memory as it can be very large, the file should be streamed to disk. For example tile package (.tpk) files can be gigabytes in size. Implementations can make use of platform-specific "background download" service to download files while an app is suspended Alternatively, an implementation could use http requests and specifically http range requests to stream a file down in chunks Consider implementing resiliency to network outages. Some background download services provide this and retry a number of times before failing the overall request. While the download is in progress any partial file must not use the filename specified in RT_FileRequest_getFilePath and prefer to use a temp directory. See RT_FileRequest_getFilePath for details. If progress of the download can be obtained use RT_FileRequest_setTotalBytesToReceive and RT_FileRequest_setCurrentBytesReceived to report it To support resuming a file download after app termination and restart, the RT_FileRequest_getPersistentRequestId should be used to store content needed to reconnect to the download. See RT_FileRequest_getPersistentRequestId for more details. A file request may be paused. Respond to this by checking the RT_FileRequest_getIsPaused property, changes are notified by the event RT_FileRequest_setIsPausedChangedCallback. See RT_FileRequest_getIsPaused for more details. When the download has successfully completed, the file must be present at the specified RT_FileRequest_getFilePath. A call to RT_Request_handleResponse completes the request. Supply the data parameter with a 0 size and null data pointer. The ArcGIS runtime will check the file exists then proceed to use as part of its current operation. If a download fails, respond with an error in the same way as other types of request with a call to RT_Request_handleResponse. Pass the parameter 'userDefinedError' with the platform specific error contained in a RT_ClientReferenceHandle instance.
Many file requests can be issued in some scenarios. For example downloading many delta files for scheduled updates workflow as part of RT_OfflineMapSyncJobHandle. The client code or the platform OS can determine if throttling the number of simultaneous file requests is required. Internal Use This should not be exposed to external Esri developers. Since: 100.0.0

member.name: P:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreFileRequest.FilePath
member.summary: *Internal Use* Gets the file path of the request.
member.remarks: This path is the file path where the request response should put the file when the download is successfully complete. While the download is in progress any partial file must not use the filename specified in RT_FileRequest_getFilePath. This avoids incomplete and invalid files being left on the system. Consider using a file extension like '.temp' until the file download is complete. Prefer to download partial in-progress files to a temp directory using unique names to prevent clashing. When complete move the file to the destination RT_FileRequest_getFilePath. This will ensure abandoned downloads can be cleaned up. Internal Use This should not be exposed to external Esri developers. Since: 100.0.0
member.value: The file path of the request.

member.name: P:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreFileRequest.IsPaused
member.summary: *Internal Use* Gets a value indicating whether the file download should be paused.
member.remarks:
Changes to this property are notified by RT_FileRequest_setIsPausedChangedCallback. When this property changes from false to true the client API file download should be paused. Similarly, when changing from true to false the download can resume. An example implementation of this would be if http range requests are used to download chunks of a file, when the file request is paused then no more requests for chunks are issued until this property becomes false. If a chunk of a file is being downloaded when pause is called then continue to complete the chunk and write to the file before pausing for the next chunk.
If pausing the request cannot be supported, for example there is no support for http range requests, then the pause can be ignored and the file continues to download to complete the request as normal.
Alternatively, the request can be cancelled then restarted when resumed, this choice may depend on how much of the file has been downloaded if this is known.
The main use of pausing file requests is from RT_JobHandle. A call to RT_Job_pause will pause any in-progress RT_FileRequestHandle instances. Resuming a paused file request is triggered by a call to RT_Job_start, when the job was previously paused.
Completing a file request while paused simply completes the request as usual. In this case a paused RT_JobHandle will not proceed to the next step. Internal Use This should not be exposed to external Esri developers. Since: 100.7.0
member.value: Indicates the file download should be paused.

member.name: P:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreFileRequest.PersistentRequestId
member.summary: *Internal Use* Gets or sets a string that can set to any content and subsequently read to resume a previous download after serialization and deserialization.
member.remarks:
This property can be set and read at any time during the the life of a RT_FileRequestHandle and can contain a string with any required content to reconnect and resume an in-progress download. This property is not modified by the core code issuing the file request. When the owning instance of the file request, typically a RT_JobHandle, is serialized then all in-progress file requests have their RT_FileRequest_getPersistentRequestId read and the value is stored along with the RT_JobHandle's state.
After deserialization the same content will be restored into the file request before it's issued through RT_Request_handleResponse.
The client code can use this content to reconnect to a partially complete download. This may be a background download service or other locations and values on the system.
The client code needs to robustly deserialize this value and handle any content changes across different versions of runtime.
This property helps support efficiently resuming a RT_JobHandle after an app termination and restart. Internal Use This should not be exposed to external Esri developers. Since: 100.0.0
member.value: A string that can set to any content and subsequently read to resume a previous download after serialization and deserialization.

member.name: M:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreFileRequest.SetCurrentBytesReceived(System.Int64)
member.summary: *Internal Use* This method can be called to report progress of a file download.
member.remarks:
Before calling this function, call RT_FileRequest_setTotalBytesToReceive to set in the total size of the file in bytes. As a file download progresses repeatedly call RT_FileRequest_setCurrentBytesReceived passing in the current size of the download until the file is complete and the current bytes is equal to the total bytes. These properties are used to calculate a progress percentage reported to other parts of the API, in particular to RT_Job_getProgress. Progress is calculated by dividing the current bytes by the total with the following exceptions: If the total or current bytes is less than or equal to 0 the progress is considered to be 0 If the current bytes is greater than total bytes the progress is considered to be 100
If the current bytes is less than the previous value the progress is not updated Internal Use This should not be exposed to external Esri developers. Since: 100.1.0
member.param: The number of bytes acquired so far.

member.name: M:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreFileRequest.SetTotalBytesToReceive(System.Int64)
member.summary: *Internal Use* Use this method to supply file download progress when file sizes are known in advance.
member.remarks:
Pass in the total number of bytes of the file being downloaded, then as the file is downloaded use RT_FileRequest_setCurrentBytesReceived as chunks of the file are downloaded. These properties are used to calculate a progress percentage reported to other parts of the API, in particular to RT_Job_getProgress. Progress is calculated by dividing the current bytes by the total with the following exceptions: If the total or current bytes is less than or equal to 0 the progress is considered to be 0 If the current bytes is greater than total bytes the progress is considered to be 100
If the current bytes is less than the previous value the progress is not updated Internal Use This should not be exposed to external Esri developers. Since: 100.1.0
member.param: The total number of bytes that will ultimately be passed to this file request.

member.summary: Manages the data displayed by a floor-aware map or scene, allowing filtering based on floor levels.
member.remarks: A RT_FloorManagerHandle must be loaded before you can access its site, facility, and level properties. When a map's floor manager is loaded, floor-aware layers display only data associated with the ground floor by default. When a scene's floor manager is loaded, floor-aware layers display data from all floors by default. You can filter the data displayed by floor-aware layers by toggling the RT_FloorLevel_getIsVisible property of levels in the floor manager. The RT_FloorManagerHandle will fail to load if: The map/scene associated with the floor manager is not floor-aware. The mandatory facility or level layer doesn't exist. It is unable to get the facilities or levels from their respective layers. It is unable to get the sites from a specified site layer. Since: 100.12.0

member.name: T:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreFrameCameraAddRastersParameters
member.summary: Adds raster datasets to a RT_MosaicDatasetRasterHandle by setting various parameters including the use of frame and camera text files.
member.remarks: Mosaic datasets (via the RT_MosaicDatasetRasterHandle class) are used to manage, display, serve, and share raster data. When you create a new mosaic dataset, it is created as an empty container in a geodatabase to which you can add raster data. The FrameCameraAddRastersParameters object provides the mechanism to set various properties including the use of camera and frame text files so that a raster can be added to a mosaic dataset via the RT_MosaicDatasetRaster_addRasters method. Some of the parameters (aka. properties) on RT_FrameCameraAddRastersParametersHandle class that enable adding a raster into a mosaic dataset include specifying, the file filter type (like .tif or .jpg) of the rasters that are to be included (RT_AddRastersParameters_getFilter property), the directory location (RT_AddRastersParameters_getInputDirectory property) of the raster files, the minimum pixel cell size of the raster to be included (RT_AddRastersParameters_getMinPixelSizeFactor property) and more. Unique attributes of using the FrameCameraAddRastersParameters class rather than the parent RT_AddRastersParametersHandle class have to do with defining 'frame' and 'camera' text files which specify how a raster image was captured from a satellite or aircraft. The frame and camera table files refers to a single perspective imaging camera with an optical lens that can be modeled as a pinhole. To define the frame table use the RT_FrameCameraAddRastersParameters_getFramesFile property, see the ArcGIS Pro document entitled 'Frames table schema' ( https://pro.arcgis.com/en/pro-app/help/data/imagery/frames-table-schema.htm ) for more information. To define the camera table use the RT_FrameCameraAddRastersParameters_getCamerasFile property, see the ArcGIS Pro document entitled 'Cameras table schema' ( https://pro.arcgis.com/en/pro-app/help/data/imagery/cameras-table-schema.htm ) for more information. Since: 100.0.0

member.name: P:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreGenerateGeodatabaseParameters.AttachmentSyncDirection
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether the direction for attachments to be synchronized.
member.remarks: This parameter is available when the service resource sync capabilities includes supportsAttachmentsSyncDirection. This parameter defines how attachments will be synced and is only applicable if the feature service has attachments. RT_AttachmentSyncDirection_bidirectional - Attachment edits can be both uploaded from the client and downloaded from the service when syncing. RT_AttachmentSyncDirection_upload - Attachment edits can only be uploaded from the client when syncing. This is useful in cases where the data collector does not want to consume space with attachments from the service, but does need to collect new attachments. RT_AttachmentSyncDirection_none - Attachment edits are never synced from either the client or the server. When RT_GenerateGeodatabaseParameters_getReturnAttachments is set to true, you can set RT_GenerateGeodatabaseParameters_getAttachmentSyncDirection to either RT_AttachmentSyncDirection_bidirectional (default) or RT_AttachmentSyncDirection_upload. In this case, create replica includes attachments from the service. When RT_GenerateGeodatabaseParameters_getReturnAttachments is set to false, you can set RT_GenerateGeodatabaseParameters_getAttachmentSyncDirection to either RT_AttachmentSyncDirection_upload or RT_AttachmentSyncDirection_none (default). In this case, the geodatabase does not include attachments from the service. Attachment sync direction is set during the RT_GeodatabaseSyncTask_generateGeodatabase operation and cannot be overridden during RT_GeodatabaseSyncTask_syncGeodatabaseWithSyncDirection . Since: 100.0.0
member.value: Specifies the direction for attachments to be synchronized.

member.name: T:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreGenerateOfflineMapParameterOverrides
member.summary: Gives access to the individual parameters objects that will generate the various geodatabase, vector tile and tile cache packages that make up the data of an offline map.
member.remarks: This object allows the user more fine-grained control over the generation of an offline map than the options presented in the standard RT_GenerateOfflineMapParametersHandle. For example, the parameter overrides allow the user to adjust specific layers so that they: use a different spatial extent or scale range; use custom attribute or geometry settings; are omitted from the download. An instance of this object can be created from the overall map settings in RT_GenerateOfflineMapParametersHandle by calling RT_OfflineMapTask_createGenerateOfflineMapParameterOverridesAsync. This object gives access to the individual parameter objects via three dictionaries containing generate geodatabase parameters, export tile cache parameters and export vector tile parameters. These can be accessed using RT_GenerateOfflineMapParameterOverrides_getGenerateGeodatabaseParameters, RT_GenerateOfflineMapParameterOverrides_getExportTileCacheParameters and RT_GenerateOfflineMapParameterOverrides_getExportVectorTilesParameters respectively. The dictionaries contain the various parameters objects mapped against an RT_OfflineMapParametersKeyHandle. An RT_OfflineMapParametersKeyHandle represents the service that a particular parameters object is intended for. The RT_OfflineMapParametersKey_createWithLayer, RT_OfflineMapParametersKey_createWithTable, or RT_OfflineMapParametersKey_createWithUtilityNetwork can be used to construct a key given its respective layer, table, or utility network. The returned key can be used to look up a value in a dictionary. The type of dictionary is indicated by the key's RT_OfflineMapParametersKey_getType property. Note that a given parameters key/value pair may be shared by multiple layers in the map: for example a single RT_GenerateGeodatabaseParametersHandle could represent the online settings for multiple feature layers that all access the same underlying feature service. All entries in the dictionaries should correspond to layers and table instances in the online RT_MapHandle. If a dictionary entry is removed the corresponding layers or tables will be removed from the offline map without raising an error. Since: 100.4.0

member.name: P:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreGenerateOfflineMapParameterOverrides.OnlineLayers
member.summary: Gets the this list indicates layers that will not be taken offline and will continue to reference online services.
member.remarks:
In some situations, you may wish to prevent a layer from being taken offline even though it is supported. For example, by continuing to reference the live online service for a RT_FeatureLayerHandle, you can benefit from the most up-to-date information. You can choose to keep layers from the map's operational layers or basemap layers collections online. To make the offline map continue to reference an online layer add it to the RT_GenerateOfflineMapParameterOverrides_getOnlineLayers collection. By adding a RT_LayerHandle to this list, you indicate that the layer will not be taken offline but will instead continue to reference the online service. Be aware that the resulting offline map will require a network connection and may also require authentication. Note that if a RT_LayerHandle is included in this collection it will not be taken offline - you should update the relevant parameters to remove the details pertaining to that layer: RT_GenerateOfflineMapParameterOverrides_getExportTileCacheParameters can be removed to prevent an RT_ArcGISTiledLayerHandle from being taken offline RT_GenerateOfflineMapParameterOverrides_getExportVectorTilesParameters can be removed to prevent an RT_ArcGISVectorTiledLayerHandle from being taken offline RT_GenerateOfflineMapParameterOverrides_getGenerateGeodatabaseParameters can be removed for an entire feature service or updated to remove an individual RT_FeatureLayerHandle using RT_GenerateGeodatabaseParameters_getLayerOptions
If a feature service contains many tables in the web map, you can choose to keep specific layers online by adding them to the RT_GenerateOfflineMapParameterOverrides_getOnlineLayers collection and updating the RT_GenerateOfflineMapParameterOverrides_getGenerateGeodatabaseParameters to remove the specific layers. Any remaining feature layers or stand-alone tables that you wish to take offline can be configured using the RT_GenerateGeodatabaseParameters_getLayerOptions for the service in RT_GenerateOfflineMapParameterOverrides_getGenerateGeodatabaseParameters.
When you create a RT_GenerateOfflineMapParameterOverridesHandle object, this collection will be populated according to the RT_GenerateOfflineMapParameters_getOnlineOnlyServicesOption setting in the original parameters. Things to consider are: If you set RT_GenerateOfflineMapParameters_getOnlineOnlyServicesOption to RT_OnlineOnlyServicesOption_exclude then this collection will be empty If you set RT_GenerateOfflineMapParameters_getOnlineOnlyServicesOption to RT_OnlineOnlyServicesOption_include then this collection will contain each online-only RT_LayerHandle in the web map. For example, layers that cannot be taken offline. If you set RT_GenerateOfflineMapParameters_getOnlineOnlyServicesOption to RT_OnlineOnlyServicesOption_useAuthoredSettings then this collection will contain each RT_LayerHandle that the web map author selected to remain online Since: 100.9.0
member.value: This list indicates layers that will not be taken offline and will continue to reference online services.

member.name: P:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreGenerateOfflineMapParameterOverrides.OnlineTables
member.summary: Gets the this list indicates tables that will not be taken offline and will continue to reference online services.
member.remarks:
In some situations, you may wish to prevent a non-spatial table from being taken offline even though it is supported. For example, by continuing to reference the live online RT_ServiceFeatureTableHandle, you can benefit from the most up- to-date information. To make the offline map continue to reference an online table, you add it to the RT_GenerateOfflineMapParameterOverrides_getOnlineTables collection. By adding a RT_ServiceFeatureTableHandle to this list, you indicate that the table will not be taken offline and it will continue to reference the online source. Be aware that the resulting offline map will require a network connection and may require authentication. Note that if a RT_ServiceFeatureTableHandle is included in this collection it will not be taken offline - you should update the RT_GenerateOfflineMapParameterOverrides_getGenerateGeodatabaseParameters to remove that table.
If a feature service contains many layers in the web map, you can choose to keep specific tables online by adding them to the RT_GenerateOfflineMapParameterOverrides_getOnlineTables collection. Any remaining tables that you wish to take offline can be configured using the service's RT_GenerateGeodatabaseParameters_getLayerOptions in the RT_GenerateOfflineMapParameterOverrides_getGenerateGeodatabaseParameters.
When you create a RT_GenerateOfflineMapParameterOverridesHandle object, this collection will be populated according to the RT_GenerateOfflineMapParameters_getOnlineOnlyServicesOption setting in the original parameters. Things to consider are: If you set RT_GenerateOfflineMapParameters_getOnlineOnlyServicesOption to RT_OnlineOnlyServicesOption_exclude then this collection will be empty If you set RT_GenerateOfflineMapParameters_getOnlineOnlyServicesOption to RT_OnlineOnlyServicesOption_include then this collection will contain each online-only RT_ServiceFeatureTableHandle in the web map. For example, layers that cannot be taken offline. because they are not sync-enabled. If you set RT_GenerateOfflineMapParameters_getOnlineOnlyServicesOption to RT_OnlineOnlyServicesOption_useAuthoredSettings, then this collection will contain each RT_ServiceFeatureTableHandle that the web map author selected to remain online Since: 100.9.0
member.value: This list indicates tables that will not be taken offline and will continue to reference online services.

member.name: P:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreGenerateOfflineMapParameters.AttachmentSyncDirection
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether the direction for attachments to be synchronized when syncing offline feature layers. This method should be used in conjunction with RT_GenerateOfflineMapParameters_getReturnLayerAttachmentOption to determine which layers should be taken offline with attachments included.
member.remarks:
This property is valid when the service resource sync capabilities includes supportsAttachmentsSyncDirection otherwise it is ignored. This property works in conjunction with RT_GenerateOfflineMapParameters_getReturnLayerAttachmentOption and in some cases may have its value overridden by RT_GenerateOfflineMapParameters_getReturnLayerAttachmentOption. The table below shows the valid combinations of values for layer attachment options and attachment sync direction. The notes column explains where the behavior for a given layer may differ from the values set for these properties.
Layer Attachment Option Valid Attachment Sync Direction Note RT_ReturnLayerAttachmentOption_none RT_AttachmentSyncDirection_none RT_AttachmentSyncDirection_upload RT_ReturnLayerAttachmentOption_allLayers RT_AttachmentSyncDirection_upload RT_AttachmentSyncDirection_bidirectional RT_ReturnLayerAttachmentOption_readOnlyLayers RT_AttachmentSyncDirection_none
Layers with attachments will treat this as RT_AttachmentSyncDirection_bidirectional
RT_AttachmentSyncDirection_upload RT_AttachmentSyncDirection_bidirectional
Layers without attachments will treat this as RT_AttachmentSyncDirection_none
RT_ReturnLayerAttachmentOption_editableLayers RT_AttachmentSyncDirection_none
Layers with attachments will treat this as RT_AttachmentSyncDirection_bidirectional
RT_AttachmentSyncDirection_upload RT_AttachmentSyncDirection_bidirectional
Layers without attachments will treat this as RT_AttachmentSyncDirection_none
If RT_GenerateOfflineMapParametersHandle is used in conjunction with RT_GenerateOfflineMapParameterOverridesHandle this property is superseded. Since: 100.1.0

member.name: P:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreGenerateOfflineMapParameters.ContinueOnErrors
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether or not the generate offline map job should continue running in the event of failure to take a layer offline.
member.remarks: If this property is true, failure to take a layer or table offline will not fail the job, the failure will be exposed in the job result. If this property is false, failure to take a layer or table offline will fail the job and no more layers or tables will be taken offline. The layer or table's error will be available as the job's error. The default value is true. Since: 100.4.0

member.name: P:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreGenerateOfflineMapParameters.DestinationTableRowFilter
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether tables will contain all rows or can be filtered to a smaller set of related rows.
member.remarks:
When the property is RT_DestinationTableRowFilter_relatedOnly (the default) this can substantially reduce the number of rows in offline tables to only those that are related to rows from other layers or tables. Only tables present in RT_GeoModel_getTables are considered as candidates for filtering. This does not apply when the table: Is the origin of a relationship and not a destination Is a destination of a relationship from a layer or table that is not in the map Is editable and RT_GenerateOfflineMapParameters_getReturnSchemaOnlyForEditableLayers is true Has a RT_ServiceFeatureTable_getDefinitionExpression and RT_GenerateOfflineMapParameters_getIsDefinitionExpressionFilterEnabled is true
The relationships of a table are accessible via RT_ArcGISFeatureTable_getLayerInfo and the RT_ArcGISFeatureLayerInfo_getRelationshipInfos property.
The default value is RT_DestinationTableRowFilter_relatedOnly.
If set to RT_DestinationTableRowFilter_all then all rows in tables are returned. Since: 100.4.0
member.value: Indicates whether tables will contain all rows or can be filtered to a smaller set of related rows.

member.name: P:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreGenerateOfflineMapParameters.EsriVectorTilesDownloadOption
member.summary: Gets or sets the describes how Esri vector tiled basemap layers will be downloaded.
member.remarks:
This property lets you choose how to download Esri vector tiled basemap layers. This property only applies when taking an Esri vector tile basemap service offline. When taking an Esri vector tiled basemap service offline (e.g. to create a RT_VectorTileCacheHandle on your device), you can choose from different versions of the service depending on your use case. Primary considerations are the download speed and the size of the resulting .vtpk file. Among other things, file size is influenced by the number of fonts downloaded from the service. Esri vector tiled basemap layers use fonts as part of their style resources - see the vector-tile-style documentation . When you take vector tiled layer offline, these fonts are downloaded as part of the RT_VectorTileCacheHandle.
Esri services also offer an alternative version with a reduced font package size. This omits the large Arial Unicode font, which greatly reduces the download size. You can view the set of reduced font vector tile services here .
If you choose RT_EsriVectorTilesDownloadOption_useOriginalService, the full set of resources used by the original online service, including all fonts, will be downloaded. This increases the download size of the RT_VectorTileCacheHandle but ensures that the offline layer will display the same as the original online data.
If you choose RT_EsriVectorTilesDownloadOption_useReducedFontsService, the smaller set of fonts used by the alternative, for export, version of the service will be downloaded. This reduces the download size of the RT_VectorTileCacheHandle but is not suitable for all locales or when your offline vector tiled layer includes certain language characters. For example, this option will not display Chinese, Japanese, Thai, Korean or Georgian characters. If an alternative, for export version of the service cannot be found, the original service will be used.
The default value is RT_EsriVectorTilesDownloadOption_useOriginalService. Since: 100.10.0
member.value: Describes how Esri vector tiled basemap layers will be downloaded.

member.name: P:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreGenerateOfflineMapParameters.IncludeBasemap
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether or not a basemap will be included in the offline map.
member.remarks:
If you do not want a basemap in the offline map then set this property to FALSE. After loading the offline map, your application can programmatically insert a basemap into the map. Note that, a programmatically inserted basemap will not be persisted in the map. If you want a basemap in the offline map then set this property to TRUE. You can choose to either: Generate and download the online basemap using the RT_GenerateOfflineMapJobHandle. This is the default. Use a local basemap on the device by setting the RT_GenerateOfflineMapParameters_getReferenceBasemapDirectory
The default value is true.
This property is superseded if the RT_GenerateOfflineMapParametersHandle is used in conjunction with RT_GenerateOfflineMapParameterOverridesHandle. Since: 100.1.0
member.value: Indicates whether or not a basemap will be included in the offline map.

member.name: P:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreGenerateOfflineMapParameters.IsDefinitionExpressionFilterEnabled
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether feature layer definition expressions are used when taking feature layers and tables offline.
member.remarks:
A value of true allows RT_GenerateOfflineMapJobHandle to use the SQL where clause in RT_FeatureLayer_getDefinitionExpression as a filter when generating offline geodatabases. Applying the definition expression may reduce the number of features taken offline for display and sync. If the value is false this could result in a larger geodatabase than is required to display the feature layer.
The default value is true.
For tables the definition expression is taken from the property RT_ServiceFeatureTable_getDefinitionExpression.
If RT_GenerateOfflineMapParametersHandle is used in conjunction with RT_GenerateOfflineMapParameterOverridesHandle this property is superseded. Since: 100.3.0
member.value: Indicates if feature layer definition expressions are used when taking feature layers and tables offline.

member.summary: Gets or sets the maximum scale for how far in to extract tiles from tiled services. The 0 default means extract the levels down to the most detailed.

This is used as input for levels of detail for RT_TileCacheHandle and RT_VectorTileCacheHandle. This is not applicable to offline data in RT_GeodatabaseHandle. A minScale of 100000 and a maxScale of 500 will select level IDs between 1:500 and 1:100,000 scale.
A minScale of 0 and a maxScale of 500 will select all global level IDs down to 1:500 scale.
A minScale of 100000 and a maxScale of 0 will select level IDs from 1:100,000 scale to the most detailed available level.

member.name: P:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreGenerateOfflineMapParameters.OnlineOnlyServicesOption
member.summary: Gets or sets the describes how data that requires an online service will be handled when taking a map offline.
member.remarks:
Online layers and tables cannot be taken offline in the following situations: The layer or table is using a service that cannot be taken offline. For example, RT_WMSLayerHandle or RT_WMTSLayerHandle. The layer or table is using a service that supports offline, such as an ArcGISFeatureLayer, but synchronization has not been enabled on the service (RT_FeatureServiceCapabilities_getSupportsSync is set to false). Services utilize synchronization to take layers and tables offline and synchronize changes. Online services that cannot be taken offline are referred to as online-only services. Online-only services require network connectivity and may involve authentication. Examples of online-only services include: Dynamic information, such as changing weather or traffic conditions, that delivers frequent and regular updates to the app Large datasets that would be impractical to take offline to a device
This property allows you to specify how online-only data will be handled when taking the map offline. There are three options: RT_OnlineOnlyServicesOption_exclude means that any data that cannot be taken offline will be omitted from the offline map. Choosing this option means that your offline map will not require a network connection but may not include all of the data from the original web map. RT_OnlineOnlyServicesOption_include means that data that cannot be taken offline will be accessed via the URL in the offline map. Choosing this option means that your offline map will retain all of the information from the original web map, but it will require a network connection and may require authentication. RT_OnlineOnlyServicesOption_useAuthoredSettings means that layers and tables will be taken offline, remain online or be omitted from the offline map according to the map author's intent as defined in the web map
The default value is RT_OnlineOnlyServicesOption_exclude. Since: 100.9.0
member.value: Describes how data that requires an online service will be handled when taking a map offline.

member.name: P:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreGenerateOfflineMapParameters.ReferenceBasemapDirectory
member.summary: Gets or sets the path to a directory on the device where the local basemap file is located.
member.remarks:
Set this property to use a basemap that is already on the device (rather than downloading it). The directory should only be set when the parameters have a RT_GenerateOfflineMapParameters_getReferenceBasemapFilename defined. This property supports any directory specified as either: An absolute path A path relative to the parent directory of the generated mobile map package (see downloadPath for RT_OfflineMapTask_generateOfflineMap)
If the directory does not exist, or does not contain the specified basemap, the RT_GenerateOfflineMapJobHandle will fail.
Note that, the mobile map package will store either a relative or absolute path to the reference basemap file so that it can be opened in the future.
A relative path typically begins with "." to denote the parent directory of the resulting mobile map package or ".." to move up one directory. The parent directory of the mobile map package will be set when calling RT_OfflineMapTask_generateOfflineMap.
For example, to generate a mobile map package to "[my root path]/my_offline_maps/my_mobile_map_package", that uses a reference basemap in "[my root path]/other_maps/my_basemap.tpk", you would set the relative path as follows: RT_GenerateOfflineMapJob_getDownloadDirectoryPath to "[my root path]/my_offline_maps/my_mobile_map_package" RT_GenerateOfflineMapParameters_getReferenceBasemapDirectory to "../other_maps" RT_GenerateOfflineMapParameters_getReferenceBasemapFilename to "my_basemap.tpk"
Note that this property is ignored if RT_GenerateOfflineMapParameters_getIncludeBasemap is FALSE. Since: 100.5.0
member.value: The path to a directory on the device where the local basemap file is located.

member.name: P:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreGenerateOfflineMapParameters.ReferenceBasemapFilename
member.summary: Gets or sets the name of a local basemap file on the device that can be used rather than downloading an online basemap.
member.remarks:
The local basemap filename must end with .tpk, .tpkx or .vtpk since these are the supported file formats. This property can be read directly from settings applied by the author of the online web map (see RT_OfflineSettingsHandle) or set by user code to a file known to be on the device. This property will be populated from online settings when created with RT_OfflineMapTask_createDefaultGenerateOfflineMapParametersAsync. If you wish to use the specified local basemap rather than downloading, you must also set RT_GenerateOfflineMapParameters_getReferenceBasemapDirectory. If the directory does not exist, or does not contain the specified basemap, the RT_GenerateOfflineMapJobHandle will fail.
The spatial reference of the reference basemap is used for the offline map when it is different to the online map's spatial reference.
Note that this property is ignored if RT_GenerateOfflineMapParameters_getIncludeBasemap is FALSE. Since: 100.5.0
member.value: The name of a local basemap file on the device that can be used rather than downloading an online basemap.

member.name: P:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreGenerateOfflineMapParameters.ReturnLayerAttachmentOption
member.summary: Gets or sets the which feature layers will include attachments when being taken offline. Attachments can be included with none of the layers, all of the layers, read only layers or editable layers. This method should be used in conjunction with RT_GenerateOfflineMapParameters_getAttachmentSyncDirection to control how the attachments are synced.
member.remarks:
For offline maps, a feature layer is considered to be editable if the feature service has capabilities that include any of create, update or delete. A read-only layer is one that supports sync, but does not have any of create, update or delete capability. Service capabilities are accessible from service infos see RT_ArcGISFeatureServiceInfo_getFeatureServiceCapabilities or RT_ArcGISFeatureLayerInfo_getCapabilities. This property works in conjunction with RT_GenerateOfflineMapParameters_getAttachmentSyncDirection and in some cases may override the value returned by RT_GenerateOfflineMapParameters_getAttachmentSyncDirection. The table below shows the valid combinations of values for layer attachment options and attachment sync direction. The notes column explains where the behavior for a given layer may differ from the values set for these properties. Layer Attachment Option Valid Attachment Sync Direction Note RT_ReturnLayerAttachmentOption_none RT_AttachmentSyncDirection_none RT_AttachmentSyncDirection_upload RT_ReturnLayerAttachmentOption_allLayers RT_AttachmentSyncDirection_upload RT_AttachmentSyncDirection_bidirectional RT_ReturnLayerAttachmentOption_readOnlyLayers RT_AttachmentSyncDirection_none
Layers with attachments will treat this as RT_AttachmentSyncDirection_bidirectional
RT_AttachmentSyncDirection_upload RT_AttachmentSyncDirection_bidirectional
Layers without attachments will treat this as RT_AttachmentSyncDirection_none
RT_ReturnLayerAttachmentOption_editableLayers RT_AttachmentSyncDirection_none
Layers with attachments will treat this as RT_AttachmentSyncDirection_bidirectional
RT_AttachmentSyncDirection_upload RT_AttachmentSyncDirection_bidirectional
Layers without attachments will treat this as RT_AttachmentSyncDirection_none
If RT_GenerateOfflineMapParametersHandle is used in conjunction with RT_GenerateOfflineMapParameterOverridesHandle this property is superseded. Since: 100.1.0
member.value: Which feature layers will include attachments when being taken offline. Attachments can be included with none of the layers, all of the layers, read only layers or editable layers. This method should be used in conjunction with RT_GenerateOfflineMapParameters_getAttachmentSyncDirection to control how the attachments are synced.

member.name: P:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreGenerateOfflineMapParameters.UpdateMode
member.summary: Gets or sets the describes how the offline map will support synchronization with online services.
member.remarks:
A value of RT_GenerateOfflineMapUpdateMode_syncWithFeatureServices instructs the RT_GenerateOfflineMapJobHandle to create offline geodatabases that support syncing with online feature services. A value of RT_GenerateOfflineMapUpdateMode_noUpdates instructs the RT_GenerateOfflineMapJobHandle to disable data synchronization for generated offline geodatabases. In this case, no synchronization replicas will be created on corresponding feature services. This reduces the load on the feature server and frees the developer from needing to unregister server replicas when they are no longer needed. The default value is RT_GenerateOfflineMapUpdateMode_syncWithFeatureServices.
If RT_GenerateOfflineMapParametersHandle is used in conjunction with RT_GenerateOfflineMapParameterOverridesHandle this property is superseded by the RT_GenerateGeodatabaseParameters_getSyncModel property of the overridden layer. Since: 100.9.0
member.value: Describes how the offline map will support synchronization with online services.

member.name: P:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreGeodatabase.GenerateGeodatabaseGeometry
member.summary: Gets the geometry (for example an RT_EnvelopeHandle or RT_PolygonHandle) used to generate a sync enabled geodatabase.
member.remarks: Edits made to a sync enabled RT_GeodatabaseHandle must intersect the geometry used to generate the geodatabase. If an edit is made outside this extent, or area of interest, it will be rejected. This property will return the geometry which was used to create this geodatabase. For example, if the geodatabase was created using a RT_GenerateGeodatabaseJobHandle, this property reflects the RT_GenerateGeodatabaseParameters_getExtent property. If the geometry was created using an RT_GenerateOfflineMapJobHandle, this property reflects the RT_GenerateOfflineMapParameters_getAreaOfInterest property. If the geodatabase was downloaded as part of a RT_PreplannedMapAreaHandle, this property will match the geometry used by the web map author when the map area was created. If no geometry was used to create the geodatabase (for example if it was authored using ArcGIS Pro), this property may be null. This property will also be null until the geodatabase is loaded and the RT_Geodatabase_getLoadStatus is RT_LoadStatus_loaded. Since: 100.7.0
member.value: The geometry (for example an RT_EnvelopeHandle or RT_PolygonHandle) used to generate a sync enabled geodatabase.

member.name: P:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreGeodatabase.MinServerGeneration
member.summary: Gets the minimum server generation number for the geodatabase.
member.remarks:
Server generation numbers indicate the state of a geodatabase (or individual layers) with respect to changes which have been synced with the online service. The number increases as new changes from the online feature service are synced to the local geodatabase. If the RT_Geodatabase_getSyncModel is RT_SyncModel_geodatabase, the value will indicate the server generation number for the entire geodatabase. If the RT_Geodatabase_getSyncModel is RT_SyncModel_layer, the value will be the lowest server generation number for all of the layers in the geodatabase. This property will be -1 if the geodatabase does not support sync (RT_SyncModel_none). This property will be -1 until the geodatabase is RT_LoadStatus_loaded.
Note that this property is only required when using advanced workflows to manually apply pre-generated changes and not when performing a sync directly against the online service. Since: 100.6.0
member.value: The minimum server generation number for the geodatabase.

member.name: T:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreGeodatabaseDeltaInfo
member.summary: Represents the delta files created to synchronize changes to a RT_GeodatabaseHandle.
member.remarks:
A delta geodatabase is a file that contains the changes that have occurred since a mobile replica RT_GeodatabaseHandle was last synchronized with its feature service. See https://developers.arcgis.com/rest/services- reference/enterprise/synchronize-replica.htm for an overview of the delta files used in synchronization. There are two types of delta geodatabase: Local edits, performed on the user's device, are exported as an "upload" delta that is applied to the originating feature service Online edits, performed by other users are requested as a "download" delta which is then applied to the local replica geodatabase.
Delta geodatabases allow you to troubleshoot sync problems. For example, you can inspect the geodatabase changes or you could send the file to the administrator of the feature service.
To access the RT_GeodatabaseDeltaInfoHandle after a sync has completed, set one of the following properties to true: RT_SyncGeodatabaseParameters_getKeepGeodatabaseDeltas. This will populate the RT_SyncGeodatabaseJob_getGeodatabaseDeltaInfo property. RT_OfflineMapSyncParameters_getKeepGeodatabaseDeltas. This will add instances to the RT_OfflineMapSyncJob_getGeodatabaseDeltaInfos property. Since: 100.10.0

member.name: P:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreGeodatabaseSyncTask.APIKey
member.summary: Gets or sets the API key to access API key enabled services and resources in ArcGIS Online.
member.remarks: An API key is a unique key used to authorize access to specific services and resources in ArcGIS Online. It is also used to monitor access to those services. An API key is created and managed in the ArcGIS developer dashboard and is tied to a specific ArcGIS account. In addition to setting an API key at a global level for your application using the RT_ArcGISRuntimeEnvironment_getAPIKey property, you can set an RT_APIKeyResource_getAPIKey property on any ArcGIS Runtime class that implements RT_APIKeyResourceInterface. When you set an individual RT_APIKeyResource_getAPIKey property on an RT_APIKeyResourceInterface it will override the default key at the global level (on the RT_ArcGISRuntimeEnvironment_getAPIKey property, in other words), enabling more granular usage telemetry and management for ArcGIS Online resources used by your app. Classes that expose an API key property by implementing RT_APIKeyResourceInterface include: RT_BasemapHandle RT_ArcGISSceneLayerHandle RT_ArcGISTiledLayerHandle RT_ArcGISVectorTiledLayerHandle RT_ServiceFeatureTableHandle RT_ExportVectorTilesTaskHandle RT_LocatorTaskHandle RT_GeodatabaseSyncTaskHandle RT_ClosestFacilityTaskHandle RT_RouteTaskHandle RT_ServiceAreaTaskHandle RT_ExportTileCacheTaskHandle Since: 100.10.0

member.name: M:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreGeodatabaseSyncTask.CreateDefaultSyncGeodatabaseParametersAsync(RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreGeodatabase)
member.summary: Creates default parameters for a sync geodatabase.
member.remarks: This will populate the parameters with values matching what the sync task's feature service and the geodatabase supports. For a geodatabase with RT_SyncModel_layer then all geodatabase layers will be included. If the service is read-only then the sync direction will be RT_SyncDirection_download. Otherwise the sync direction will be RT_SyncDirection_bidirectional. Non-overloaded method: CreateDefaultSyncGeodatabaseParametersAsync Since: 100.0.0
member.param: a geodatabase to sync.
member.returns: Returns a sync parameters object with defaults populated. The returned RT_TaskHandle contains a RT_SyncGeodatabaseParametersHandle.

member.name: M:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreGeodatabaseSyncTask.CreateDefaultSyncGeodatabaseParametersAsync(RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreGeodatabase,RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreSyncDirection)
member.summary: Creates default parameters for a sync geodatabase using the given sync direction.
member.remarks: This will populate the parameters with values matching what the sync task's feature service and the geodatabase supports. For a geodatabase with RT_SyncModel_layer then all geodatabase layers will be included. A service is editable if it has capabilities that include any of create, update or delete. In this case both RT_SyncDirection_bidirectional and RT_SyncDirection_upload are supported sync directions. Alternatively, a service that does not have create, update or delete capability is considered read-only and only RT_SyncDirection_download will be supported. If the given sync direction is not compatible with the sync task's feature service or the geodatabase is not sync enabled, the returned task will fail. Non-overloaded method: CreateDefaultSyncGeodatabaseParametersWithSyncDirectionAsync Since: 100.3.0
member.param: a geodatabase to sync.
the sync direction to use.
member.returns: Returns a Future containing a sync parameter object of type RT_SyncGeodatabaseParametersHandle with the given sync direction. Other parameters are populated with default values.

member.name: M:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreGeodatabaseSyncTask.ExportDeltaAsync(RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreGeodatabase,System.String)
member.summary: Generates an upload delta geodatabase file containing all the changes since the last sync.
member.remarks:
A delta geodatabase contains the changes that have occurred since a mobile replica RT_GeodatabaseHandle was last- synchronized with the feature service. See https://developers.arcgis.com/rest/services-reference/enterprise/synchronize- replica.htm for an overview of the delta files used in synchronization. An "upload" delta geodatabase contains the local edits, performed on the user's device, to be sent to the originating feature service. When you run this task, any local edits in the RT_GeodatabaseHandle will be exported to the specified output path. The output path should include the full path and file name (ending in ".geodatabase") for the export. The delta file created by this method is not sent to the server and has no impact on any subsequent sync job. You can call this method repeatedly without affecting the state of the local geodatabase.
The task returned by this method has a boolean result that indicates whether or not a delta geodatabase was created.
You should not execute more than one sync on a particular geodatabase at the same time. This includes any operations that export or import deltas from the local RT_GeodatabaseHandle, which are: RT_GeodatabaseSyncTask_exportDeltaAsync RT_GeodatabaseSyncTask_importDeltaAsync RT_SyncGeodatabaseJobHandle RT_OfflineMapSyncJobHandle Non-overloaded method: ExportDeltaAsync Since: 100.10.0
member.param: The geodatabase to generate a delta from.
The path and filename to save the generated delta to.
member.returns: a task that generates a geodatabase delta and has an element type of bool. This bool indicates whether a delta was generated or not.

member.param: The parameters for generate geodatabase.

member.remarks: A delta geodatabase contains the changes that have occurred since a mobile replica RT_GeodatabaseHandle was last- synchronized with the feature service. See https://developers.arcgis.com/rest/services-reference/enterprise/synchronize- replica.htm for an overview of the delta files used in synchronization. A "download" delta geodatabase contains the online edits that will be imported to the local geodatabase. The task returned by this method returns an array of RT_SyncLayerResultHandle. You should not execute more than one sync on a particular geodatabase at the same time. This includes any operations that export or import deltas from the local RT_GeodatabaseHandle, which are: RT_GeodatabaseSyncTask_exportDeltaAsync RT_GeodatabaseSyncTask_importDeltaAsync RT_SyncGeodatabaseJobHandle RT_OfflineMapSyncJobHandle Since: 100.3.0
member.param: The geodatabase to apply a delta to.
The path and filename to import the delta from
member.returns: a task that imports a geodatabase delta and has an element type of RT_ArrayHandle. The array elements are of type RT_SyncLayerResultHandle.

member.summary: Loads the metadata for the object asynchronously.
member.remarks: Loads the metadata if the object is not loaded and always calls RT_Loadable_setDoneLoadingCallback. DOCUMENTATION FOR THE ArcGISFeature IMPLEMENTATION OF Loadable.load ONLY An ArcGISFeature is loadable. Depending on a ServiceFeatureTable's feature request mode, queries on the table can return ArcGISFeature objects which have the minimum set of attributes required for rendering and labeling (and geometries do not include m-values). See RT_ServiceFeatureTable_queryFeaturesWithFieldOptions, RT_FeatureRequestMode_onInteractionCache, and RT_FeatureRequestMode_onInteractionNoCache. To access all attributes in the returned ArcGISFeatures, call this method on each feature. member.name: M:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreGeodatabaseSyncTask.RegisterSyncEnabledGeodatabaseAsync(RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreGeodatabase)
member.summary: Registers a copy of a sync enabled geodatabase with a service to allow the copy to sync changes.
member.remarks: This method is typically used as part of services pattern workflow, sometimes known as a pre-planned workflow. A sync enabled geodatabase is generated centrally and not modified or synced. Copies of this original geodatabase are distributed and loaded onto each user's device. The copy must first be registered with the service to allow the server to identify changes in subsequent sync operations. One of the main benefits of this workflow is a reduction in server load to generate geodatabases for many clients. It is important not to sync the copy before registering to ensure the server can maintain consistent state on each copy. This operation is not the opposite of RT_GeodatabaseSyncTask_unregisterGeodatabaseAsync which is used to remove a geodatabase from the service prior to deletion. Since: 100.0.0
member.param: a geodatabase to register.
member.returns: Returns a task that registers a geodatabase with the service.

member.summary: Loads or retries loading metadata for the object asynchronously.
member.remarks: Will retry loading the metadata if the object is failed to load. Will load the object if it is not loaded. Will not retry to load the object if the object is loaded. Will always call the done loading if this is called. Since: 100.0.0

member.name: M:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreGeodatabaseSyncTask.SyncGeodatabase(RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreSyncGeodatabaseParameters,RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreGeodatabase)
member.summary: Returns a job to synchronize a geodatabase back to a service.
member.remarks: For a successfully completed job the job's result returns an array of RT_SyncLayerResultHandle, typically the array is empty. If individual edits failed then the result array provides these errors grouped by each table using RT_SyncLayerResultHandle instances which in turn contain each edit error. You should not execute more than one sync on a particular geodatabase at the same time. This includes any operations that export or import deltas from the local RT_GeodatabaseHandle, which are: RT_GeodatabaseSyncTask_exportDeltaAsync RT_GeodatabaseSyncTask_importDeltaAsync RT_SyncGeodatabaseJobHandle RT_OfflineMapSyncJobHandle Non-overloaded method: SyncGeodatabase Since: 100.0.0
member.param: Parameters to use to sync the geodatabase.
The geodatabase to sync
member.returns: a job to synchronize a geodatabase.

member.summary: Returns a job to synchronize a geodatabase back to its service using the given sync direction and rollback on failure boolean value.
member.remarks: If the given sync direction is not compatible with the sync task's feature service, the returned job will fail. member.summary: Unregisters a geodatabase from a service removing the services replica id.

member.summary: Unregisters a geodatabase from a service removing the service's replica id. This overload uses the geodatabase's sync ID rather than a reference to the geodatabase itself.
member.remarks: This method is used to unregister a geodatabase from a service using the sync ID. This is commonly used to enable cleanup of the service after the local geodatabase has already been deleted. See RT_Geodatabase_getSyncId. After unregistering a geodatabase it can no longer be synced back to the service. member.param: sync ID of geodatabase to unregister.
member.returns: Returns a task that will unregister a geodatabase, the task does not contain a return value. This task will fail if the unregister process is unsuccessful.

member.name: T:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreGeographicTransformation
member.summary: Used to transform coordinates of geometries between spatial references that have two different geographic coordinate systems.
member.remarks:
Each geographic transformation has an input and an output spatial reference. The transformation operates on the horizontal (geographic) datums in each spatial reference. The inverse of the geographic transformation, if any, used to transform in the opposite direction, may be accessed using a member function. A geographic transformation can be constructed from a single geographic transformation step object, or from a list of geographic transformation steps objects that are chained together. Most transformations between spatial references that do not share the WGS 1984 datum use WGS 1984 as an intermediate datum. Thus, it is common to create a geographic transformation object with two geographic transformation steps: first to transform from the datum in the input spatial reference to WGS 1984, and then from WGS 1984 to the output spatial reference's datum. There are a limited number of transformations directly between two non-WGS84 datums, such as WKID 4461, which is NAD_1983_HARN_To_NAD_1983_NSRS2007_1. These do not need WGS 1984 as an intermediate datum.
In most cases, you do not need to construct your own RT_GeographicTransformationHandle. You can get a list of suitable transformations for a given input and output spatial reference using one of the functions on the transformation catalog class.
A geographic transformation object is immutable. Client: DOTNET JAVA KOTLIN OBJECTIVE_C PRO QT RUST SWIFT UNITY UNREAL Since: 100.2.0

member.name: T:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreGeographicTransformationStep
member.summary: Represents a step in the process of transforming between datums.
member.remarks:
Each geographic transformation step can be constructed from a well-known ID (WKID) that represents a geographic transformation. Because the Projection Engine supports thousands of transformations, WKIDs are not presented in the SDK as enumerations. Instead, they are documented in the developers guide. The list of supported WKIDs includes a transformation from every supported datum to WGS 1984. Additionally, there is more limited list of transformations directly between two non-WGS84 datums, such as 4461, which is NAD_1983_HARN_To_NAD_1983_NSRS2007_1. Transformations with more than one step typically go via WGS84, with one forward and one inverse geographic transformation chained together to get the required geographic coordinates.
A geographic transformation step object is immutable. Client: DOTNET JAVA KOTLIN OBJECTIVE_C PRO QT RUST SWIFT UNITY UNREAL Since: 100.2.0

member.name: T:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreGeometry
member.summary: Base class for all classes that represent geometric shapes.
member.remarks:
RT_GeometryHandle is the base class for two-dimensional (x,y) or three-dimensional (x,y,z) geometries. Objects that inherit from the RT_GeometryHandle class may also include a measure (m-value) for each vertex. The RT_GeometryHandle class provides functionality common to all types of geometry. RT_PointHandle, RT_MultipointHandle, RT_PolylineHandle, RT_PolygonHandle, and RT_EnvelopeHandle all inherit from RT_GeometryHandle and represent different types of shapes. RT_GeometryHandle represents real-world objects by defining a shape at a specific geographic location. It is used throughout the API to represent the shapes of features and graphics, layer extents, viewpoints, and GPS locations. It is also used, for example, to define inputs and outputs for spatial analysis and geoprocessing operations and to measure distances and areas. All types of geometry: Have a RT_SpatialReferenceHandle indicating the coordinate system used by its coordinates Can be empty, indicating that they have no specific location or shape May have z-values and/or m-values to define elevation and measures respectively Can be converted to and from JSON to be persisted or to be exchanged directly with REST services
Immutability Most geometries are created and not changed for their lifetime. Examples include features created to be stored in a geodatabase or read from a non-editable layer, and features returned from tasks such as a spatial query, geocode operation, network trace, or geoprocessing task. Immutable geometries (geometries that cannot be changed) offer some important benefits to your app. They are inherently thread-safe, help prevent inadvertent changes, and allow for certain performance optimizations.
Instead of changing the properties of existing geometries, you can create and update geometries using the various subclasses of RT_GeometryBuilderHandle (for example, RT_PolygonBuilderHandle), which can represent the state of a geometry under construction while allowing modifications, thus enabling editing workflows.
Additionally, RT_GeometryEngineHandle offers a range of topological and spatial transformations that read the content of existing geometries and create new geometries, for example, project, buffer, union, and so on. Relational tests such as intersects and overlaps are also available on RT_GeometryEngineHandle.
Coordinate units The coordinates that define a geometry are only meaningful in the context of the geometry's RT_SpatialReferenceHandle. The vertices and spatial reference together allow your app to translate a real-world object from its location on the Earth to its location on your map or scene.
In some cases, a geometry's spatial reference may not be set. For example, a RT_GraphicHandle that does not have a spatial reference is drawn using the same spatial reference as the RT_MapViewHandle to which it was added. If the coordinates are in a different spatial reference, the graphics may not display in the correct location, or at all.
When using RT_GeometryBuilderHandle to create a RT_PolylineHandle or RT_PolygonHandle from a collection of RT_PointHandle, you don't need to set the spatial reference of every point before you add it to the builder, as it will be assigned the spatial reference of the builder itself. In most other cases, such as when using a geometry in geometry operations or when editing a feature table, RT_Geometry_getSpatialReference must be set.
Spatial reference and projection Changing the coordinates of a geometry to have the same shape and location represented using a different RT_SpatialReferenceHandle is known as "projection" or sometimes as "reprojection". Because geometries are immutable, they do not have any member methods that project, transform, or otherwise modify their content. Client: DOTNET JAVA KOTLIN OBJECTIVE_C PRO QT RUST SWIFT UNITY UNREAL Since: 100.0.0

member.name: P:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreGeometry.HasCurves
member.summary: Gets a value indicating whether this geometry contains curve segments; false otherwise.
member.remarks: The ArcGIS Platform supports polygon and polyline geometries that contain curve segments (where RT_Segment_getIsCurve is true, sometimes known as true curves or nonlinear segments). Curves may be present in certain types of data - for example Mobile Map Packages (MMPK) or geometry JSON. When connecting to ArcGIS feature services that ref<a href="ArcGISFeatureServiceInfo.supportsTrueCurve">support curves, ArcGIS Runtime retrieves densified versions of curve feature geometries by default. If a polygon or polyline geometry contains curve segments, this property returns true. Prior to v100.12, it was not possible to access curve segments, and only RT_LineSegmentHandle instances would be returned when iterating through the segments in a RT_PolygonHandle or RT_PolylineHandle object, irrespective of this property. From v100.12, you can use curve segments when using a RT_MultipartBuilderHandle to create or edit polygon and polyline geometries, and also get curve segments when iterating through the segments of existing RT_MultipartHandle geometries when this property returns true. You can also choose to return true curves from feature services by using RT_ArcGISRuntimeEnvironment_getServiceCurveGeometryMode. member.name: M:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreGeometry.Equals(RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreGeometry,System.Double)
member.summary: Check if two geometries are equal to within some tolerance.
member.remarks: This function performs a lightweight comparison of two geometries, such as might be useful when writing test code. It uses the tolerance to compare each of x, y, and any other values the geometries possess (such as z or m) independently in the manner: abs(value1 - value2) <= tolerance. Returns true if the difference of each is within the tolerance and all other properties of the geometries are exactly equal (spatial reference, vertex count, etc.). A single tolerance is used even if the units for the horizontal coordinates and other values differ, e.g horizontal coordinates in degrees and vertical coordinates in meters. This function does not respect modular arithmetic of spatial references which wrap around, so longitudes of -180 and +180 degrees are considered to differ by 360 degrees. Returns false if an error occurs. For topological equality, use relational operators instead of this function. See RT_GeometryEngine_equals. Client: DOTNET JAVA KOTLIN OBJECTIVE_C PRO QT RUST SWIFT UNITY UNREAL Non-overloaded method: EqualsWithTolerance Since: 100.1.0
member.param: The second geometry.
The tolerance.
member.returns: True if the geometries are equal, within the tolerance, otherwise false.

member.name: P:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreGeometryBuilder.IsSketchValid
member.summary: Gets a value indicating whether a geometry builder contains sufficient points to show a valid graphical sketch.
member.remarks:
This can be used as an initial lightweight check to see if the current state of a builder will produce a non-empty geometry; for example, it may be used to enable or disable functionality in an editing user interface. The exact requirements vary depending on the type of geometry produced by the builder: A RT_PointBuilderHandle must contain non- NaN x,y coordinates A RT_MultipointBuilderHandle must contain at least one valid Point An RT_EnvelopeBuilderHandle must contain non-NaN minimum and maximum x and y values A RT_PolylineBuilderHandle must contain at least one RT_MutablePartHandle. Each RT_MutablePartHandle it contains must have: At least two valid points, or At least one RT_SegmentHandle where RT_Segment_getIsCurve is true A RT_PolygonBuilderHandle must contain at least one RT_MutablePartHandle. Each RT_MutablePartHandle it contains must have: At least three valid points, or At least one RT_SegmentHandle where RT_Segment_getIsCurve is true Note that this is not equivalent to topological simplicity, which is enforced by RT_GeometryEngine_simplify and checked using RT_GeometryEngine_isSimple. Geometries must be topologically simple to be successfully saved in a geodatabase or used in some service operations. Does not check the spatial reference. Will return false if an error occurs.
Prior to v100.8, only one part of a multipart polygon or polyline was required to have the minimum number (2 for a polyline, 3 for a polygon) of points, and only RT_LineSegmentHandle instances were supported in builders.
Prior to v100.12, a RT_PolygonBuilderHandle required at least three valid Points in each RT_MutablePartHandle, and at least one part. Client: DOTNET JAVA KOTLIN OBJECTIVE_C PRO QT RUST SWIFT UNITY UNREAL Since: 100.0.0

member.name: T:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreGeometryEngine
member.summary: Performs geometric operations such as spatial relationship tests, reprojections, shape manipulations, topological query and analysis operations on RT_GeometryHandle objects.
member.remarks: Capabilities include: Create new geometries from others with RT_GeometryEngine_buffer, RT_GeometryEngine_clip and RT_GeometryEngine_union Test spatial relationships between geometries such as RT_GeometryEngine_intersects and RT_GeometryEngine_contains Find the RT_GeometryEngine_nearestCoordinate or RT_GeometryEngine_nearestVertex between geometries Reproject a geometry to another RT_SpatialReferenceHandle using RT_GeometryEngine_project Calculate area and length using RT_GeometryEngine_area and RT_GeometryEngine_length, or the geodetic equivalents (RT_GeometryEngine_bufferGeodetic and RT_GeometryEngine_lengthGeodetic) that account for the curvature of the earth RT_GeometryEngineHandle generally operates in two dimensions; operations do not account for z-values unless documented as such for a specific method (for example RT_GeometryEngine_project will transform z-values in some cases). Geodetic methods are better suited to data that have a geographic spatial reference (see RT_SpatialReference_getIsGeographic), especially for large-area, small-scale use, while planar methods are suitable to data that have a projected coordinate system, especially for local, large-scale areas. Geodetic methods indicate this in the name, for example GeometryEngine.bufferGeodetic(Geometry, double, LinearUnit, double, GeodeticCurveType). Client: DOTNET JAVA KOTLIN OBJECTIVE_C PRO QT RUST SWIFT UNITY UNREAL Since: 100.0.0

member.name: M:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreGeometryEngine.AutoComplete(RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreVector,RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreVector)
member.summary: Fills the closed gaps between polygons using polygon boundaries and polylines as the boundary for the new polygons.
member.remarks:
The new polygons are created in the closed empty areas bounded by the edges of the existing polygon boundaries and the new boundary polylines. The newly created polygons do not overlap any existing polygons or polylines, and the boundary of a new polygon must contain at least one edge from the polylines. Only polygons that intersect the input polylines will participate in the operation, so it makes sense to prefilter the input accordingly. The geometries in existing_boundaries must all have an area, i.e. be polygons or envelopes. The geometries in new_boundaries must all be polylines.
The geometries in existing_boundaries and new_boundaries must have consistent spatial references. Client: DOTNET JAVA KOTLIN OBJECTIVE_C PRO QT RUST SWIFT UNITY UNREAL Since: 100.1.0
member.param: The polygons.
The polylines.
member.returns: The new polygons that were created. If either existing_boundaries or new_boundaries is empty, returns an empty array. Returns null on error.

member.name: M:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreGeometryEngine.Cut(RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreGeometry,RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CorePolyline)
member.summary: Cut the 'geometry' RT_GeometryHandle with the 'cutter' RT_PolylineHandle.
member.remarks:
The cutter and geometry's spatial references must match. A touch event is considered to be a cut (applies when cutting an RT_PolylineHandle). When cutting an RT_PolylineHandle, all left cuts will be grouped together in the first RT_GeometryHandle, right cuts and coincident cuts are grouped in the second RT_GeometryHandle, and each undefined cut, along with any uncut parts, are output as separate Polylines.
When cutting an RT_PolygonHandle, all left cuts are grouped in the first RT_GeometryHandle, all right cuts are in the second RT_GeometryHandle, and each undefined cut, along with any left-over parts after cutting, are output as a separate RT_GeometryHandle.
If there were no cuts the an empty RT_ArrayHandle will be returned.
If the left or right cut does not exist, the returned RT_GeometryHandle will be empty for this type of cut. An undefined cut will only be produced if a left cut or right cut was produced, and there was a part left over after cutting or a cut is bounded to the left and right of the cutter.
If an error occurs, null is returned. Client: DOTNET JAVA KOTLIN OBJECTIVE_C PRO QT RUST SWIFT UNITY UNREAL Since: 100.0.0
member.param: The input RT_GeometryHandle to be cut.
The RT_PolylineHandle that will be used to divide the geometry into pieces where they cross the cutter.
member.returns: An RT_ArrayHandle of RT_GeometryHandle.
