member.name: M:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreGeometryEngine.Intersection(RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreGeometry,RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreGeometry)
member.summary: Calculates the intersection of two geometries.
member.remarks: The result has the same dimensionality as the lower dimensionality of the two intersecting geometries. If there is no intersection with this dimensionality, returns an empty geometry. For example, the intersection of two polygons (geometries with area, so they have dimensionality of 2) or, say, a polygon and an envelope (also an area) is a polygon. Similarly, the intersection of a polyline (a line, so dimensionality of 1) and another polyline is always a polyline. Therefore when computing the intersection of polylines, this function does not return points where they cross, but rather lines of overlap. If there are no lines of overlap, an empty polyline is returned even if the input lines cross. To obtain all intersections, irrespective of dimensionality, see RT_GeometryEngine_intersections. Returns an empty geometry if the two input geometries do not intersect. Returns null on error. Supports true curves. Client: DOTNET JAVA KOTLIN OBJECTIVE_C PRO QT RUST SWIFT UNITY UNREAL Since: 100.0.0
member.param: A geometry object.
Another geometry object.
member.returns: A geometry object that represents the intersection of the given geometries.

member.summary: Calculates the intersection of two geometries.
member.remarks: The returned collection contains one geometry of each dimension for which there are intersections. For example, if both inputs are polylines, the collection will contain at most two geometries: the first a multipoint containing the points at which the lines cross, and the second a polyline containing the lines of overlap. If a crossing point lies within a line of overlap, only the line of overlap is present the result set is not self-intersecting. If there are no crossing points or there are no lines of overlap, the respective geometry will not be present in the returned collection. If the input geometries do not intersect, the resulting collection will be empty. The table below shows, for each combination of pairs of input geometry types, the types of geometry that will be contained within the returned collection if there are intersections of that type. Set of potential output geometry types for pairs of input geometry types Input type Point/Multipoint Polyline Polygon/Envelope Point/Multipoint Multipoint Multipoint Multipoint Polyline Multipoint Multipoint, Polyline Multipoint, Polyline Polygon/Envelope Multipoint Multipoint, Polyline Multipoint, Polyline, Polygon The geometries in the returned collection are sorted by ascending dimensionality, e.g. multipoint (dimension 0) then polyline (dimension 1) then polygon (dimension 2) for the intersection of two geometries with area that have intersections of those types. Returns null on error. Supports true curves. Client: DOTNET JAVA KOTLIN OBJECTIVE_C PRO QT RUST SWIFT UNITY UNREAL Since: 100.1.0

member.name: M:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreGeometryEngine.IsSimple(RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreGeometry)
member.summary: Gets a value indicating whether or not the geometry is simple.
member.remarks:
Point geometry is always simple. For Multi_point: there can be no point with exactly equal x and y - the tolerance is not taken into account. For Polylines: the only condition is there can be no degenerate segments. When the polyline has no Z, the degenerate segments are those that have length in xy plane less or equal the tolerance. When the polyline has Z, the degenerate segments are those that are shorter than the tolerance in xy plane, and the change in Z value along the segment is less than or equal to the Z tolerance.
For Polygons: Exterior rings are clockwise, and holes are counterclockwise Rings can touch other rings in finite number of points Rings can be self tangent in finite number of points Vertices are either exactly coincident, or further than the Spatial_reference tolerance from each other If a vertex is not equal to any boundary point of a segment, it has to be further than tolerance from any segment No segment length is zero or less than tolerance Each path contains at least three non-equal vertices No empty paths allowed Order of rings does not matter
Supports true curves. Client: DOTNET JAVA KOTLIN OBJECTIVE_C PRO QT RUST SWIFT UNITY UNREAL Since: 100.0.0
member.param: The geometry object.
member.returns: True if the geometry object is simple.

member.name: P:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreGeoModel.Basemap
member.summary: Gets or sets the optional layers in a map or scene that show background information—roads, landmarks, and so on—to help orient the user of the map or scene. Typically image tile or vector tile layer types. Basemaps can be composed of different layers organized in RT_Basemap_getBaseLayers (displayed beneath other layers) and RT_Basemap_getReferenceLayers (displayed on top of other layers). You can use ready-to-use basemaps, style your own with the ArcGIS Vector Tile Style Editor, or create and publish your own with ArcGIS Pro.

You can use ready-to-use basemaps, style your own with the ArcGIS Vector Tile Style Editor, or create and publish your own with ArcGIS Pro.

member.name: T:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreGeoprocessingFeatures
member.summary: The geoprocessing features used as input or output parameters.
member.remarks:
Corresponds to GPRecordSet and GPFeatureRecordSetLayer parameter types on the service. A feature contains a RT_GeoprocessingFeatures_getFeatures and may contains extra attributes on RT_GeoElement_getAttributes collection. A record (or a row) doesn't contain RT_FeatureHandle and information is stored in attributes on RT_GeoElement_getAttributes collection. When RT_GeoprocessingFeatures_getFeatures are returned as an output parameter the returned results are provided as a read-only list of RT_FeatureHandle using RT_GeoprocessingFeatureSetHandle. These features can be visualized on a map using temporary RT_GraphicHandle on a RT_GraphicsOverlayHandle or using RT_FeatureCollectionTableHandle on a RT_FeatureCollectionLayerHandle. If used geoprocessing service is configured to use a result map server, then RT_GeoprocessingResult_getMapImageLayer was populated and it can be used to visualize the results using the symbology predefined by the service.
When providing RT_GeoprocessingFeaturesHandle as an input to the geoprocessing task, features can be provided directly from the RT_FeatureQueryResultHandle that was returned from the RT_FeatureTableHandle. If there is a need to create a new set a features or records, RT_FeatureCollectionTableHandle can be used. Since: 100.0.0

member.name: T:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreGeoprocessingLinearUnit
member.summary: A linear unit input or output parameter.
member.remarks:
Corresponds to GPLinearUnit parameter type on the service. Geoprocessing tasks support a set of linear units defined in the RT_GeoprocessingLinearUnits. When a RT_GeoprocessingLinearUnitHandle parameter is created with one of the supported RT_GeoprocessingLinearUnits the value is sent to the service using defined linear unit type.
When a RT_GeoprocessingLinearUnitHandle parameter is created with a RT_LinearUnitHandle, the value is converted to meters if the type is not supported. For example if provided RT_LinearUnitHandle is international miles, the value is converted to meters since only the US Survey Miles unit is supported in geoprocessing. After RT_GeoprocessingLinearUnitHandle is created, the used linear unit type can be checked from RT_GeoprocessingLinearUnit_getLinearUnit.
When RT_GeoprocessingLinearUnitHandle is created with a supported RT_LinearUnitHandle, then no conversion takes place and the value is sent to the service using the defined type.
When RT_GeoprocessingLinearUnitHandle is returned as an output parameter, you can get RT_LinearUnitHandle using RT_GeoprocessingLinearUnit_getLinearUnit method. Since: 100.0.0

member.name: T:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreGeoprocessingResult
member.summary: Contains output parameters returned from the service.
member.remarks: Single output parameters can be found from RT_GeoprocessingResult_getOutputs dictionary where the key of the item is the name of the output parameters and the value is the returned RT_GeoprocessingParameterHandle. If used geoprocessing service is configured to use result map server then RT_GeoprocessingResult_getMapImageLayer might be populated. RT_GeoprocessingResult_getMapImageLayer is a dynamic map service that accompanies a geoprocessing service to visualize the geoprocessing results. Each geodataset output parameter of a geoprocessing task will be added as a layer to a map service. The visualization of the layer is determined by the symbology on geoprocessing service. RT_GeoprocessingResult_getMapImageLayer are mainly used to visualize RT_GeoprocessingRasterHandle or RT_GeoprocessingFeaturesHandle but in some cases RT_GeoprocessingStringHandle is used as a reference to a geodataset which is added to the result map service as a layer. Since: 100.0.0

member.name: P:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreGeotrigger.MessageExpression
member.summary: Gets or sets an RT_ArcadeExpressionHandle that controls the message when a RT_GeotriggerHandle is met.
member.remarks:
The expression uses the Arcade language to form an output message that can be: A string literal that is the same for all messages relating to this RT_GeotriggerHandle. A message that is specific to the attributes of objects that met the RT_GeotriggerHandle.
The expression is evaluated whenever the RT_GeotriggerHandle condition is met in order to populate the RT_GeotriggerNotificationInfo_getMessage property. This message can be displayed to alert the user that the RT_GeotriggerHandle condition has been met. Note that the expression cannot be changed when the RT_GeotriggerMonitorHandle is running.
For example, with a RT_FenceGeotriggerHandle, using the following expression:
"You have " + $fencenotificationtype + " " + $fencefeature.area_name
would return the RT_GeotriggerNotificationInfo_getMessage "You have entered Area A", where "area_name" is an attribute field on the RT_FenceGeotriggerNotificationInfo_getFenceGeoElement. Note that this property is an RT_ArcadeExpressionHandle object rather than a string.
Optionally, the expression can return extra properties in addition to the message. For example, it could produce another string, suitable for logging to a database. To supply additional properties, write an arcade expression that evaluates to a dictionary of key value pairs. A value with the key "message" will be used to populate the RT_GeotriggerNotificationInfo_getMessage property and additional key value pairs will be returned in the RT_GeotriggerNotificationInfo_getMessageProperties dictionary.
The RT_ArcadeExpressionHandle must evaluate to either a string or a dictionary - see RT_ArcadeExpression_getReturnType.
For more information on the available globals and functions for creating the RT_Geotrigger_getMessageExpression see the "Geotrigger Notification" profile at https://developers.arcgis.com/arcade/guide/profiles/ . Since: 100.12.0
member.value: An RT_ArcadeExpressionHandle that controls the message when a RT_GeotriggerHandle is met.

member.name: T:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreGeotriggerMonitor
member.summary: A RT_GeotriggerMonitorHandle monitors a RT_GeotriggerHandle condition and, when it is met, results in a RT_GeotriggerNotificationInfoHandle.
member.remarks: A RT_GeotriggerHandle defines a query that is evaluated against GIS data as it changes in real time. For example, "Notify me when my device location enters one of my target areas" or "Notify me when my device location is within 50 m of my destination". A RT_GeotriggerMonitorHandle is created with a RT_GeotriggerHandle that it continually checks to determine whether the condition has been met. Once a RT_GeotriggerMonitorHandle is created, you begin checking the condition by calling RT_GeotriggerMonitor_startAsync. Once you are finished, call RT_GeotriggerMonitor_stop. When a RT_GeotriggerHandle evaluates to true, a RT_GeotriggerMonitor_setGeotriggerNotificationEventCallback is sent. You can subscribe to the notification info to receive details of where the RT_GeotriggerHandle was activated and the condition that was met. Since: 100.12.0

member.remarks: A RT_GeotriggerMonitorHandle begins with a monitoring status of RT_GeotriggerMonitorStatus_stopped and changes to RT_GeotriggerMonitorStatus_started when you call RT_GeotriggerMonitor_startAsync. member.name: P:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreGeotriggerMonitor.Warning
member.summary: Gets an error that describes a problem encountered while starting or monitoring the RT_GeotriggerHandle.
member.remarks:
A warning can occur at various stages of monitoring a RT_GeotriggerHandle: when starting the RT_GeotriggerMonitorHandle when accessing the components of the RT_GeotriggerHandle such as the RT_GeotriggerFeedHandle when performing on-going monitoring
If the problem is resolved, this property will be cleared.
Problems that occur when starting the RT_GeotriggerMonitorHandle result in a RT_GeotriggerMonitor_getStatus of RT_GeotriggerMonitorStatus_failedToStart. These issues must be fixed and start called again before you receive any notifications. For example, if the RT_Geotrigger_getMessageExpression is an invalid RT_ArcadeExpressionHandle, monitoring cannot be carried out.
Problems that occur when accessing the components of the RT_GeotriggerHandle will not prevent the RT_GeotriggerMonitorHandle from starting. However, until the problem is resolved, you will not receive any notifications. For example, if a RT_LocationGeotriggerFeedHandle uses a RT_LocationDataSourceHandle that is not started, you will not receive any notifications. Once the RT_LocationDataSourceHandle is successfully started, monitoring will resume. If a RT_FenceParametersHandle has no valid data for a fence you will not receive any notifications.
Problems that occur during ongoing monitoring relate to issues with individual objects such as the graphics that make up the fences for a RT_GraphicFenceParametersHandle. These warnings do not prevent notifications from being sent for other valid fences. For example, a fence is considered invalid if it has:
an empty RT_GeometryHandle a missing RT_SpatialReferenceHandle a point or polyline RT_GeometryHandle and a buffer distance of 0 Since: 100.12.0
member.value: An error that describes a problem encountered while starting or monitoring the RT_GeotriggerHandle.

member.name: P:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreGeotriggerNotificationInfo.FeedEntityId
member.summary: Gets a unique ID for the entity within the feed that triggered the notification info.
member.remarks:
This property will be consistent for all notifications for a given feed entity. For example, use this ID to count the number of sites a team-member visits. If a feed is a RT_LocationGeotriggerFeedHandle, all location updates for that feed will share the same ID. With a RT_FenceGeotriggerHandle, you can combine this property with the RT_FenceGeotriggerNotificationInfo_getFenceId to create an ID that groups all notifications for a given feed entity and a specific fence. For example, use a concatenation of the two properties to display a list of areas of interest that are currently occupied and the details of who has entered them.
To group events by the geotrigger, use the RT_Geotrigger_getGeotriggerId property. Since: 100.13.0
member.value: A unique ID for the entity within the feed that triggered the notification info.

member.name: P:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreGeotriggerNotificationInfo.FeedLocation
member.summary: Gets a RT_LocationHandle, received from the feed, that meets the RT_GeotriggerMonitorHandle condition.
member.remarks: The RT_LocationHandle is set if a RT_LocationGeotriggerFeedHandle was used to create the RT_GeotriggerHandle that the RT_GeotriggerMonitorHandle is monitoring. This allows you to access the position and meta-data from the feed, such as the horizontal accuracy, velocity, time stamp and other RT_Location_getAdditionalSourceProperties. Since: 100.12.0
member.value: A RT_LocationHandle, received from the feed, that meets the RT_GeotriggerMonitorHandle condition.

member.name: P:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreGeotriggerNotificationInfo.GeotriggerMonitor
member.summary: Gets the RT_GeotriggerMonitorHandle that sent this notification.
member.remarks: The RT_GeotriggerMonitorHandle evaluates a specific RT_GeotriggerHandle condition that has been met by this RT_GeotriggerNotificationInfoHandle. A single RT_GeotriggerHandle condition can result in multiple, repeat notifications. This property can be used to interact directly with the RT_GeotriggerMonitorHandle. For example, if you no longer want to receive future notifications, you can call RT_GeotriggerMonitor_stop. Since: 100.12.0
member.value: The RT_GeotriggerMonitorHandle that sent this notification.

member.name: P:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreGeotriggerNotificationInfo.Message
member.summary: Gets a message that describes the notification.
member.remarks:
The notification message is the result of evaluating the RT_Geotrigger_getMessageExpression for the specific objects that triggered this notification. The message could be a hard-coded string or use attributes from an area of interest that was entered to display a custom message. For example, with a RT_FenceGeotriggerHandle, setting the RT_Geotrigger_getMessageExpression property to: "You have entered " + $fencefeature.area_name
would return the RT_GeotriggerNotificationInfo_getMessage "You have entered Area A", where "area_name" is an attribute field on the RT_FenceGeotriggerNotificationInfo_getFenceGeoElement.
You can use this message to alert the user directly or in other business logic in your app. Since: 100.12.0
member.value: A message that describes the notification.

member.name: P:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreGeoView.SelectionProperties
member.summary: Gets or sets the selection properties that is applied to the geo view.
member.remarks:
This property allows configuration of new selection highlighting functionality such as selection promotion and switchable selection halo. Notes on per-layer selection coloring (supported in 2D only): The deprecated per-layer selection coloring functionality is initially enabled.
If the RT_GeoViewHandle's RT_SelectionPropertiesHandle are touched, per-layer selection coloring is then disabled for the lifetime of the view. (here, 'touched' means replacing the view's SelectionProperties, or calling a setter property on the view's SelectionProperties).
Use of per-layer selection coloring is deprecated and may have a detrimental impact on rendering performance.
When per-layer coloring is enabled and more than one selection color is configured, selection halo will be disabled.
To enable selection halo or promotion, set the properties to true. Again, this will automatically disable per-layer selection coloring for the lifetime of the view. Since: 100.4.0
member.value: The selection properties that is applied to the geo view.

member.name: P:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreGeoView.TimeExtent
member.summary: Gets or sets the current RT_TimeExtentHandle of the GeoView.
member.remarks: The Time Extent of the GeoView defines how time-enabled data is displayed. Participating layers filter their data to only show data within the time extent set on the GeoView (see RT_TimeAwareInterface for details). The range of the time extent includes the start and end values (a feature at 10/24/2016 would be included in a time extent defined as 10/24/2016 - 11/14/2016). Time filtering is not enabled until a non-null time extent is set on the GeoView. When the time extent is null on the GeoView, no time filtering is applied and all content is rendered. Since: 100.2.0

member.name: M:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreGeoView.IdentifyGraphicsOverlay(RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreGraphicsOverlay,RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreCoordinate2D,System.Double,System.Boolean)
member.summary: Initiate an Identify operation on the specified graphics overlay. This overload will return the visible topmost graphic.
member.remarks: The 'tolerance' parameter determines the extent of the region used during the identify operation. Any graphics that intersect this test region when rendered are returned, up to the maximum_results limit. A tolerance of 0 tests just the physical pixel at screen_point. Tolerance values above 0 are in DIPs and specify a circular region centered on screen_point, with radius equal to tolerance. The maximum allowed tolerance value is 100 DIPs, resulting in an identify circle of diameter 200 DIPs. The 'return_popups_only' parameter controls what properties are populated in the RT_IdentifyGraphicsOverlayResultHandle instance that is returned by the identify operation. true: only the 'popups' property will be populated with results. If the overlay does not have popups an error will be returned. false: the 'graphics' property will be populated, and the 'popups' property will be populated if the overlay has popups. Non-overloaded method: IdentifyGraphicsOverlay Since: 100.0.0
member.param: The overlay on which to run the identify.
The location at which to run identify in screen coordinates.

Controls whether the graphics property of the result is populated.
member.returns: A RT_TaskHandle of RT_IdentifyGraphicsOverlayResultHandle

member.remarks: Results are returned in top-to-bottom order. The 'tolerance' parameter determines the extent of the region used during the identify operation. Any Geo-elements that intersect this test region when rendered are returned, up to the maximum_results limit. A tolerance of 0 tests just the physical pixel at screen_point. Tolerance values above 0 are in DIPs and specify a circular region centered on screen_point, with radius equal to tolerance. The maximum allowed tolerance value is 100 DIPs, resulting in an identify circle of diameter 200 DIPs. The 'return_popups_only' parameter controls what properties are populated in the RT_IdentifyLayerResultHandle instances that are returned by the identify operation. true: each result's popups property will be populated with results. Layers without popups will be omitted. false: geoElements will be populated. Layers with popups will also return popups. Non-overloaded method: IdentifyLayers Since: 100.0.0
member.param: The location on which to run identify in screen coordinates.
Determines the extent of the region used during the identify operation. See remarks for further detail.
Controls whether the geoElements property of the results are populated.
member.returns: An RT_TaskHandle of RT_ArrayHandle of RT_IdentifyLayerResultHandle, containing one entry for each layer in the view that supports identify. Each entry contains a RT_LayerHandle and a RT_ArrayHandle of elements of the type contained by the layer (e.g. RT_FeatureHandle for an RT_FeatureLayerHandle).

member.name: P:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreGraphic.ZIndex
member.summary: Gets or sets the defines the draw order for graphics. Graphics with higher Z-index values are drawn on top of lower Z-index graphics.
member.remarks: A graphic's Z-index is mostly relevant for display in a two dimensional map. For dynamic 3D rendering (in a scene), graphic display order is determined by the distance to the camera rather than by Z-index. Z-index is considered, however, when using static rendering in a scene (draping graphics on the surface, in other words). If Z-index is not set, graphics will usually render in the order in which they were added to the graphics overlay, the first added is rendered first and subsequent ones on top. In rare cases, the rendering algorithm may change the display order to provide more efficient rendering. If ordering is important, set the Z-index explicitly on graphics. You can also place graphics of the same geometry type in their own graphics overlay and manage the order of the overlays in the RT_MapViewHandle or RT_SceneViewHandle. Since: 100.0.0
member.value: Defines the draw order for graphics. Graphics with higher Z-index values are drawn on top of lower Z-index graphics

member.name: T:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreGraphicFenceParameters
member.summary: Geotrigger fence parameters data created from graphics.
member.remarks: The graphics used to create a RT_GraphicFenceParametersHandle provide a set of geometries and attributes that define targets for a RT_FenceGeotriggerHandle condition. For example, if the condition is "notify me when my position comes within 50 meters of one of my target areas", the fence data is "my target areas". A RT_GraphicFenceParametersHandle allows you to track a specific set of RT_GraphicHandle objects: these can be a selection of the graphics from a RT_GraphicsOverlayHandle or graphics that are not displayed on a RT_GeoViewHandle. If you wish to track all of the graphics displayed in a RT_GraphicsOverlayHandle, use a RT_GraphicsOverlayFenceParametersHandle. A RT_GraphicFenceParametersHandle is created using a list of RT_GraphicHandle objects. The graphics can have point, line, or polygon geometry. A RT_FenceParameters_getBufferDistance must be supplied for points or lines. Since: 100.12.0

member.name: T:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreGraphicsOverlay
member.summary: Contains a collection of graphics for display in a map or scene view.
member.remarks: Graphics overlays display on top of all other data in a map or scene view. A graphics overlay can contain graphics of various geometry types and can define symbology for the graphics it contains using its RT_GraphicsOverlay_getRenderer. A graphic's Z-index can be used to define its draw order in the collection and is mostly relevant for display in a two dimensional map. For dynamic 3D rendering (in a scene), graphic display order is determined by the distance to the camera rather than by Z-index. Z-index is considered, however, when using static rendering in a scene (draping graphics on the surface, in other words). If Z-index for graphics is not set, they will usually render in the order in which they were added to the graphics overlay, the first added is rendered first and subsequent ones on top. In rare cases, the rendering algorithm may change the display order to provide more efficient rendering. If ordering is important, set the RT_Graphic_getZIndex explicitly on graphics. You can also place graphics of the same geometry type in their own graphics overlay and manage the order of the overlays in the view. Since: 100.0.0

member.name: T:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreGraphicsOverlayFenceParameters
member.summary: Geotrigger fence parameters data created from a RT_GraphicsOverlayHandle.
member.remarks: The RT_GraphicsOverlayHandle used to create a RT_GraphicsOverlayFenceParametersHandle provides a dynamic set of graphics that define targets for a RT_FenceGeotriggerHandle condition. For example, if the condition is "notify me when my position comes within 50 meters of one of my target areas", "my target areas" are the graphics in the overlay. Changes to the RT_GraphicsOverlayHandle will be reflected in the fences tracked by the RT_GeotriggerHandle. A RT_GraphicsOverlayFenceParametersHandle allows you to track all of the graphics displayed on the RT_GeoViewHandle in a RT_GraphicsOverlayHandle. This allows you to track new target areas as they are added to the view and to stop tracking areas that are removed. If you wish to track a subset of the graphics displayed in a RT_GraphicsOverlayHandle, or graphics which are not displayed in a RT_GeoViewHandle, use a RT_GraphicFenceParametersHandle. The graphics can have point, line, or polygon geometry. A RT_FenceParameters_getBufferDistance must be supplied for points or lines. Since: 100.12.0

member.name: T:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreGroupLayer
member.summary: A container for other layers and group layers. It is used to represent datasets that are composed of multiple layers to be managed as a single layer with respect to display in a map or scene.
member.remarks:
Group layers are designed for presentation of operational layers that are related by a theme. You can add several related operational child layers into a group layer so the layers can be displayed together. Suppose there are several feature layers that represent existing infrastructure projects (buildings, sidewalks, roads, and trees). You can add these feature layers into a single group layer called "Existing". Similarly assume there are also proposed infrastructure projects that are features in other layers. These layers can be added to a group layer called "Planned". You can manage the visibility of the existing or planned features as separate groups. For the most part, group layers behave like any other layer in that: A group layer has visual properties (visibility, opacity) that can be applied to all layers in the group layer at once. This is helpful when controlling the visibility of the group. You can set a scale range on a group layer using the minimum and maximum scale properties. If a child layer has more restricted scale range, that scale range will be honored for that child layer. A group layer may be queried for the aggregate geographic extent of its child layers A group layer may be nested inside another group layer. There is no defined nesting level limit. Cloning a group layer will also clone its child layers A group layer does not have its own attribute values. The text from the child layers is displayed instead. A group layer is not time-aware, but may contain layers that are A group layer cannot be added to a basemap
The full extent of a group layer is derived asynchronously based on what information is available from the child layers. This means the full extent can change when child layers are added or removed. The full extent geometry will have the spatial reference of the first loaded child layer.
Group layers are not supported in Web maps. Saving a map with a group layer to a web map flattens the operational layers. Group layers are supported in Web scenes.
The visual opacity property of the group layer affects the opacity of the child layers. The opacity of the child layers is a mathematical product of the individual child layer's opacity and the group layer's opacity. Opacity values range from 0.0 (transparent) to 1.0 (opaque). This means that setting the opacity of the group layer to 0.0 will make all child layers transparent [0 * AnyNumber = 0]. Likewise when the group layer opacity is 1.0, will set the opacity of the child layers to their individual layer opacity [1 * AnyNumber = AnyNumber]. Since: 100.5.0

member.name: T:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreHatchFillSymbolLayer
member.summary: A struct that implements hatch fill symbol layer inside of the geometry attached to a multilayer polygon symbol.
member.remarks: A RT_HatchFillSymbolLayerHandle represents a polygon geometry filled with hatch lines. "Hatch lines" are uniformly spaced parallel lines. A RT_HatchFillSymbolLayerHandle, in a multilayer polygon symbol, fills the geometry of the symbol with the specified hatch lines. Each hatch line is itself a multilayer polyline symbol. You can define a custom hatch line (through the setPolyline and certain create methods) that is repeated in parallel throughout the inside of the geometry attached to a multilayer polygon symbol's geometry. The RT_HatchFillSymbolLayerHandle provides a similar experience to the RT_SimpleFillSymbolHandle, but with more customizability. Whereas you can select from a list of predefined hatch fill styles for a RT_SimpleFillSymbolHandle, the RT_HatchFillSymbolLayerHandle allows you to specify a fully-customized symbol to use as the hatch line. You can also adjust line angle, offset, and separation distance. Since: 100.5.0

member.name: T:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreHorizontalVerticalTransformation
member.summary: Used to transform coordinates of z-aware geometries between spatial references that have different geographic and/or vertical coordinate systems.
member.remarks:
A HorizontalVerticalTransformation is an ordered list of RT_HorizontalVerticalTransformationStepHandle objects. Each HorizontalVerticalTransformation has an input and an output RT_SpatialReferenceHandle, and this HorizontalVerticalTransformation object can be used to convert coordinates between the horizontal (geographic) and vertical datums of these spatial references using the series of steps it contains. Use the RT_GeometryEngine_projectWithTransformation method to transform the coordinates of a specific RT_GeometryHandle. A horizontal transformation step is not needed when the input and output spatial references have the same underlying geographic coordinate systems. A vertical transformation is not needed if both datums (for ellipsoidal heights) or vertical datums (for gravity-related heights) are the same. To transform coordinates only between different horizontal (geographic) coordinate systems, you can use a RT_GeographicTransformationHandle instead. The inverse of this transformation, used to transform in the opposite direction, is returned from the RT_DatumTransformation_getInverse method.
A HorizontalVerticalTransformation can be constructed from a single RT_HorizontalVerticalTransformationStepHandle object, or from a number of transformation step objects that are chained together.
You can get a list of suitable transformations for a given input and output spatial reference using one of the methods on the RT_TransformationCatalogHandle class.
Some transformations require that certain Projection Engine data files be present on the local file system, and vertical transformation steps are especially likely to use such files, which can be very large in size. The RT_DatumTransformation_getIsMissingProjectionEngineFiles property indicates whether any of the files are missing. The complete list of necessary files for each specific step is available using the RT_HorizontalVerticalTransformationStep_getProjectionEngineFilenames property.
A HorizontalVerticalTransformation object is immutable. Client: DOTNET JAVA KOTLIN OBJECTIVE_C PRO QT RUST SWIFT UNITY UNREAL Since: 100.9.0

member.name: T:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreImageOverlay
member.summary: An overlay that contains a frame with an image to display in the view.
member.remarks: Currently, this feature is supported in a RT_SceneViewHandle (3D) only. The overlay can contain exactly one image at any given time. Multiple overlays, however, can be added and rendered at the same time on the RT_SceneViewHandle. An RT_ImageOverlayHandle can be used to quickly render frequently changing images. For example, rendering realtime sensor data, such as weather, where each static image represents a single frame from the radar. In this workflow, images are constantly updated via a new RT_ImageFrameHandle each time new data is available. This provides a fast-refreshing workflow where the underlying images are frequently updated as new data comes in. Since RT_ImageOverlayHandle does not support the rich processing and rendering capabilities of a RT_RasterLayerHandle, you should use RT_RasterHandle and RT_RasterLayerHandle for workflows that require static image rendering, analysis, and persistence. Image overlays are rendered above all other layers in the scene, draped on the surface, and below any graphics overlays in the scene view. Since: 100.8.0

member.name: T:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreImageServiceRaster
member.summary: An instance of this class represents a raster that is retrieved from an ArcGIS image service.
member.remarks: An image service provides access to raster data through a web service. A single raster dataset or a mosaic dataset which contains a collection of raster datasets can be served as one image service. The mosaic dataset can dynamically process and mosaic the images on the fly. An image service supports accessing both the mosaicked image and its catalog, as well as individual rasters in the catalog. An image service raster allows you to display raster data from image services using a RT_RasterLayerHandle. It also allows you to apply service-defined or client-defined rendering rules by setting RT_RenderingRuleHandle on it. You can pass an image service raster as a raster input to an RT_RasterFunctionHandle to work with local raster functions. The image service raster is derived from the raster class. It's the same as a RT_RasterHandle. Since: 100.1.0

member.name: T:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreImageTiledLayer
member.summary: A base class for layers that display cached maps. You would typically work with one or more sub-classes of this class.
member.remarks: RT_ImageTiledLayerHandle defines a base class for layers that display tiled map services and cached image services. This is an abstract class that can be derived in a custom class to implement a local tile data scheme. To implement a custom RT_ImageTiledLayerHandle, for example to load your own local tile data, you should derive from this type and supply the data for each tile as it is requested. Additionally, implementers must also supply a RT_TileInfoHandle that describes the tiling scheme, and an RT_EnvelopeHandle that defines the layer extent. Implement this class if you want to create a custom tiled layer where the cached images cannot be referenced by a simple URI. If your images can be referenced by a simple URI, you should instead implement RT_ServiceImageTiledLayerHandle. Since: 100.0.0

member.name: P:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreImageTiledLayer.NoDataTileBehavior
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether how a tile request that returns 'NoData' is resampled.
member.remarks: Zooming in can result in tile requests with no tiles at the requested level of detail. In this case, there are options that control what to display where the tile should be including: RT_NoDataTileBehavior_upSample - Resample the pixels from a lower level of detail tile. This can result in pixelation or blurriness. This is the default behavior for operational layers. RT_NoDataTileBehavior_blank - The 'NoData' pixels will show the raster picture as being blank (or disappearing). This is the default behavior for basemap reference layers. RT_NoDataTileBehavior_show - This will show the raster picture with the text 'No Data' stamped over it once you pass the lowest level-of-detail scale. Sometimes, to see the effect on the map when setting the RT_ImageTiledLayer_getNoDataTileBehavior property, the RT_Layer_getMaxScale value must also be explicitly set. The RT_Layer_getMaxScale property may need to be smaller than the level-of-detail setting that was used to create the tiled images in ArcGIS Pro or ArcGIS Desktop. For example, consider an operational image tile layer showing forest cover that was created with the level-of-detail assumption that it was to be viewed above a scale of 5000 (meaning you will not see 'NoData' until you zoom closer to the Earth than a 5000 scale). However, you want to be able to zoom in closer to the Earth surface, say down to 3000 or 300. By setting the RT_Layer_getMaxScale property to a number smaller than 5000, you will be able to zoom in closer to the Earth and see the effects of changing the RT_ImageTiledLayer_getNoDataTileBehavior enumerations. Since: 100.0.0
member.value: Determines how a tile request that returns 'NoData' is resampled.

member.name: T:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreImmutablePart
member.summary: Represents a single part of a multipart geometry (polygon or polyline).
member.remarks: A collection of RT_SegmentHandle objects that together represent a part in a RT_MultipartHandle geometry. You can also access the RT_PointHandle objects that represent the vertices of the geometry (that is, the ends of each segment), using point-based helpers such as RT_ImmutablePart_getPoint. Prior to v100.12, the only supported segment type was RT_LineSegmentHandle. If the underlying geometry contained curve segments (RT_Geometry_getHasCurves is true) then the curve information was lost when iterating through the segments in that part. From v100.12, curve segments may be returned from RT_ImmutablePart_getSegment. A part may contain a mix of linear and curve segments. member.name: M:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreIndoorsLocationDataSource.PushAccelerometerReading(RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreDateTime,System.Double,System.Double,System.Double)
member.summary: *Internal Use* Push accelerometer reading from device sensors. All values are in SI units (m/s^2). The measurements are expected to be calibrated (e.g. while being stationary we would only read the Earth's gravitational acceleration). Ideally, if device sensors are able to provide new data with that frequency, this method is expected to be called at least 200 times per second (200 Hz). G=(Gx,Gy,Gz) is the gravitational acceleration vector pointing towards Earth in the local frame of reference.
member.remarks:
The coordinate system is defined relative to the screen of the device in its default orientation. The X-axis is horizontal and points to the right, the Y-axis is vertical and points up and the Z-axis points towards the outside of the front face of the screen (e.g. normally towards the user).
Note that on some platforms (e.g. iOS) the values reported by the system need to be converted, as they may be using a different coordinate system and different units.
Platforms are expected to provide data as soon as they are provided by the system. Platforms must not filter, process or cache such data prior to passing it to the IndoorsLocationDataSource. Internal Use This should not be exposed to external Esri developers. Since: 100.13.0
member.param: Timestamp when the new signal was received. It is preferred to use current system time rather than timestamp from the original reading.
Acceleration including Gx in m/s^2
Acceleration including Gy in m/s^2
Acceleration including Gz in m/s^2

member.name: M:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreItem.UpdateItemPropertiesAsync
member.summary: Updates an item's properties in a file on disk when this item instance is a RT_LocalItemHandle.
member.remarks: This method resides in the RT_ItemHandle base class to match the public API, but within the C API it's implemented only on RT_LocalItemHandle and RT_PortalItemHandle simply throws an exception. The client APIs provide their own implementations of this method for PortalItems. The following remarks apply when the item instance is a RT_LocalItemHandle. Updating properties can be only done for local items that are unpacked. For example a mobile map package file (.mmpk) can be unpacked using RT_MobileMapPackage_unpackAsync. Once unpacked local items within the package can be updated see RT_MobileMapPackage_getItem and for any maps use RT_GeoModel_getItem. As well as packages, the local item available from an item resource cache can be updated. This is accessed with RT_ItemResourceCache_getItem. member.name: M:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreJob.Cancel
member.summary: Cancel the job.
member.remarks:
The job is canceled and goes into a failure status RT_JobStatus_failed. For jobs running on a server, a cancel request will be sent for the associated RT_Job_getServerJobId. You should always cancel unneeded jobs (for example when exiting your app) to avoid placing unnecessary load on the server. For example, server side jobs include: RT_ExportTileCacheJobHandle RT_ExportVectorTilesJobHandle RT_GenerateGeodatabaseJobHandle RT_GeoprocessingJobHandle
In addition, the RT_GenerateOfflineMapJobHandle is composed of several server-side jobs, depending on the layers in your RT_MapHandle. Canceling this high-level job will also send a cancel request to the underlying server jobs. Since: 100.0.0
member.returns: true if the job was canceled, false if the job is already succeeded or failed. Returns false if an error occurs.

member.name: M:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreJob.CheckStatusAsync
member.summary: Initiates a request to check the server status.
member.remarks: The task contains a bool indicating if the check was successful. The task completes after the status has been checked. If the job is polling the server for status and is in a time gap, then calling this method will ensure a request is sent right away. The result can be false if the job is not checking server status for example if the job status is paused or uploading. Since: 100.0.0
member.returns: a task containing bool which indicates if the status was successfully checked.

member.remarks: Creates a KML dataset. KML dataset is the source of KML information backing a KML layer. Use the KML dataset to interact with the contents of a KML layer. member.param: The location of the file, either on disk or from the network.

member.name: P:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreKMLDataset.URI
member.summary: Gets the location of the KML/KMZ file, which can either be on disk or from the network.
member.remarks: The URI of the backing file. Files can be loaded from local storage or the network. Note that KML files often point to network locations for their data (using network links). As a result, the loaded KML layer may display more information than is contained in the loaded KML file. KML files can point to network locations. These locations may be insecure (over plain text HTTP) even when the URI returned from this function is pointing to an SSL/TLS-secured resource. Since: 100.2.0
member.value: The location of the KML/KMZ file, which can either be on disk or from the network.

member.name: M:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreKMLDataset.Load
member.summary: Loads the metadata for the object asynchronously.
member.remarks: Loads the metadata if the object is not loaded and always calls RT_Loadable_setDoneLoadingCallback. DOCUMENTATION FOR THE ArcGISFeature IMPLEMENTATION OF Loadable.load ONLY An ArcGISFeature is loadable. Depending on a ServiceFeatureTable's feature request mode, queries on the table can return ArcGISFeature objects which have the minimum set of attributes required for rendering and labeling (and geometries do not include m-values). See RT_ServiceFeatureTable_queryFeaturesWithFieldOptions, RT_FeatureRequestMode_onInteractionCache, and RT_FeatureRequestMode_onInteractionNoCache. To access all attributes in the returned ArcGISFeatures, call this method on each feature. For alternative ways to load all attributes in the returned features, see RT_ServiceFeatureTable_loadOrRefreshFeatures or RT_ServiceFeatureTable_queryFeaturesWithFieldOptions. Since: 100.2.0

member.name: T:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreKMLImageCoordinate
member.summary: A KML image coordinate object.
member.remarks: According to the OGC 2.3 specification in section 16.26.2 ( http://docs.opengeospatial.org/is/12-007r2/12-007r2.html#1254 ) "Specifies an image coordinate system. The x and y values may each be specified in three different ways - as pixels (pixels), as fractions of the icon (fraction), or as inset pixels (insetPixels), which is an offset in pixels from the upper right corner of the icon. They may or may not be specified in a consistent manner - for example, x can be specified in pixels and y as a fraction." Use the RT_KMLUnitsType enumeration (either via the RT_KMLImageCoordinate_getXUnits and RT_KMLImageCoordinate_getYUnits properties or via the RT_KMLImageCoordinate_createWithValues constructor) to establish the KML image coordinate system. The RT_KMLUnitsType_pixels and RT_KMLUnitsType_insetPixels image coordinate systems are defined with device-independent pixels (DIPs). Since: 100.6.0

member.name: T:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreKMLLayer
member.summary: A layer that can visualize KML data.
member.remarks:
Keyhole Markup Language (KML) is a specification for working with geographic content. KML files can contain 2D and 3D content, as well as links to content from the network. ArcGIS Runtime provides the ability to read .kml and .kmz files from disk or the network. You can also create, edit, and save a KML layer via the RT_KMLDatasetHandle. Functional characteristics KML represents features as a tree of nodes, including network links, folders, and place marks. Like ArcGIS features, place marks are defined with point, line, or polygon geometry. KML geometry, however, is always based on the WGS84 coordinate system. KML can also have attributes, but unlike ArcGIS feature services, a KML document does not use a schema to define a standard set of fields. ArcGIS Runtime supports version 2.2 of the KML specification as defined by the Open Geospatial Consortium (OGC).
Unique features of KML include network links and screen overlays. Network links are useful for retrieving network content on a specified interval—perfect for keeping a live map up to date. Network links can also be used to split a large KML file into multiple per-region KML files, with each being loaded only when the region is in view. Screen overlays can be used to show content, such as branding or a legend, on top of the view. Screen overlay content does not scroll with the map or react to user interaction.
All coordinates are expressed in latitude and longitude (using decimal degrees), and are based on the RT_SpatialReference_WGS84 geographic coordinate system. Altitude is always expressed in meters. The geographic features can contain attribute information and various styles can be specified to render them. Ground overlays allow images to be displayed for specific geographic objects or draped onto the map itself. Screen overlays allow fixing images to the RT_GeoViewHandle, and may be used for compasses, logos, legends, etc. Network links give the ability to reference remote .kml or .kmz files, and refresh them periodically.
Loading the RT_KMLLayerHandle also loads its underlying RT_KMLDatasetHandle, creating one if you didn't supply one through a constructor. The structure of a KML document can be examined through RT_KMLDataset_getRootNodes after the RT_KMLDatasetHandle has successfully loaded. Missing or inaccessible .kml and .kmz files would cause loading to fail. Missing resources referenced by the KML document (such as images or files referenced via a network link will not prevent the layer from loading.
Performance characteristics KML files can vary significantly in the features they use, including 3D models, network links, and refresh intervals. Not all features are supported in 2D and 3D. For example, 3D models only appear when the KML layer is shown in a scene. Many KML files consist solely of a pointer to another KML file and a refresh interval. For example, the National Weather Service distributes forecast maps in the United States this way. Since: 100.0.0

member.name: P:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreKMLNode.TimeExtent
member.summary: Gets or sets the KML node's time extent.
member.remarks: Represents the RT_TimeExtentHandle equivalent of a KML node's TimeStamp or TimeSpan . A RT_KMLContainerHandle node such as RT_KMLDocumentHandle or RT_KMLFolderHandle may have its own RT_TimeExtentHandle independent of its child nodes. All KML TimeStamps and TimeSpans specified in a KML/KMZ file are converted to their UTC RT_TimeExtentHandle equivalents. Examples: Kml TimeStamp RT_TimeExtent_getStartTime RT_TimeExtent_getEndTime 2021 2021-01-01T00:00:00 2021-12-31T23:59:59 2021-01 2021-01-01T00:00:00 2021-01-31T23:59:59 2021-01-01 2021-01-01T00:00:00 2021-01-01T23:59:59 2021-01-01T12:34:56 2021-01-01T12:34:56 2021-01-01T12:34:56 Kml TimeSpan RT_TimeExtent_getStartTime RT_TimeExtent_getEndTime 2021 - 2022 2021-01-01T00:00:00 2022-12-31T23:59:59 2021-01 - 2021-02 2021-01-01T00:00:00 2021-02-28T23:59:59 No beginning - 2021 Infinite start time 2021-12-31T23:59:59 2021 - No end 2021-01-01T00:00:00 Infinite end time Since: 100.11.0

member.name: M:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreKMLNode.SaveAsAsync(System.String)
member.summary: Saves the node and any referenced local files into a zipped KMZ archive.
member.remarks: The node will be saved to a KMZ file to ensure that any referenced files are available locally when sharing the file with others. If this method is called on a leaf node (e.g. KMLPlacemark, KMLGroundOverlay, etc), only that node and its referenced files will be saved. If this method is called on container node (e.g. KMLDocument, KMLFolder), the node and all of its children and referenced files will be saved. If this method is called on a KMLNetworkLink, the link will be saved but the children will not. This is because the children will simply be refetched when the saved KMLNetworkLink is loaded. Saving referenced files will differ based on the type of reference. For HTTP paths, the path will be saved as is but the referenced file will not be zipped into the archive, as it will simply be refetched when the new KMZ is loaded. For relative paths, the path will be saved as is and the referenced file will be zipped relative to the root of the KMZ file. For absolute paths, the path will be converted to a relative path, and the referenced file will be zipped into a "files" folder at the root of the KMZ file. For example, "C:/icons/some_icon.png" would be converted to "files/some_icon.png" and stored at that location in the KMZ file. The filename supports unicode characters as well as nested directories. It must be non-empty and there must not be an existing file located there. Saving a node to a KMZ file requires an ArcGIS Runtime 'Standard' license level. Since: 100.6.0
member.param: The KMZ filepath to which the node should be saved.
member.returns: An RT_TaskHandle that contains no return value.

member.name: F:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreKMLRefreshMode.OnChange
member.summary: (default) Refresh when the file is loaded and whenever the Link parameters change.

member.name: F:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreKMLRefreshMode.OnInterval
member.summary: Refresh every n milliseconds, where n is specified by refresh interval. If no refresh interval is set, the default value is 4000 milliseconds.

member.name: F:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreKMLRefreshMode.OnExpire
member.summary: Refresh the file when the expiration time is reached. If a fetched file has a NetworkLinkControl, the "expires" time takes precedence over expiration times specified in HTTP headers. If no "expires" time is specified, the HTTP max-age header is used (if present). If max-age is not present, the Expires HTTP header is used (if present). Currently this is treated the same as if the mode were onChange.

member.name: P:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreKMLScreenOverlay.OverlayCoordinate
member.summary: Gets or sets the specifies a point on (or outside of) the overlay image that is mapped to the screen coordinate (RT_KMLScreenOverlay_getScreenCoordinate). It requires x and y values, and the units for those values.
member.remarks: The x and y values can be specified in three different ways: as pixels ("pixels"), as fractions of the image ("fraction"), or as inset pixels ("insetPixels"), which is an offset in pixels from the upper right corner of the image. If not specified, the default is the center of the overlay image. Since: 100.7.0
member.value: Specifies a point on (or outside of) the overlay image that is mapped to the screen coordinate (RT_KMLScreenOverlay_getScreenCoordinate). It requires x and y values, and the units for those values.

member.name: P:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreKMLScreenOverlay.ScreenCoordinate
member.summary: Gets or sets the specifies a point relative to the screen origin that the overlay image is mapped to.
member.remarks: The x and y values can be specified in three different ways: as pixels ("pixels"), as fractions of the screen ("fraction"), or as inset pixels ("insetPixels"), which is an offset in pixels from the upper right corner of the screen. The x and y positions can be specified in different ways—for example, x can be in pixels and y can be a fraction. The origin of the coordinate system is in the lower left corner of the screen. If not specified, the default is the center of the screen. Since: 100.7.0
member.value: Specifies a point relative to the screen origin that the overlay image is mapped to.

member.name: P:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreKMLScreenOverlay.Size
member.summary: Gets or sets the specifies the size of the image for the screen overlay.
member.remarks: A value of −1 indicates to use the native dimension A value of 0 indicates to maintain the aspect ratio A value of n sets the value of the dimension For example: A x value of -1 and y value of -1 in fractions indicates the image size equals its original x and y dimensions. A x value of -1 and y value of 0.2 in fractions indicates the image size equals its original x dimension and 20% of its y dimension. A x value of 100 and y value of 500 in pixels indicates the image is of size 100 pixels by 500 pixels. If not specified, the default is the original size of the image. Since: 100.7.0
member.value: Specifies the size of the image for the screen overlay.

member.name: T:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreKMLUnitsType
member.summary: A KML units type object.
member.remarks: Use the RT_KMLUnitsType enumeration (either via the RT_KMLImageCoordinate_getXUnits and RT_KMLImageCoordinate_getYUnits properties or via the RT_KMLImageCoordinate_createWithValues constructor) to establish the KML image coordinate system. Values of type fraction must be between 0.0 and 1.0. Values below 0.0 will be set to 0.0, and values above 1.0 will be set to 1.0. If a non-integral number is specified with a unit type of device-independent pixels (RT_KMLUnitsType_pixels or RT_KMLUnitsType_insetPixels), it will be rounded down to a whole number (e.g. 2.243 will be rounded to 2.0). Since: 100.6.0

member.name: F:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreKMLUnitsType.Fraction
member.summary: Fraction is the default value. Treat the x/y value as a fraction of the width/height.

member.name: F:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreKMLUnitsType.Pixels
member.summary: Treat the x/y value as an integral number of device-independent pixels (DIPs).

member.name: F:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreKMLUnitsType.InsetPixels
member.summary: Treat the x/y value as an integral number of device-independent pixels (DIPs) from the top right corner.

member.name: P:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreKMLViewpoint.Pitch
member.summary: Gets the KML viewpoint's pitch.
member.remarks: Angle in degrees between the camera and the target RT_KMLViewpoint_getLocation. Ranges between 0 and 90 for LookAt viewpoints, 0 and 180 for Camera viewpoints. 0 means the camera is pointing straight down towards the Earth and 90 means the camera is looking from/towards the horizon. For Camera viewpoints, values between 90 and 180 indicate the camera is looking towards the sky. Corresponds to 'tilt' in the KML specification. Since: 100.4.0
member.value: The KML viewpoint's pitch.

member.name: P:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreKMLViewpoint.Range
member.summary: Gets the KML viewpoint's range, which defines the distance between the camera and RT_KMLViewpoint_getLocation.
member.remarks: The distance between the camera and the LookAt viewpoint's target location. This only applies to 'LookAt' viewpoints. Since: 100.4.0
member.value: The KML viewpoint's range, which defines the distance between the camera and RT_KMLViewpoint_getLocation.

member.name: P:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreKMLViewpoint.Roll
member.summary: Gets the KML viewpoint's roll.
member.remarks: The rotation in degrees of the viewpoint camera around the Z axis. Values range from -180 to 180 degrees. Only applies to 'Camera' type viewpoints. Since: 100.4.0
member.value: The KML viewpoint's roll.

member.name: P:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreKMLViewpoint.Type
member.summary: Gets the KML viewpoint's type (Camera or LookAt).
member.remarks: A RT_KMLViewpointType_camera viewpoint defines the position of the camera directly. A RT_KMLViewpointType_lookAt viewpoint defines the position of the camera relative to a point of interest. See Google's KML reference for details about KML viewpoint (abstractView) specification, including diagrams. Since: 100.4.0
member.value: The KML viewpoint's type (Camera or LookAt).

member.name: P:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreLabelDefinition.Expression
member.summary: Gets or sets the expression script used to calculate the label text.
member.remarks:
The expression may be a combination of literal text and attribute values from the feature being labeled. The syntax of the expression is determined by which label expression object is used: RT_ArcadeLabelExpressionHandle, RT_SimpleLabelExpressionHandle or RT_WebmapLabelExpressionHandle. A label expression using one scripting language can be replaced by an expression using a different scripting language just by creating an object of the new RT_LabelExpressionHandle subclass and assigning it to RT_LabelDefinition_getExpression. The default value is an empty RT_ArcadeLabelExpressionHandle, which will evaluate to an empty text label.
The expression needs to create a text string which will be used as the label text. The text string can be any legal UTF16 characters.
The text string can also include HTML-style formatting tags e.g.
"Hello <BOL>World</BOL>"
where the angle-bracketed tags will not appear in the label, but may change the presentation of the text. In the example, the "World" will appear in bold.
The available tags are: "<BOL></BOL>" for bold text "<UND></UND>" for underlined text "<ITA></ITA>" for italic text "<CLR red='256'></CLR>" for colored text "<FNT name='Arial' size='18'></FNT>" for text using a different size or font (if available on client).
Tags can be upper or lower case, but not a mixture. Tags can be nested e.g. "<ITA>Hello <BOL>World</BOL></ITA>".
Full documentation of the tag parameters is available at https://pro.arcgis.com/en/pro-app/latest/help/mapping/text/text-formatting-tags.htm .
Note that not all ArcGISPro tags are currently supported in Runtime. The "<CLR>" tag is currently only supported for text in 2D views. Any unsupported tags will be ignored and not written as part of the label text. Since: 100.11.0
member.value: The expression script used to calculate the label text.

member.name: P:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreLabelDefinition.Priority
member.summary: Gets or sets the defines which labels are placed first, and can also supplant existing lower-priority labels (e.g. during panning).
member.remarks:
Lower values indicate more important labels i.e.: 0 is the most important 5 is high priority 15 is medium priority Higher values indicate lower priority If set to -1 or not set at all, then default values are used, depending on the geometry types of the features: 12 for point features 15 for line features 18 for polygon features

member.name: P:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreLabelDefinition.StackAlignment
member.summary: Gets or sets the strategy for how multi-row (stacked) text should be aligned.
member.remarks: Multi-row text labels can be horizontally aligned on the left, right or at its center. This preference can be specified by the RT_TextSymbolHandle assigned to the RT_LabelDefinitionHandle. By using the RT_LabelDefinition_getStackAlignment property, the user can choose to use the RT_TextSymbol_getHorizontalAlignment property for all labels, or can choose to have the most aesthetic alignment calculated case-by-case for each label depending on its placement position around its feature. This is particularly useful for labels of dense point features, where labels may move above, below, left or right of their point symbol, in order to fit on the display. The default value is RT_LabelStackAlignment_automatic (which will have the same effect on labels as RT_LabelStackAlignment_textSymbol). This property has no effect if RT_LabelDefinition_getStackStrategy = RT_LabelStackStrategy_none. Since: 100.11.0
member.value: The strategy for how multi-row (stacked) text should be aligned.

member.name: P:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreLabelDefinition.StackBreakPosition
member.summary: Gets or sets the strategy for whether a row of text should be broken before or after it exceeds the ideal length.
member.remarks: If stacking is turned on, label placement can insert a line break before or after the word that overruns the maximum number of characters per row. Using the RT_LabelStackBreakPosition_before option means rows will generally be shorter than the RT_LabelDefinition_getStackRowLength (although will overrun for individual words larger than this count). The default is RT_LabelStackBreakPosition_automatic (which will have the same effect on labels as RT_LabelStackBreakPosition_after). This property has no effect if RT_LabelDefinition_getStackStrategy = RT_LabelStackStrategy_none. Since: 100.11.0
member.value: The strategy for whether a row of text should be broken before or after it exceeds the ideal length.

member.name: P:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreLabelDefinition.StackRowLength
member.summary: Gets or sets a value that limits the number of characters in a row of stacked text.
member.remarks: This length guides the decision on when to break long text strings into separate rows. The line break will be inserted between words, not in the middle of a word, so rows may be longer or shorter than the ideal. Depending on RT_LabelDefinition_getStackBreakPosition, the break may be inserted before the breaking word, or after. The default value is -1 which means to use a default length determined by ArcGIS Runtime (currently 13 characters but may vary with feature-geometry in the future). This property has no effect if RT_LabelDefinition_getStackStrategy = RT_LabelStackStrategy_none. Since: 100.11.0
member.value: A value that limits the number of characters in a row of stacked text.

member.name: P:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreLabelDefinition.StackSeparators
member.summary: Gets or sets the stack separators that should be used for automatic line breaking of label text.
member.remarks:
Each RT_LabelStackSeparatorHandle specifies a code point to be looked for in the text. A code point is often thought of as a single character in the text, but may need several chars in a RT_StringHandle to describe it. So each RT_LabelStackSeparator_getSeparator is a RT_StringHandle intended to describe one code point. For example: To use a comma as a separator, the RT_LabelStackSeparator_getSeparator string would be just "," To use a Hebrew punctuation Paseq as a separator, the RT_LabelStackSeparator_getSeparator would need to encode the code point with utf16 value "\u05c0" if your SDK uses utf16 strings (e.g. Java, C#) or with the utf8 string "\x30\x35\x63\x30" if your SDK uses utf8 strings To use higher range unicode code points such as Aegean Word Separator Dot which has utf32 hex value 10101, the RT_LabelStackSeparator_getSeparator would need to encode the code point with utf16 value "\ud800\udd01" if your SDK uses utf16 strings (e.g. Java, C#) or with the utf8 string "\xf0\x90\x84\x81" if your SDK uses utf8 strings
If it is found, then the RT_LabelStackSeparatorHandle also specifies whether: The text should always be broken here Whether the separator code point should remain visible Whether the separator code point should appear at the end of one row, or the beginning of the next
Three default separators are provided: a comma, a space, and a hyphen. Custom separators can be added, and default separators can be removed if not required.
Note that a carriage-return ( ) in the label will always be considered a forced separator.

member.summary: The strategy for whether line features with the same label, and matching end vertices, should be joined before sharing a label.

member.name: F:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreLabelLineConnection.Automatic
member.summary: The default approach for connectable features is to connect them (RT_LabelLineConnection_minimizeLabels)
member.remarks: This value corresponds to no value being specified for a RT_LabelDefinition_getLineConnection property. Since: 100.11.0

member.name: F:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreLabelLineConnection.MinimizeLabels
member.summary: Line geometries with the same label and coincident end vertices should be considered together as a single, continuous geometry when placing labels.
member.remarks: For example, if a single label is being placed on a line feature, then the single location will be chosen along the combined geometries. This combining will ignore junctions, so it may be ambiguous which line feature after a junction is the continuation of the earlier geometry. Since: 100.11.0

member.name: F:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreLabelLineConnection.None
member.summary: Keep one label per line feature geometry.

member.name: F:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreLabelLineConnection.UnambiguousLabels
member.summary: Line geometries with the same label and coincident end vertices should be joined, until they hit a junction.
member.remarks: For example, if a single label is being placed on a line geometry (composed of multiple features' geometries, but all having the same label text), then a label will be placed on both sides of any junction, to make it unambiguous which geometries are the continuation of the initial geometry. Since: 100.11.0

member.name: T:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreLabelMultipartStrategy
member.summary: The strategy for the number of labels to be placed on a multi-part feature.

member.name: F:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreLabelMultipartStrategy.Automatic
member.summary: Labeling will use the default distribution of labels across multi-part features.
member.remarks: This depends on Feature type: Polygon labels will use RT_LabelMultipartStrategy_labelLargest Point and Line labels will use RT_LabelMultipartStrategy_labelPerPart Since: 100.11.0

member.name: F:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreLabelMultipartStrategy.LabelLargest
member.summary: If a feature consists of multiple parts, only the largest one will be assigned a label.
member.remarks: If a line feature consists of multiple part geometries, or a polygon feature consists of multiple ring geometries, only the largest one will be assigned a label. If the largest part of the feature is not currently visible on the RT_MapViewHandle or RT_SceneViewHandle, then the label will not be visible. It will not automatically move to the largest visible part. Since: 100.11.0

member.name: F:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreLabelMultipartStrategy.LabelPerFeature
member.summary: One label per feature, but not supported yet in runtime.
member.remarks: The intended use is to place one label to represent each feature, even if the feature is made up of multiple parts, e.g. placing a single label at the center of a group of point parts, not necessarily at the position of any individual part. This value can be set when labeling is authored in ArcGIS Pro, but is not supported yet in runtime. If used, the placement will be as for RT_LabelMultipartStrategy_labelPerPart. Since: 100.11.0

member.name: F:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreLabelMultipartStrategy.LabelPerPart
member.summary: If a feature consists of multiple geometries, each geometry will be assigned a label.
member.remarks: If a line feature consists of multiple line geometries, or a polygon feature consists of multiple ring geometries, each geometry will be assigned a label. Since: 100.11.0

member.name: F:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreLabelMultipartStrategy.LabelPerSegment
member.summary: One label per segment, but not supported yet in runtime.
member.remarks: The intended use is to place a label on each segment of each line geometry. This value can be set when labeling is authored in ArcGIS Pro, but is not supported yet in runtime. If used, the placement with be as for RT_LabelMultipartStrategy_labelPerPart. Since: 100.11.0

member.name: T:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreLabelStackAlignment
member.summary: The strategy for how multi-row (stacked) text should be horizontally aligned.
member.remarks: Multi-row text labels can each be horizontally aligned on the left, right or at their center. By using the RT_LabelStackAlignment, the user can choose to use the RT_TextSymbol_getHorizontalAlignment property for all labels, or can choose to have the most aesthetic alignment calculated case-by-case for each label depending on its placement position around its feature. This is particularly useful for labels of dense point features, where labels may move above, below, left or right of their point symbol, in order to fit on the display. Since: 100.11.0

member.name: F:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreLabelStackAlignment.Automatic
member.summary: The default behavior is to use RT_LabelStackAlignment_textSymbol.
member.remarks: This value corresponds to no value being specified for a RT_LabelDefinition_getStackAlignment property. Since: 100.11.0

member.name: F:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreLabelStackAlignment.Dynamic
member.summary: Set the alignment depending upon the label's position with respect to its feature.
member.remarks: Have the alignment decided case-by-case for each label depending on its placement position around its feature. This is particularly useful for labels of dense point features, where labels may move above, below, left or right of their point symbol, in order to fit on the display. For example, a stack to the right of a point symbol will be left-aligned. Since: 100.11.0

member.name: F:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreLabelStackAlignment.TextSymbol
member.summary: Follow the alignment specified by the RT_TextSymbol_getHorizontalAlignment.

member.name: T:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreLabelStackBreakPosition
member.summary: The strategy for whether a row of text should be broken before or after it exceeds the ideal length.

member.name: P:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreLabelStackSeparator.Separator
member.summary: Gets or sets a RT_StringHandle intended to describe one code point.
member.remarks: Each RT_LabelStackSeparatorHandle specifies a code point to be looked for in the text. A code point is often thought of as a single character in the text, but may need several chars in a RT_StringHandle to describe it. For example: To use a comma as a separator, the RT_LabelStackSeparator_getSeparator string would be just "," To use a Hebrew punctuation Paseq as a separator, the RT_LabelStackSeparator_getSeparator would need to encode the code point with utf16 value "\u05c0" if your SDK uses utf16 strings (e.g., Java, C#) or with the utf8 string "\x30\x35\x63\x30" if your SDK uses utf8 strings To use higher range unicode code points such as Aegean Word Separator Dot which has utf32 hex value 10101, the RT_LabelStackSeparator_getSeparator would need to encode the code point with utf16 value "\ud800\udd01" if your SDK uses utf16 strings (e.g., Java, C#) or with the utf8 string "\xf0\x90\x84\x81" if your SDK uses utf8 strings The default value is an empty string, meaning that the RT_LabelStackSeparatorHandle will be ignored. Since: 100.11.0
member.value: A RT_StringHandle intended to describe one code point.

member.name: F:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreLabelTextLayout.Automatic
member.summary: The text layout will be determined by the individual feature type.
member.remarks: For each label, the layout will be determined by the feature geometry type: Point feature labels will use RT_LabelTextLayout_horizontal Line feature labels will use RT_LabelTextLayout_followFeature Polygon feature labels will use RT_LabelTextLayout_horizontal Since: 100.11.0

member.name: F:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreLabelTextLayout.Horizontal
member.summary: Text will be written horizontally (with respect to the screen).
member.remarks: If the map is rotated within the screen, then the text will be redrawn (and possibly repositioned) to remain horizontal with respect to the screen. Since: 100.11.0

member.name: F:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreLabelTextLayout.Perpendicular
member.summary: Text will be written perpendicular to the RT_LabelTextLayout_straight text layout.

member.name: F:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreLabelTextLayout.Straight
member.summary: Text will be written along a straight line, following the point positioning angle or at a tangent to the line feature. Offset point labels will be positioned around the point feature, at the position specified by the angle. The text will lie along this angle, so that it stretches radially from the edge of the point feature. Note that if a label has an angle of zero then its text will be drawn horizontally with respect to the map. If the map is rotated within the screen, the text will rotate with the map. Line labels will be positioned as usual, but then rotated (around their midpoint) to lie on a straight line at a tangent to the line geometry at that point.
member.remarks: An angle for placement and orientation will be calculated for each label if the "labelAngleInfo" json property for the RT_LabelDefinitionHandle has been specified. Centered point labels will stay centered on the point feature, but will be rotated to the angle (or horizontal, if none has been defined). Since: 100.11.0

member.name: F:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreLabelTextLayout.FollowFeature
member.summary: Text will bend to follow a curved or multi-segment line feature.
member.remarks: Individual characters will be angled to follow the changes in angle of the line geometry. If the text overruns the beginning or end of the line geometry, then the remaining characters will be laid out in a straight line extrapolated from the last geometry segment. Since: 100.11.0

member.name: T:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreLatitudeLongitudeGrid
member.summary: A grid consisting of east-west lines of latitude and north-south lines of longitude.
member.remarks:
This class represents graticules lines showing parallels of latitude and meridians of longitude for the earth. The position of the graticules are based on the WGS84 ellipsoid, irrespective of the spatial reference used by the map view. To display graticules, create a LatitudeLongitudeGrid and set it as the grid property within the MapView.
LatitudeLongitudeGrid extends Grid, adding the label unit property. Since: 100.0.0
