member.name: M:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreLatitudeLongitudeGrid.#ctor
member.summary: Constructs a grid consisting of east-west lines of latitude and north-south lines of longitude (also known as graticules).
member.remarks: The grid is supported in spatial references which are continuously pannable or some polar spatial references. You can check the RT_SpatialReference_getIsPannable property is true on your spatial reference. Examples of continuously pannable spatial references include WGS84 (WKID 4326) and Web Mercator Auxiliary Sphere (WKID 102113, 102100, or 3857). The following polar spatial references are also supported: North pole Azimuthal Equidistant (WKID 102016) North pole gnomic (WKID 102034) North pole Lambert equal area (WKID 102017) North pole orthographic (WKID 102035) North pole stereographic (WKID 102018) NSIDE EASE North (WKID 3408) NSIDC Sea Ice polar stereographic north (WKID 3411) WGS 1984 NSIDC Sea Ice Polar Stereographic North (WKID 3413) UPS North (WKID 32661) South pole Azimuthal Equidistant (WKID 102019) South pole gnomic (WKID 102036) South pole Lambert equal area (WKID 102020) South pole orthographic (WKID 102037) South pole stereographic (WKID 102021) NSIDE EASE South (WKID 3409) NSIDC Sea Ice polar stereographic South (WKID 3412) UPS South (WKID 32761) WGS1984 Antarctic polar stereographic (WKID 3031) Since: 100.0.0

member.name: T:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreLayer
member.summary: A base class for all layers.
member.remarks: RT_LayerHandle is the base class for all layer types. A layer is a representation of geographic data portrayed using symbols and text labels. Multiple layers can be 'stacked' to enhance the information displayed. Layers are displayed in a RT_MapHandle inside a RT_MapViewHandle control. Layers are drawn bottom-to-top, so the first layer in a map's layer collection is drawn first (on the bottom) and each subsequent layer is drawn on top of it. member.name: T:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreLayerViewStatus
member.summary: The status of a layer in the RT_GeoViewHandle.
member.remarks:
This status is used to determine whether a layer is displaying in a RT_GeoViewHandle or whether it is still loading, not visible, out of scale, or has encountered an error or warning. Each layer can have multiple states at the same time. For example, a layer could be both RT_LayerViewStatus_notVisible and RT_LayerViewStatus_outOfScale, or it could be RT_LayerViewStatus_notVisible and RT_LayerViewStatus_loading. These multiple states are represented using a flag enumeration. A status of RT_LayerViewStatus_active indicates that the layer is being displayed in the view. Note, that some of the layer view states are not possible together. For example, a layer cannot be both RT_LayerViewStatus_active and RT_LayerViewStatus_notVisible at the same time. If you implement a layer list in a table of contents (TOCs), you can use the layer view status to manage the TOC user interface. For example, you could gray out the layer if it is RT_LayerViewStatus_outOfScale, or you could show a spinning icon if the layer is RT_LayerViewStatus_loading. If the layer list contains a RT_GroupLayerHandle that is RT_LayerViewStatus_notVisible then its child layers will be RT_LayerViewStatus_notVisible. If, the RT_GroupLayerHandle is visible then each child layer can be either visible or RT_LayerViewStatus_notVisible.
If the layer completely fails to load or render you will encounter a RT_LayerViewStatus_error. If the layer fails to render some of its content then you will encounter a RT_LayerViewStatus_warning. This could be due to the temporary loss of a network connection, failing layer requests or exceeding the max feature count. In both cases you will find more details about the problem in the RT_LayerViewState_getError. Client: DOTNET JAVA KOTLIN OBJECTIVE_C PRO QT RUST SWIFT UNITY UNREAL Since: 100.0.0

If the view is zoomed too far in (e.g. to a street level) it is beyond the max scale defined for the layer. member.name: T:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreLicense
member.summary: A class that contains properties of a Runtime license.
member.remarks:
Until an app is licensed, it runs at the Developer license level. All functionality is available, but the map display is watermarked and the API logs messages stating that the app is in developer mode. A deployed app needs to be run at minimum with the Lite license level to disable the map watermark. The Lite, Basic, Standard, or Advanced license level is set by calling RT_ArcGISRuntimeEnvironment_setLicense with a license string obtained from the ArcGIS for Developers website or Esri Customer Service. With the varying license levels, a subset of functionality is available. Any attempt to use licensed functionality that is not available at the current license level will log or emit error messages. To get Lite, Basic, Standard, or Advanced license level functionality, a user app is licensed in one of two ways:
With license information retrieved after logging in to a portal (Lite and Basic levels). With a license string acquired from the ArcGIS for Developers website or Esri Customer Service.
To license with a license string, call RT_ArcGISRuntimeEnvironment_setLicense.
To validate with information from a portal, you need a RT_LicenseInfoHandle instance. You can get one by calling RT_PortalInfo_getLicenseInfo. Pass the RT_LicenseInfoHandle to RT_ArcGISRuntimeEnvironment_setLicenseInfo.
Both of these methods return a RT_LicenseResultHandle that reports the status of the license. Note that there is a 30-day timeout when using RT_LicenseInfoHandle. If the app is licensed using this method, the user must log in to the portal again before licensing the app. When this period has expired, calling RT_ArcGISRuntimeEnvironment_setLicenseInfo returns a RT_LicenseResultHandle which contains license status of RT_LicenseStatus_loginRequired, and the app continues to run at the current license level (default is RT_LicenseLevel_developer). Since: 100.0.0

If there is no consensus (one or more layers have different colors), a null value is reported for the color. Likewise, setting a value for color on a symbol will apply that color to all layers the symbol contains. If you don't want changes to the symbol color to propagate to some of the symbol layers it contains, you can lock the color (or tint color) for those layers. If a symbol layer is color-locked, changes to the parent symbol will not affect the symbol layer. This also means that the layer will not be considered when determining a consensus color for the symbol as a whole. Since: 100.0.0

member.name: M:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreLocation.#ctor(RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreDateTime,RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CorePoint,System.Double,System.Double,System.Double,System.Double,System.Boolean,RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreDictionary)
member.summary: Creates a location object with timestamp and additional source properties.
member.remarks:
A RT_LocationHandle can be created from a variety of sources and using different technologies. By supplying RT_Location_getAdditionalSourceProperties you can allow users of this RT_LocationHandle to find out how the data was captured. Information should be provided as a set of key-value pairs, where the RT_StringHandle key describes the type of data held in the RT_ElementHandle value. Values must be basic data types such as string, floating point, integer, boolean or date. You can use any string for the key - but the Runtime SDK recognizes a number of well known keys which should be used if available. See RT_LocationSourcePropertiesKeysHandle: "floor" (an integer value). The floor number of the RT_LocationHandle when in a building. Use RT_LocationSourcePropertiesKeys_getFloor to reference this key. "satelliteCount" (an integer value). The number of satellites used to fix the RT_LocationHandle. Use RT_LocationSourcePropertiesKeys_getSatelliteCount to reference this key. "positionSource" (a string value). This key can be used to indicate the position source: GNSS, BLE, WIFI, CELL, IP. Where GNSS indicates global navigation satellite system. It is possible to have multiple position sources. In that case positionSource is a list with comma-separated values.
Keys are case-sensitive. Since: 100.10.0
member.param: A timestamp when location was received.
A point geometry object.
The horizontal accuracy in meters. Positive values or NaN are supported.
The vertical accuracy in meters. Positive values or NaN are supported.
The location's velocity in meters per second.
The location's course in degrees (clockwise), 0 being true North.

Indicates whether this is an outdated device position retrieved and cached earlier and therefore not guaranteed to represent the current location. Setting this to true will render with the RT_LocationDisplay_getAcquiringSymbol, typically a grayed out location symbol.
A set of key-value pairs providing additional meta-data and properties about the source of this RT_LocationHandle.

member.name: P:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreLocation.AdditionalSourceProperties
member.summary: Gets a set of key-value pairs providing additional meta-data and properties about the source of this RT_LocationHandle.
member.remarks:
A RT_LocationHandle object can be created manually or by a variety of RT_LocationDataSourceHandle types, for example from the default platform data source or external GPS. When user code receives a new RT_LocationHandle, it can be important to determine how the information was obtained. In addition, mobile devices may provide different details about their in-built location services. For example, Android systems can provide data on the number of satellites used to find a position, whereas on iOS this information is not available. When a given property is not available to the data source the entry should be omitted from the RT_Location_getAdditionalSourceProperties. The RT_Location_getAdditionalSourceProperties provide a means for the creator of a RT_LocationHandle object to record flexible information such as: The confidence level associated with the location The method used to obtain the location The provenance of the location
Information is provided as a set of key-value pairs, where the RT_StringHandle key describes the type of data held in the RT_ElementHandle value. Values must be basic data types such as string, numeric, boolean or date. The creator of the RT_LocationHandle can use any string for the key - but the Runtime SDK recognizes a number of well known keys which should be used if available. See RT_LocationSourcePropertiesKeysHandle: "floor" (an integer value). The floor number of the RT_LocationHandle when in a building. Use RT_LocationSourcePropertiesKeys_getFloor to reference this key. "satelliteCount" (an integer value). The number of satellites used to fix the RT_LocationHandle. Use RT_LocationSourcePropertiesKeys_getSatelliteCount to reference this key. "positionSource" (a string value). This key can be used to indicate the position source: GNSS, BLE, WIFI, CELL, IP. Where GNSS indicates global navigation satellite system. It is possible to have multiple position sources. In that case positionSource is a list with comma-separated values.
Keys are case-sensitive. Since: 100.10.0
member.value: A set of key-value pairs providing additional meta-data and properties about the source of this RT_LocationHandle.

member.summary: An enumeration of the various modes that define how the map view extent reacts to location changes.

member.name: F:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreLocationDisplayAutoPanMode.Off
member.summary: Displays the location symbol at the current location without adjusting the map view's extent, so no auto-panning is performed.

member.name: F:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreLocationDisplayAutoPanMode.Recenter
member.summary: Centers the map view at the current location, and shows the location symbol. When the current location changes, the map view is automatically panned to re-center at the new location. Behavior is affected by the wander extent factor.

member.name: F:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreLocationDisplayAutoPanMode.Navigation
member.summary: Pans the map view so that the current location symbol is shown near the bottom of the map view, and rotates the map view to align it with the direction of travel. When the current location or direction of travel changes the map view is automatically panned and rotated to maintain this position. To use this mode effectively, the device location must be moving at a speed greater than 0 meters per second. Behavior is affected by the navigation point height factor.

member.name: F:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreLocationDisplayAutoPanMode.CompassNavigation
member.summary: Centers the map view at the current location, rotates the map view to align with the direction in which the device is currently, and shows the location symbol. When the current location or position of the device changes, the map view is automatically panned and rotated to maintain this position, thus if the device is spun in a circle, the map view stays aligned with the real world.

member.name: T:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreLocationGeotriggerFeed
member.summary: Feed data for a RT_GeotriggerHandle created from a RT_LocationDataSourceHandle.
member.remarks: The RT_GeotriggerFeedHandle is the dynamic component of a RT_GeotriggerHandle. Typically, it is the data that moves around and triggers the condition. For example, if the condition is "notify me when my position comes within 50 meters of one of my target areas", the feed data is "my position". To receive location updates, the RT_LocationDataSourceHandle must be RT_LocationDataSource_getStarted. If you call RT_GeotriggerMonitor_stop, the underlying RT_LocationDataSourceHandle will not be stopped for you. For example, it may continue to receive GPS readings. Since: 100.12.0

member.name: P:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreLocationGeotriggerFeed.Filter
member.summary: Gets or sets an RT_ArcadeExpressionHandle that controls whether an update from the RT_LocationGeotriggerFeedHandle is sent to a RT_GeotriggerMonitorHandle.
member.remarks:
The expression uses the Arcade language to determine whether feed entity updates are suitable for monitoring. The RT_ArcadeExpressionHandle must evaluate to a boolean where: True indicates that the update will be used. False indicates that the update will not be used.
Filtering out undesirable updates reduces inaccurate notifications from your RT_GeotriggerMonitorHandle. For example, you could filter out GPS updates where the horizontal accuracy is poor, to avoid false enter and exit notifications.
With a RT_LocationGeotriggerFeedHandle, the expression inspects a new RT_LocationHandle object and returns true if it is suitable and false if not. Typically, your expression excludes RT_LocationHandle objects where the RT_Location_getHorizontalAccuracy does not meet your criteria - but it could also consider other properties such as RT_Location_getVelocity and RT_Location_getCourse.
Arcade gives you access to the properties of the feed entity with the $locationupdate global variable. This represents a new RT_LocationHandle received from your device GPS. For example, an RT_ArcadeExpressionHandle with the following string rejects RT_LocationHandle updates with a horizontal accuracy greater than 10 meters:
return $locationupdate.horizontalaccuracy <= 10; Since: 100.13.0
member.value: An RT_ArcadeExpressionHandle that controls whether an update from the RT_LocationGeotriggerFeedHandle is sent to a RT_GeotriggerMonitorHandle.

member.remarks: To receive location updates, the RT_LocationDataSourceHandle must be RT_LocationDataSource_getStarted. If you call RT_GeotriggerMonitor_stop, the underlying RT_LocationDataSourceHandle is not stopped for you. In other words, it may continue to receive GPS readings. Since: 100.12.0

member.summary: Creates a viewshed analysis object whose observer is defined using a point location. Provide a Camera and distance range to define the analysis frustum.
member.remarks: Visible and non-visible areas are determined for an area defined by the camera and the min/max distance range. member.name: M:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreLocationViewshed.#ctor(RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CorePoint,System.Double,System.Double,System.Double,System.Double,System.Double,System.Double)
member.summary: Creates a viewshed analysis object whose observer is defined using a point location. Provide a map location and frustum parameters for the analysis.
member.remarks: Visible and non-visible areas are determined for an area defined by the observer location, view angles, and the min/max distance range. The parameters define the frustum over which visibility is calculated from the observer location. The horizontal and vertical angles must be greater than zero to define a valid frustum and are constrained to a maximum of 120 degrees. Terrain and other obstacles between the observer and the minimum distance are excluded from the analysis, as are areas beyond the maximum distance. Since: 100.2.0
member.param: A geographic point location for the observer.
The heading value (azimuth) that defines the observer's view direction.
The pitch value (angle) of the observer's view relative to the surface. Valid values are from 0 (looking straight down) to 180 (straight up).
The horizontal angle of the observer's view. The value must be greater than 0 and no greater than 120.
The vertical angle of the observer's view. The value must be greater than 0 and no greater than 120.
The minimum distance from the observer at which visibility will be evaluated.
The maximum distance from the observer at which visibility will be evaluated.

member.name: P:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreLocatorTask.APIKey
member.summary: Gets or sets the API key to access API key enabled services and resources in ArcGIS Online.
member.remarks: An API key is a unique key used to authorize access to specific services and resources in ArcGIS Online. It is also used to monitor access to those services. An API key is created and managed in the ArcGIS developer dashboard and is tied to a specific ArcGIS account. In addition to setting an API key at a global level for your application using the RT_ArcGISRuntimeEnvironment_getAPIKey property, you can set an RT_APIKeyResource_getAPIKey property on any ArcGIS Runtime class that implements RT_APIKeyResourceInterface. When you set an individual RT_APIKeyResource_getAPIKey property on an RT_APIKeyResourceInterface it will override the default key at the global level (on the RT_ArcGISRuntimeEnvironment_getAPIKey property, in other words), enabling more granular usage telemetry and management for ArcGIS Online resources used by your app. Classes that expose an API key property by implementing RT_APIKeyResourceInterface include: RT_BasemapHandle RT_ArcGISSceneLayerHandle RT_ArcGISTiledLayerHandle RT_ArcGISVectorTiledLayerHandle RT_ServiceFeatureTableHandle RT_ExportVectorTilesTaskHandle RT_LocatorTaskHandle RT_GeodatabaseSyncTaskHandle RT_ClosestFacilityTaskHandle RT_RouteTaskHandle RT_ServiceAreaTaskHandle RT_ExportTileCacheTaskHandle Since: 100.10.0
member.value: The API key to access API key enabled services and resources in ArcGIS Online.

member.name: P:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreMap.ReferenceScale
member.summary: Gets or sets the reference scale for the map.
member.remarks: The reference scale of the map is the scale at which a client should view the map for the feature symbols and text to appear at their authored size. If the client changes the viewing scale, then feature symbols and text will grow or shrink to keep a consistent size on the map (not the screen). This only happens if the reference scale is greater than zero and for feature layers that have scaleSymbols set to true, otherwise the symbols and text stay at their authored size. The reference scale will be zero if the map is not loaded or if there is no reference scale and the symbols and text should appear at default size regardless of the viewing scale. This property is intended to be used for new Map objects, that will have layers attached that expect a reference scale. Subsequent updates to the map.referenceScale will cause a redraw of all layers that use the referenceScale, and possible knock-on redraw of other layers that depend on them (e.g. dynamic labels that need to re-position to avoid overlaps) Since: 100.5.0
member.value: The reference scale for the map.

member.summary: Gets or sets the utility networks in the map.
member.remarks:
This collection of RT_UtilityNetworkHandle is specific to this map. A RT_MapHandle created with a webmap portal item with utility networks will pre-populate this collection. When this RT_MapHandle is used to create a RT_UtilityNetworkHandle, the RT_UtilityNetworkHandle that was created will be added to this collection.
Only a RT_UtilityNetworkHandle that is not loaded may be added to this collection. An attempt to add a RT_UtilityNetworkHandle that is loaded or loading will throw a RT_ErrorType_commonInvalidCall error.
An attempt to add a RT_UtilityNetworkHandle that is already part of a RT_Map_getUtilityNetworks to this collection will throw a RT_ErrorType_commonObjectAlreadyOwned error.
An attempt to add a null RT_UtilityNetworkHandle to this collection will throw a RT_ErrorType_commonNullPtr error. Since: 100.10.0

member.name: M:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreMap.CanSaveWithoutForce
member.summary: *Internal Use* Determine if a Webmap can be serialized from the map without losing any data.
member.remarks: When serializing a Webmap it is possible to lose some of the data that comprises the map due to: Unknown JSON data, Because some of the layers reference local data (.tpk, .tpkx, .vtpk, MobileBasemapLayers), or Because of layers supported by Runtime but not the Webmap (KML, Raster, etc), or Because non-default WMS styles can't be persisted in the webmap Internal Use This should not be exposed to external Esri developers. member.name: T:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreMapView
member.summary: A view to render and allow interaction with 2D geographic content from an RT_MapHandle on a screen.
member.remarks:
In a Model View Controller (MVC) architecture, this class represents the View and the Map object represents the Model. To display a map, create a MapView of the required size and then set a Map object. The mapview will automatically load the map, its basemap, operational layers, and display their contents on screen. MapView inherits from GeoView and adds 2D specific methods for map navigation that set the visible area of the map (the current extent) by setting a viewpoint. For example, RT_MapView_setViewpointGeometryAsync zooms the map to the extent of a geometry, and RT_MapView_setViewpointCenterAsync zooms the map to a given scale, centered at the given Point. More setViewpoint methods are available, including overloads where an animation duration can be specified. Geometries passed to these methods will be automatically re-projected if required. Use RT_GeoView_getIsNavigating or a Navigation Changed event to determine if navigation is ongoing or completed. Once navigation is complete, get the new viewpoint from getCurrentViewPoint.
The MapView comes with default gestures to allow users to pan, zoom, and rotate the map specific to each platform. Platforms also allow you to override these gestures with your own. Events are also available on the MapView to allow applications to be notified of gesture events. Since: 100.0.0

member.name: M:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreMapView.#ctor(System.Int32,System.Int32,System.Single,RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CorePulseThread)
member.summary: *Internal Use* Create a map view for displaying a map.
member.remarks:
Creates map view for displaying a map. You need to connect a map to the map view before anything is draw. If using RT_PulseThread_useGeoView you must call RT_GeoView_resume to start the pulse thread which starts the drawing and RT_GeoView_pause to stop the pulse thread. There can only be 1 set of function callbacks for each map view. The options are: initialization_completed - Called when map view is ready for you to start interacting with it draw_requested - Called when map view requires a RT_GeoView_draw to be called start_drawing - Called when map view starts a new draw phase. Multiple draws can occur after this call but this will not be called again until completed_draw is called.
completed_draw - Called when map view is finished drawing in a draw phase. Multiple draws can occur before this call. Internal Use This should not be exposed to external Esri developers. Since: 100.0.0 Warning: With RT_PulseThread_useGeoView you must call RT_GeoView_resume and RT_GeoView_pause to control the pulse thread.
member.param: The width of the viewport.
The height of the viewport.
The number of pixels per DIP (sometimes referred to as screen density or device pixel ratio).
Determines if the map view owns the pulse or not.

member.remarks: The background grid determines the color and context grid of a map view when no RT_MapView_getMap has been set. The RT_MapHandle displays on top of the background grid or the optional RT_Map_getBackgroundColor to determine what is displayed under transparent areas of the map. If RT_Map_getBackgroundColor is not null, then RT_MapView_getBackgroundGrid is ignored and RT_Map_getBackgroundColor will be used as the background color of the map. Since: 100.0.0

member.name: T:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreMarkerSymbolLayer
member.summary: A base class for marker symbol layers, representing a symbol layer used to display a marker.
member.remarks:
RT_MarkerSymbolLayerHandle draws a shape or picture at a specific location relative to point geometry. A marker symbol layer is most often used in point symbols, but they can also be included in polyline and polygon symbols to draw a symbol at locations along lines and outlines, or within areas (the center of a polygon, for example). ArcGIS Runtime includes the following types of marker symbol layers: RT_VectorMarkerSymbolLayerHandle - Vector geometry defines the shape and appearance of the marker RT_PictureMarkerSymbolLayerHandle - Uses an image file (specified using a URI or image data) to define the marker
This symbol layer controls many common operations vital for working with markers.
Anchors, angles, offsets, and size properties are controlled on RT_MarkerSymbolLayerHandle.
The RT_MarkerSymbolLayerHandle has methods affecting both 2D and 3D markers. Some properties apply only to 3D markers, such as angleX, or offsetZ. These properties have no effect on markers in 2D. Properties on 2D markers, such as offsetX, affect the marker's position in screen space, not world space. This means that the x-axis for a 2D marker runs from negative-x on the West edge of the screen to positive-x on the East edge of the screen. Negative-y to positive-y runs from the South edge of the screen to the North edge of the screen.
Properties that apply only to 3D markers affect the marker's position in world space, rather than screen space. This means that the x, y, and z-axes to which the class methods are the axes of the world, with the following layout: from negative to positive, the x-axis spans from world West to world East, the y-axis from world South to world North, and the z-axis from directly into the surface to the sky.
While a simple text symbol (RT_TextSymbolHandle) can be used to display a character as a marker, proper display is dependent on the referenced font being available on the machine or device running the app. If the exact font is not found, which is likely to occur on many mobile devices, a fallback mechanism is used to find the best available font to use. A character marker symbol authored from ArcGIS Pro, however, is represented by a vector marker symbol. This symbol stores the geometry that represents the character, is not dependent on the font to render the shape of the marker, and displays as expected on all devices. Since: 100.5.0

member.remarks: The RT_SymbolAnchorHandle determines how Runtime anchors the RT_MarkerSymbolLayerHandle. RT_SymbolAnchorHandle specifies the marker's anchor point and anchor placement mode. The default symbol anchor is at XYZ(0, 0, 0) and uses 'relative' mode. See the RT_SymbolAnchorHandle documentation for a detailed description of the object. Since: 100.5.0
member.value: The anchor object of a marker symbol layer.

member.name: P:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreMarkerSymbolLayer.Heading
member.summary: Gets or sets the marker symbol layer's heading: the angle of rotation about the anchor point.
member.remarks: The input value can be any real number. The default value is 0. This property affects markers in both maps and scenes. Positive angles rotate the marker counterclockwise. Angle for RT_MarkerSymbolLayerHandle is measured in degrees counterclockwise from from 0 to 360. Marker symbol layers can have a separate heading value defined (which is also 0 by default). Setting a heading for a marker symbol layer does not affect the angle of the point symbol. When an angle value is set for the point symbol, however, that value is applied cumulatively to all the marker symbol layers it contains. The heading for individual symbol layers must be re-fetched in order to see the updated value. In 2D, the rotation applies around the anchor point of the 2D marker. For 3D markers, the rotation applies around the z-axis. Since: 100.5.0
member.value: The marker symbol layer's heading: the angle of rotation about the anchor point.

The x-offset is a delta applied to the marker in the direction corresponding to the given value. For example, a positive x-offset moves the marker in the positive-x direction. Since: 100.5.0

member.summary: The choice of MGRS lettering scheme is based on the datum and ellipsoid of the spatial reference provided. Spatial references with new datums (e.g. WGS 84) assume new lettering scheme (AA scheme). This is equivalent to RT_MGRSConversionMode_new180InZone60. Spatial references with older datums (e.g. Clarke 1866, Bessel 1841, Clarke 1880) assume old lettering scheme (AL scheme). This is equivalent to RT_MGRSConversionMode_old180InZone60. member.name: T:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreMGRSGrid
member.summary: A class that represents the display of the Military Grid Reference System (MGRS) on the map view.
member.remarks: The military grid reference system is the geocoordinate standard used by various militaries for locating points on the earth. The MGRS grid is derived from the Universal Transverse Mercator (UTM) grid system and the universal polar stereographic (UPS) grid system, but uses a different labeling convention. MGRS is used for the entire earth. To display the MGRS grid, create a MGRSGrid and set it as the grid property within the MapView. MGRSGrid inherits from Grid and adds a property for the label unit to use. Since: 100.0.0

member.name: T:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreMobileBasemapLayer
member.summary: A layer that can visualize the basemap layer of a map from mobile map package.
member.remarks: A mobile basemap layer can render feature, tiled, vector tiled and raster data together in a group as a single basemap layer. This layer abstracts the complexity of multiple layers into one simple-to-use layer. You can create a basemap layer using ArcGIS Pro and package it, along with its map, into a mobile map package (.mmpk) for use offline. Each package may contain one or more maps, each of which can contain a basemap with basemap layers. If a basemap layer contains features, they will be stored in a compressed format that can be displayed quickly along with any associated labels. This compressed format does not support feature selection, query, identify and time. Since: 100.0.0

member.name: T:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreMobileMapPackage
member.summary: A mobile map package.
member.remarks:
Mobile map packages allow you to work with maps on a mobile device. A mobile map package contains all of the files necessary to work with your maps and is stored on a device as either: A single archive file with an .mmpk extension A directory containing an unpacked mobile map package You can create a mobile map package using either: ArcGIS Pro (from version 1.3). This version of the ArcGIS Runtime SDK supports any RT_MobileMapPackageHandle up to major version 4. Mobile map packages created with ArcGIS Pro are stored in a file with an .mmpk extension. ArcGIS Runtime. Use the RT_OfflineMapTask_generateOfflineMap method to generate and download a mobile map package on-demand, or use the RT_OfflineMapTask_downloadPreplannedOfflineMapWithParameters to download a mobile map package already prepared by the map author. Mobile map packages created with the RT_OfflineMapTaskHandle are stored in a directory containing an unpacked mobile map package.
A mobile map package can encapsulate one or more maps along with their layers and data. Each package contains an RT_ItemHandle with metadata about the package (description, thumbnail, etc.).
Mobile map packages created with ArcGIS Pro can also include transportation networks, locators, and links to online services. You can choose whether to use: A tile package (such as .tpkx or .vptk) or an online basemap as the RT_GeoModel_getBasemap A mobile geodatabase (.geodatabase) or an online feature service as one of the RT_GeoModel_getOperationalLayers. Online services (such as traffic or weather) can provide excellent contextual information for your users. If the mobile map package is going to be used in areas of poor connectivity, however, you must ensure that data critical to your workflow is stored locally on the device.
Mobile map packages implement the RT_LoadableInterface interface; you need to load the RT_MobileMapPackageHandle before you can access its content. Once loaded you can:
Determine the version of this package using the RT_MobileMapPackage_getVersion property. ArcGIS Runtime currently supports mobile map packages up to and including major version If the package is from an unsupported version, it will fail to load.
Discover whether the mobile map package has expired using the RT_MobileMapPackage_getExpiration property Access the individual maps and display them in a RT_MapViewHandle Programmatically add, modify, and remove layers in the map. Mobile map packages, however, are read-only and these changes to maps or layers are not persisted. Since: 100.0.0

member.name: P:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreMobileMapPackage.Expiration
member.summary: Gets the expiration details for this mobile map package, if provided.
member.remarks:
Expiration details provide: The package’s expiration date and time Whether the maps can be accessed after expiration Any messages relevant for the user These expiration details can be specified when the author creates a mobile map package using ArcGIS Pro (from version 2.4). This requires the ArcGIS Pro Publisher Extension. Mobile map packages created with the RT_OfflineMapTaskHandle do not support expiration. By publishing a package with expiration details, the author can control the experience an end-user has when they try to access information that is no longer valid. For example, for time limited data (such as major sporting events), the author can ensure that the data cannot be accessed after the expiry date.
During package loading, the ArcGIS Runtime will determine whether the mobile map package was authored with expiration. If so, then this property will be populated.
If the package has expired and was authored as RT_ExpirationType_preventExpiredAccess, loading will fail and you will not be able to access the maps. The expiration details will be accessible for you to examine and/or communicate to the user. Since: 100.5.0
member.value: Expiration details for this mobile map package, if provided.

member.remarks: The item includes the metadata about the mobile map package, such as: Title Snippet (summary) Description Tags Thumbnail If the package was created with ArcGIS Pro, the metadata was provided by the package author. If the package was created using the RT_OfflineMapTaskHandle, the metadata was provided by the originating web map. A package's item will be an instance of a RT_LocalItemHandle. Returns null if the package is not loaded. Since: 100.0.0
member.value: The mobile map package's RT_ItemHandle describing metadata about the package.

member.name: M:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreMobileMapPackage.Close
member.summary: Closes a mobile map package.
member.remarks:
Closes a mobile map package and frees file locks on the underlying .mmpk file or directory. All references to mobile map package data (maps, layers, tables, networks, locators, etc.) should be released before closing the package. If active references to mobile map package data exist, this method will still close the package, but subsequent rendering and data access methods will fail. Results of accessing mobile map package data after RT_MobileMapPackage_close are undefined. After closing a mobile map package, the underlying .mmpk file or directory can be moved or deleted.
Closing a mobile map package is not necessary if the package has not been loaded. Since: 100.6.0

member.summary: Checks if the package can be read directly without requiring to be unpacked. Always returns true after deprecation in version 100.7.
member.remarks: Prior to ArcGIS Runtime version 100.7, some data formats (such as RT_RasterLayerHandle) could only be accessed if they were unpacked from the mobile map package file (.mmpk). In these situations, this method would return false and you would need to call the RT_MobileMapPackage_unpackAsync to unpack the mmpk. From version 100.7 and onwards this limitation has been removed allowing the data to be read directly from the mobile map package file. This method always returns a result of true. Since this method is no longer required it can be removed from calling code including any subsequent use of RT_MobileMapPackage_unpackAsync. member.summary: Unpacks a mobile map package file (.mmpk) to an output directory.

member.name: T:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreMobileScenePackage
member.summary: A mobile scene package.
member.remarks:
Mobile scene packages allow you to work with 3D scenes on a mobile device. A mobile scene package contains all of the files necessary to work with your scenes and is stored on a device as either: A single archive file with an .mspk extension A directory containing an unpacked mobile scene package A mobile scene package can encapsulate one or more scenes, their layers and data, transportation networks and a locator. The mobile scene package also contains an RT_ItemHandle with metadata about the package (description, thumbnail, etc.). You can use these packages to share scenes across the ArcGIS platform and to allow your users to work with scenes in the field. Mobile scene packages also allow you to continue working when you have limited connectivity. Starting with ArcGIS Pro 2.3 you can create mobile scene packages for use in ArcGIS Runtime. This version of ArcGIS Runtime will support any mobile scene package up to major version 3.
Mobile scene packages can contain links to online services, but be aware that these services will be unavailable if your device is offline. You can choose whether to use: A tile package (.tpkx) or an online basemap as the RT_GeoModel_getBasemap A mobile geodatabase (.geodatabase) or an online feature service as one of the RT_GeoModel_getOperationalLayers Local raster data (such as a DTED, GeoTIFF) or online image services as the elevation sources in a RT_Scene_getBaseSurface
Online services (such as traffic or weather) can provide excellent contextual information for your users. If the mobile scene package is going to be used in areas of poor connectivity, however, you must ensure that data critical to your workflow is stored locally on the device.
Mobile scene packages implement the RT_LoadableInterface interface; you need to load the RT_MobileScenePackageHandle before you can access its content. Once loaded you can:
Determine the version of this package using the RT_MobileScenePackage_getVersion property. ArcGIS Runtime currently supports mobile scene packages up to and including major version If the package is from an unsupported version it will fail to load.
Discover whether the package has expired using the RT_MobileScenePackage_getExpiration property Access the individual scenes and display them in a RT_SceneViewHandle Programmatically add, modify, and remove layers in the scene. Mobile scene packages, however, are read-only and these changes to scenes or layers will not be persisted to the device. Since: 100.5.0

member.name: T:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreMultilayerSymbol
member.summary: A base class for multilayer symbols. Multilayer symbols are built from multiple layers of symbols, which combine to let you add complex symbols to maps and scenes.
member.remarks: Multilayer symbols can be returned from feature layers based on web maps, feature services (with Use Advanced Symbology set to true), or mobile map packages, and can also be created from JSON by calling RT_Symbol_fromJSON. The same multilayer symbols and the components used to build them are available in ArcGIS Runtime, allowing you to programmatically create and change them using the RT_MultilayerPointSymbolHandle, RT_MultilayerPolylineSymbolHandle, and RT_MultilayerPolygonSymbolHandle subclasses. You can access the layers that comprise the symbol through RT_MultilayerSymbol_getSymbolLayers. You can modify symbol layer properties, such as the color of a multilayer symbol. Some subclasses also expose additional symbol properties. The symbol layers that comprise the symbol can be of different types. For example, a polyline geometry may be drawn with a RT_MultilayerPolylineSymbolHandle that has line (stroke) symbol layers that draw the line geometry, and also point (marker) symbol layers that are drawn at specified point locations relative to the line geometry. When you save an ArcGIS Pro map as a web map, any multilayer symbols in the map are converted to simple symbols. In general, point symbols are converted to picture marker symbols optimized for the web, and line and polygon symbols are simplified while representing the original symbol as closely as possible. If you're authoring a feature service from ArcGIS Pro or ArcGIS Desktop, however, both the original symbols and the simplified symbols are stored. The stored symbols allow clients that support advanced symbols to render the features as originally symbolized, while those that do not support advanced symbols (such as ArcGIS Online Map Viewer) can use the simple symbols for display. Having both sets of symbols allows you to retain the advanced symbology where available and still share the feature service as widely as possible. Symbols used by web scenes are also multilayer but use a different specification than the ArcGIS Pro and ArcGIS Runtime symbols. When you read symbols from a web scene in your ArcGIS Runtime app, you get an ArcGIS Runtime representation of the multilayer symbol. Symbol layers in an ArcGIS Runtime multilayer symbol are in reverse order of how they appear in the JSON representation from the server. Since: 100.2.0

member.name: T:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreMultipart
member.summary: Defines common members for polyline and polygon multipart geometries.
member.remarks: Multipart geometries are based upon the parent RT_GeometryHandle class. The geometry class is immutable which means that you cannot change its shape once it is created. If you need to modify a multipart once it has been created, use the RT_MultipartBuilderHandle class instead. The RT_GeometryBuilder_toGeometry method will provide you with the base geometry object. A multipart geometry is comprised of a collection of shapes (of the same type) that is managed as a single geometry. A classic example is a set of islands that represent a single country or state. The individual island shapes are distinct, but ArcGIS considers it a single geometry. RT_PolygonHandle and RT_PolylineHandle inherit from multipart, which in turn inherits from RT_GeometryHandle. Multipart provides access to the geometry's RT_ImmutablePartCollectionHandle via the RT_Multipart_getParts property. Each RT_ImmutablePartHandle in the collection is a collection of RT_SegmentHandle objects. You can iterate through the segments or points in each part. Client: DOTNET JAVA KOTLIN OBJECTIVE_C PRO QT RUST SWIFT UNITY UNREAL Since: 100.0.0

member.name: T:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreMultipoint
member.summary: An ordered collection of points that can be managed as a single geometry.
member.remarks: RT_MultipointHandle geometries represent an ordered collection of points. They can be used as the geometry of features and graphics, or as input or output for spatial operations. For features that consist of a very large number of points that share the same set of attribute values, multipoints may be more efficient to store and analyze in a geodatabase compared to using multiple point features. A RT_MultipointHandle is composed of a single read-only collection of RT_PointHandle. Use RT_MultipointBuilderHandle to build a multipoint one point at a time or to modify an existing RT_MultipointHandle. member.name: T:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreMutablePart
member.summary: Represents a single part of a multipart builder.
member.remarks: Multipart builder is the base class of RT_PolygonBuilderHandle or RT_PolylineBuilderHandle. A part is made up of a collection of segments making the edge of the multipart. Additionally access and modified using the points (vertexes) of segments is available. Adjacent segments which share an end point and a start point are connected and the shared vertex is not duplicated when accessing points. The mutable part can represent gaps between one end point and an adjacent start. However, this is only recommended as a temporary state while modifying a multipart builder, when using RT_GeometryBuilder_toGeometry the gaps are closed with line segments. Prior to v100.12, the only supported segment type was RT_LineSegmentHandle. From v100.12, curve segments can be added to a RT_MutablePartHandle and used build polygon and polyline geometries. A part may contain a mix of linear and curve segments. Client: DOTNET JAVA KOTLIN OBJECTIVE_C PRO QT RUST SWIFT UNITY UNREAL Since: 100.0.0

member.summary: An accuracy calculated from GST (pseudo-range error statistics) message.

member.summary: An accuracy calculated from GSA (DOP and active satellites) message.

member.name: F:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreNMEAAccuracyType.GGA
member.summary: An accuracy calculated from GGA (time, position, and fix-related data) message.

member.name: T:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreNMEAFixType
member.summary: The list of NMEA fix types.
member.remarks: Indicates the type of signal or technique being used by the GPS receiver to determine its location. For example it indicates the quality of the signal, or the accuracy and reliability of the location being reported. The fix type is determined by the receiver based on number of satellites visible, the type of GPS receiver and the GPS technology being used. Since: 100.10.0

member.name: F:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreNMEAFixType.Invalid
member.summary: An invalid GPS fix type. Indicates that there is no satellite signal being received or there are not enough satellites available for proper location determination.

member.name: F:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreNMEAFixType.Standard
member.summary: A standard GPS fix type. Indicates a standard GPS signal, or Standard Positioning Service (SPS) is being used. SPS is the standard specified level of positioning and timing accuracy that is available, without qualification or restrictions, to any user on a continuous worldwide basis.

member.name: F:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreNMEAFixType.DGPS
member.summary: A differential GPS fix type. Indicates that Differential GPS is being used to provide increased accuracy over SPS. This technique uses a network of fixed ground based reference stations to broadcast the difference between the positions indicated by the satellite systems and the known fixed positions.

member.name: F:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreNMEAFixType.PPS
member.summary: A PPS GPS fix type. Indicates that Precise Positioning System, encrypted for government use is being used by the receiver. PPS is the most accurate positioning, velocity, and timing information continuously available, worldwide, from the basic GPS.

member.name: F:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreNMEAFixType.RTK
member.summary: A real time kinematic GPS fix type. A technique used in land survey based on the use of carrier phase measurements of the GPS signals where a single reference station provides the real-time corrections of even to a centimeter level of accuracy.

member.name: F:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreNMEAFixType.FRTK
member.summary: A float real time kinematic GPS fix type. The type is very similar to the fixed RTK (RT_NMEAFixType_RTK) method of calculating location, but is not as precise, typically around 20 cm to 1 meter accuracy range.

member.name: F:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreNMEAFixType.Estimated
member.summary: An estimated GPS fix type. The type is the determination of a location based on computations of position given an accurately known point of origin and measurements of speed, heading and elapsed time.

member.name: F:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreNMEAFixType.Manual
member.summary: A manual input mode GPS fix type. Indicates that the location has been manually entered into the GPS receiver, and is not based on the satellite system.

member.name: F:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreNMEAFixType.Simulation
member.summary: A simulation mode GPS fix type.

member.name: T:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreNMEALocationDataSource
member.summary: An NMEA location data source object.
member.remarks: This object will parse specific NMEA messages pushed into it. Valid GGA, GSA, GST, GSV, RMC, VTG messages are parsed and, depending upon the message type and contents, a RT_LocationDataSource_locationChanged_fn or RT_NMEALocationDataSource_satellitesChanged_fn may be raised. The RT_LocationDataSource_locationChanged_fn will return a RT_NMEALocationHandle object. The RT_NMEALocationDataSource_satellitesChanged_fn will return an array of RT_NMEASatelliteInfoHandle objects. This data source is based on NMEA version 4.11 (November 2018). The Apple AppStore has guidelines and restrictions for apps that communicate with MFi accessories (for example: an external GPS receiver). Apps that use NMEA data need to satisfy the Apple requirements to be accepted in the store. Apps need to declare support via PPID in their submission and the MFi provider needs to list the bundle ID so Apple can cross reference it. For more information see the site, MFi Program Since: 100.10.0

member.name: M:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreNMEALocationDataSource.#ctor(RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreSpatialReference,RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreSpatialReference,RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreDatumTransformation)
member.summary: Creates an NMEA data source object.
member.remarks: Locations created from an NMEA data source object instantiated with this constructor will be projected from the RT_SpatialReferenceHandle defined by the receiverSpatialReference parameter to the RT_SpatialReferenceHandle defined by the outputSpatialReference parameter using the outputDatumTransformation. If the outputSpatialReference parameter is null the locations will not be projected and the locations will be in the receiverSpatialReference, if the outputDatumTransformation parameter is set it will be ignored. This constructor can be used when a receiver is outputting locations in a RT_SpatialReferenceHandle other than WGS84, such as when using a reference base station, and/or the application requires the output locations to be projected to a different RT_SpatialReferenceHandle using a RT_DatumTransformationHandle. Since: 100.10.0

member.name: M:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreNMEALocationDataSource.PushData(System.Byte[])
member.summary: Reads the input NMEA data creating a RT_NMEALocationHandle. The NMEA location data source needs to be started before calling this method.
member.remarks: When pushing data: Each sentence needs to begins with a '$' Each sentence needs to end with carriage return/line feed sequence Single or multiple sentences can be pushed at one time, all strings in the buffer will be parsed There is no explicit limit on the amount of data that can pushed at one time If a partial sentences are pushed the data source accumulates (and concatenates) the pushed data until a carriage return/line feed sequence is reached The data source parses these messages types: GGA, GSA, GST, GSV, RMC, VTG Each sentence's checksum is validated Unknown/bad/incorrect sentences are ignored (they do not produce any location, satellite updates etc.) Sentences support up to 256 characters (this is beyond the NMEA spec's 82 character limit to support receiver's that output longer sentences) Messages should be of the form: "$XXYYY,[data]*[checksum]\r\n" Example: $GPGGA,092750.000,5321.6802,N,00630.3372,W,1,8,1.03,61.7,M,55.2,M,,*76 $GPGSA,A,3,10,07,05,02,29,04,08,13,,,,,1.72,1.03,1.38*0A $GPGSV,3,1,11,10,63,137,17,07,61,098,15,05,59,290,20,08,54,157,30*70 See https://www.nmea.org/ Since: 100.10.0
member.param: The data buffer that contains NMEA data.

member.name: T:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreOfflineMapParametersKey
member.summary: A key comprising of a service URL and type of an online service. The key is used to lookup values in a dictionary exposed by a RT_GenerateOfflineMapParameterOverridesHandle.
member.remarks: RT_GenerateOfflineMapParameterOverridesHandle consist of instances of data type specific parameters RT_GenerateGeodatabaseParametersHandle, RT_ExportTileCacheParametersHandle and RT_ExportVectorTilesParametersHandle. Each instance is associated with the service URL that the parameters will be sent to when taking the given data offline. The data type specific parameters can be retrieved from their respective dictionaries on RT_GenerateOfflineMapParameterOverridesHandle with an instance of RT_OfflineMapParametersKeyHandle. A key instance for a particular layer can be constructed by calling RT_OfflineMapParametersKey_createWithLayer. For a table, call RT_OfflineMapParametersKey_createWithTable. For a utility network, call RT_OfflineMapParametersKey_createWithUtilityNetwork. Use the key with the dictionary returned by one of these properties: RT_GenerateOfflineMapParameterOverrides_getGenerateGeodatabaseParameters, RT_GenerateOfflineMapParameterOverrides_getExportVectorTilesParameters, RT_GenerateOfflineMapParameterOverrides_getExportTileCacheParameters. The particular dictionary property will be determined by the RT_OfflineMapParametersKey_getType property. Note that a given parameters key/value pair may be shared by multiple layers in the map: for example a single RT_GenerateGeodatabaseParametersHandle could represent the online settings for multiple feature layers and tables which all access the same underlying feature service. Since: 100.4.0

member.name: P:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreOfflineMapSyncParameters.KeepGeodatabaseDeltas
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether or not the upload or downloaded delta geodatabases should be removed at the end of the sync job.
member.remarks:
A delta geodatabase is a file that contains the changes that have occurred since a mobile replica RT_GeodatabaseHandle was last synchronized with its feature service. See https://developers.arcgis.com/rest/services- reference/enterprise/synchronize-replica.htm for an overview of the delta files used in synchronization. There are two types of delta geodatabase: Local edits, performed on the user's device, are exported as an "upload" delta that is applied to the originating feature service Online edits, performed by other users are requested as a "download" delta which is then applied to the local replica geodatabase
Delta geodatabases allow you to troubleshoot sync problems. For example, you can inspect the geodatabase changes or you could send the file to the administrator of the feature service.
You can choose to retain both the uploaded and downloaded delta geodatabases once the sync job has completed. Set to true to retain both delta geodatabases and set to false to have them deleted at the end of the sync job. Deltas will be retained regardless of whether the job succeeds or fails. Note that when this property is set to true, the upload delta geodatabase will only be available if there are changes to upload and the sync direction is RT_SyncDirection_upload or RT_SyncDirection_bidirectional. The download delta geodatabase will only be available when there are changes to download and the sync direction is RT_SyncDirection_download or RT_SyncDirection_bidirectional. The default value is false.
No geodatabase deltas will be retained if your geodatabase uses a scheduled updates workflow. Since: 100.10.0
member.value: Indicates whether or not the upload or downloaded delta geodatabases should be removed at the end of the sync job.

member.name: P:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreOfflineMapSyncParameters.PreplannedScheduledUpdatesOption
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether scheduled updates will be downloaded from an online map area and applied to the map's data.
member.remarks: If the mobile geodatabases in your offline map were not registered for sync you can choose to download and apply those updates by setting this property to RT_PreplannedScheduledUpdatesOption_downloadAllUpdates. You specify whether an offline map will make use of scheduled updates by setting the RT_DownloadPreplannedOfflineMapParameters_getUpdateMode property before downloading. The default value is RT_PreplannedScheduledUpdatesOption_downloadAllUpdates. Since: 100.6.0
member.value: Determines whether scheduled updates will be downloaded from an online map area and applied to the map's data.

member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether geodatabase feature service synchronization should roll back on a failure.
member.remarks: The default is false (no rollback on failure). Since: 100.1.0
member.value: Indicates if geodatabase feature service synchronization should roll back on a failure.

member.name: P:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreOfflineMapSyncParameters.SyncDirection
member.summary: Gets or sets the synchronization direction for geodatabases registered with feature services.
member.remarks: This property applies to any geodatabases that are registered for feature service synchronization. It does not apply to geodatabases which use scheduled updates. The default value is RT_SyncDirection_bidirectional. If you select RT_SyncDirection_upload, any download only geodatabases (e.g. with RT_FeatureServiceCapabilities_getSupportsUpdate = false) will not be updated and you will receive a RT_ErrorType_mappingSyncDirectionUploadNotSupported error in the associated RT_OfflineMapSyncResult_getLayerResults. member.name: M:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreOfflineMapSyncTask.CheckForUpdatesAsync
member.summary: Returns a RT_TaskHandle of RT_OfflineMapUpdatesInfoHandle for the offline map that was used to construct this task.
member.remarks:
The returned RT_OfflineMapUpdatesInfoHandle provides high level information on what updates are available for this offline map. Information is provided on: Online changes that can be applied to update your offline map Local changes from your offline map that can be sent back to the online services Calling this method provides high-level information on the available updates. It can help you to determine whether to call RT_OfflineMapSyncTask_syncOfflineMap immediately, based upon factors such as current disk space and network availability. Examine these properties before starting the potentially time-consuming offline map sync process. The resulting RT_OfflineMapUpdatesInfoHandle provides a snap-shot of available updates when this method was called.
To check for new updates you need to call this method again. Since: 100.6.0
member.returns: A RT_TaskHandle of RT_OfflineMapUpdatesInfoHandle.

member.name: T:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreOfflineMapTask
member.summary: A task used to take a map offline.
member.remarks: Taking a map offline involves downloading an online map and its data, including all the supported layers, tables, renderers, web map configuration etc. so that it can be used offline without a network connection. There are two workflows available for taking maps offline: The preplanned offline workflow The on-demand offline workflow Preplanned offline workflow. In this workflow the author of an online map can define individual geographical areas called map areas. These map areas prepare map content that is stored online. An app can download that map content to a device using the RT_DownloadPreplannedOfflineMapJobHandle. On-demand offline workflow. Here the app passes a specific area of interest to a RT_GenerateOfflineMapJobHandle to generate and download the map content to the device. Using this workflow, you can choose to keep online only services (e.g. those that require a network connection) in your offline map. Be aware that an offline map which uses online only services will require a network connection and may require authentication. Since: 100.1.0

member.name: M:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreOfflineMapTask.CreateDefaultGenerateOfflineMapParametersAsync(RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreGeometry)
member.summary: Returns a RT_TaskHandle of RT_GenerateOfflineMapParametersHandle created from the specified area of interest.
member.remarks:
The supported geometry types for the area of interest are RT_EnvelopeHandle and RT_PolygonHandle. The area of interest must have a spatial reference. Where a RT_PolygonHandle is supplied, features and tiles will be filtered according to the polygon geometry, which can help reduce the size of the resulting offline map. Note that the filtered set of tiles may vary, depending on the the underlying service. The returned parameters min scale and max scale are zero so data will be taken at the full range of scales the services support.
The returned RT_GenerateOfflineMapParametersHandle has its itemInfo property initialized from the offline map task's portal item, if that is set.
The ItemInfo's thumbnail will be copied from the portal item's thumbnail.
The default parameters will be populated using the values in the online map's RT_OfflineSettingsHandle (if present). Non-overloaded method: CreateDefaultGenerateOfflineMapParametersAsync Since: 100.1.0
member.param: the region of the online map that is to be taken offline.
member.returns: a RT_TaskHandle of RT_GenerateOfflineMapParametersHandle

member.summary: Returns a RT_TaskHandle of RT_GenerateOfflineMapParametersHandle created from the specified area of interest, min scale and max scale.
member.remarks:

member.name: M:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreOfflineMapTask.CreateGenerateOfflineMapParameterOverridesAsync(RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreGenerateOfflineMapParameters)
member.summary: Returns a RT_TaskHandle of RT_GenerateOfflineMapParameterOverridesHandle created from the specified RT_GenerateOfflineMapParametersHandle parameters.
member.remarks:
When the task completes the RT_GenerateOfflineMapParameterOverridesHandle will be populated reflecting the values in the RT_GenerateOfflineMapParametersHandle parameters. The overrides may be inspected and modified to change the offline data before passing onto creating a job with RT_OfflineMapTask_generateOfflineMap. If there are errors with loading individual layers or tables, or they cannot be taken offline due to service settings, the outcome depends on the value of RT_GenerateOfflineMapParameters_getContinueOnErrors. If RT_GenerateOfflineMapParameters_getContinueOnErrors is true, the overrides correspond to the remaining layers and tables that can go offline.
The resulting offline map will not contain the layers or tables which had errors.
If RT_GenerateOfflineMapParameters_getContinueOnErrors is false, the returned RT_TaskHandle will complete containing an RT_ErrorHandle in the RT_Task_getError property from the failed layer or table.
To check upfront which layers or tables are valid for taking offline see RT_OfflineMapTask_getOfflineMapCapabilitiesAsync.
If RT_GenerateOfflineMapParameters_getReferenceBasemapDirectory is set, the overrides corresponding to online basemap layers will be omitted, since no basemap layers will be downloaded. Since: 100.4.0
member.param: The generate offline map parameters from which the overrides will be populated.
member.returns: a RT_TaskHandle of RT_GenerateOfflineMapParametersHandle

member.name: M:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreOfflineMapTask.DownloadPreplannedOfflineMap(RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CorePreplannedMapArea,System.String)
member.summary: Returns a job that is used to download the specified preplanned map area of an online map.
member.remarks:
The job that is returned is dormant and needs to be explicitly started. The job will fail if the last directory in the download directory path cannot be created or is not empty. Deprecated 100.10.0 Please use RT_OfflineMapTask_downloadPreplannedOfflineMapWithParameters.
This method does not support the scheduled updates workflow and will default to use RT_PreplannedUpdateMode_syncWithFeatureServices.
An instance of RT_DownloadPreplannedOfflineMapParametersHandle can be created and populated as required. Alternatively the recommended workflow is to use RT_OfflineMapTask_createDefaultDownloadPreplannedOfflineMapParametersAsync and then make any adjustments. This will determine if scheduled updates are present and update the property RT_DownloadPreplannedOfflineMapParameters_getUpdateMode appropriately. Non-overloaded method: DownloadPreplannedOfflineMap Since: 100.2.0
member.param: Specifies the preplanned map area to be downloaded.

The path to a folder where the map content is stored on the device. For example, to create a new mobile map package "my_mobile_map_package" in a parent directory "[my root path]/my_mobile_maps", this property would be "[my root path]/my_mobile_maps/my_mobile_map_package".
member.returns: A RT_DownloadPreplannedOfflineMapJobHandle to download a preplanned map area.

member.name: M:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreOfflineMapTask.DownloadPreplannedOfflineMap(RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CorePreplannedMapArea,System.String,System.Boolean)
member.summary: Returns a job that is used to download the specified preplanned map area of an online map but excludes the map's basemap.
member.remarks: If you exclude the map's basemap from the download the offline map's size will be smaller and consequently the download process will be faster. If you already have a basemap stored locally on your device you can add that to the offline map. The job that is returned is dormant and needs to be explicitly started. The job will fail if the last directory in the download directory path cannot be created or is not empty. Specifying exclude_basemap true will override the authored settings of preplanned map area and always exclude the basemap content. Deprecated 100.4.0 This method has been replaced by RT_OfflineMapTask_downloadPreplannedOfflineMapWithParameters. Use RT_DownloadPreplannedOfflineMapParameters_getIncludeBasemap to set basemap inclusion. Note reversal of logic from 'exclude basemap' to 'include basemap'. Non-overloaded method: DownloadPreplannedOfflineMapWithExcludeBasemap Since: 100.2.0
member.param: Specifies the preplanned map area to be downloaded.

The path to a folder where the map content is stored on the device. For example, to create a new mobile map package "my_mobile_map_package" in a parent directory "[my root path]/my_mobile_maps", this property would be "[my root path]/my_mobile_maps/my_mobile_map_package".
A boolean to exclude the basemap from the offline map.
member.returns: A RT_DownloadPreplannedOfflineMapJobHandle to download a preplanned map area.

member.name: P:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreOfflineMapUpdateCapabilities.SupportsScheduledUpdatesForFeatures
member.summary: Gets a value indicating whether an offline map supports downloading of read-only scheduled feature updates.
member.remarks: If this property is true, updates are generated whenever the online map area is refreshed. For example: according to its update schedule. Updates are prepared once and cached for download by all users of the offline map area. Sharing a single set of cached updates, rather than performing individual sync operations, reduces the load on the back-end services. This approach is scalable for large deployments. As updates are only downloaded, this approach can only be used with read-only workflows. The updates reflect a snapshot of the feature data at the time the online map area was refreshed. It does not reflect the most up-to-date feature data. For this approach the web map author must configure the online map to perform scheduled updates. If this property is false, no updates will be available for download. Since: 100.6.0
member.value: Whether an offline map supports downloading of read-only scheduled feature updates.

member.name: P:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreOfflineMapUpdatesInfo.ScheduledUpdatesDownloadSize
member.summary: Gets the total size in bytes of update files to download for a scheduled updates workflow.
member.remarks: The scheduled updates workflow allows read-only updates to be stored with the online map area and downloaded to your device at a later time. Updates can cover several sets of changes to the online geodatabase and can cover multiple geodatabases in an offline map. This property is the total download size of all files required to update your offline map. You can use this information to determine whether you want to download updates immediately - for example based on available disk space or network availability. If there are no updates available, or your offline map does not use a scheduled updates workflow, this property will be 0. Since: 100.6.0
member.value: The total size in bytes of update files to download for a scheduled updates workflow.

member.name: T:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreOGCFeatureCollectionTable
member.summary: An OGC API - Features feature collection table.
member.remarks:
To display data from an OGC feature collection table in a RT_FeatureLayerHandle use the RT_FeatureLayer_createWithFeatureTable constructor where the RT_OGCFeatureCollectionTableHandle is the parameter that is passed into the constructor. Note: The RT_OGCFeatureCollectionTableHandle should not be confused with RT_FeatureCollectionTableHandle which is used as an input to create a RT_FeatureCollectionLayerHandle. The ArcGIS Runtime API for OGC API Features provides building blocks for manipulating features on the Web. For more information about the OGC API Features specification see the documents: OGC API - Features - Part 1 and OGC API - Features - Part 2 .
The class includes two important members: the RT_OGCFeatureCollectionTable_getFeatureRequestMode property and the RT_OGCFeatureCollectionTable_populateFromService method. Only the RT_FeatureRequestMode_manualCache mode is supported. This means RT_OGCFeatureCollectionTable_populateFromService must be called to populate, query, and return features from the service. For the RT_QueryParameters_getWhereClause that is used by the RT_OGCFeatureCollectionTable_populateFromService method, you can put any CQL-TEXT or CQL-JSON string as defined in the document OGC API - Features - Part3 .
When populating or updating a local table from an OGC service, you can now request features in a specified RT_SpatialReferenceHandle (also referred to as SRS in ArcGIS or CRS in OGC). This leverages the power of the server to return features in the same spatial reference as your map rather than having to re-project them on the client.
This class supports loading and querying of features from a non-spatial OGC feature collection table. Since: 100.9.0

member.name: T:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreOpenStreetMapLayer
member.summary: A layer that requests images from OpenStreetMap servers.
member.remarks: OpenStreetMap (OSM) is a project to create a free, publicly editable map of the world. This layer displays map content from OpenStreetMap tile servers . An RT_OpenStreetMapLayerHandle is a preconfigured RT_WebTiledLayerHandle. Unlike a web tiled layer, it comes with predefined attribution and does not support identify, query, selection, or time. Performance of OSM layers is similar to web tiled layer performance. Raster tiles are read from the service as needed by the map. Use of OpenStreetMap's tiles is subject to their tile usage policy. Consider the following before using an OpenStreetMap layer in your app: Service availability is not guaranteed. Apps with high demand may be denied access at any time. There are many organizations providing OpenStreetMap tiles. Consider using one of these services (or hosting your own) if you anticipate high demand. Since: 100.1.0

member.name: M:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreOrbitLocationCameraController.#ctor
member.summary: Create an orbit camera controller object for a geo element.
member.remarks: An Orbit camera controller is used associate camera navigation and movement with a point object. This can take the form of a point Graphic RT_GraphicHandle or a point feature RT_FeatureHandle. When the controller is set on the Scene View using RT_SceneView_getCameraController the interaction mode for will change for the active navigation model be focused on the input point object allowing the user to rotation around and zoom in an out from the object. For a moving point object the camera will move in synchronization it. Adjusting it position, heading, pitch and roll with the object by simply changing the object with no requirement to change the camera. Client: DOTNET QT Since: 100.1.0

member.summary: Create an orbit camera controller object with a target point and distance from that point.
member.remarks: Create an Orbit camera controller and associate it with a point object and set the distance of the camera from this point object. When the controller is set on the Scene View using RT_SceneView_getCameraController the interaction mode for will change for the active navigation model be focused on the input point allowing the user to rotation around and zoom in an out from the point. Since: 100.1.0
member.param: A pointer to the RT_PointHandle which will be the focus of the camera in the view.
The distance from the point the camera will be placed.

Since: 100.3.0
member.param: A RT_PointHandle which will be the focus of the camera in the view.
A RT_PointHandle which is where the camera is located.

member.name: T:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CorePictureFillSymbolLayer
member.summary: A symbol layer that fills polygon geometry with an image.
member.remarks: The specified image fills the layer's polygon if it's the only symbol layer in a RT_MultilayerPolygonSymbolHandle. If a single image doesn't completely fill the geometry, it is tiled to complete the fill. This layer can also represent the Web Scene specification's Icon3DSymbolLayers. RT_PictureFillSymbolLayerHandle represents IconSymbol3DLayers that contain pictures and RT_VectorMarkerSymbolLayerHandle represents Icon3DSymbolLayers that are primitives or vector paths. Since: 100.5.0

member.name: P:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CorePictureFillSymbolLayer.Image
member.summary: Gets the image held by a picture fill symbol layer.
member.remarks: The RT_ImageHandle held by the given RT_PictureFillSymbolLayerHandle. Setting the image visually changes the image that makes up the fill pattern. If the image is valid and non-empty, this function sets the image and sets the symbol layer's load status to RT_LoadStatus_loaded. You cannot set an image on a RT_PictureFillSymbolLayerHandle that has already loaded. Since: 100.5.0

member.name: P:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CorePictureFillSymbolLayer.TintColor
member.summary: Gets or sets the tint color of a picture fill symbol layer.
member.remarks: The tint color is applied to the entire image by multiplying each RGB color channel in the image by the corresponding color channel of the tint color. The default tint color is white with 100% opacity, i.e. RGBA(255, 255, 255, 255), which leaves the image with its native colors. A white tint color with opacity less than 100% tints the image white, with the reduced opacity respected. When getting the tint color from a symbol, the consensus value is reported. If there is no consensus (one or more layers have different colors), a null value is reported for the color. Likewise, setting a value for tint color on a symbol will apply that tint color to all layers the symbol contains. Since: 100.6.0
member.value: The tint color of a picture fill symbol layer.

member.name: T:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CorePictureMarkerSymbolLayer
member.summary: A struct that implements picture marker symbol layers.
member.remarks: A RT_PictureMarkerSymbolLayerHandle represents a symbol layer used to place a picture marker on a point geometry. This symbol layer, in a RT_MultilayerPointSymbolHandle, places a picture marker at the location of the point feature. The class supports changing dimensions of the marker, specifying the image (or URI linking to the image) to use as the marker, as well as the general marker options provided by the RT_MarkerSymbolLayerHandle base class. This symbol layer is similar to the Web Scene specification's IconSymbol3DLayer, when the IconSymbol3DLayer references an image. RT_PictureMarkerSymbolLayerHandle is also similar to the Web Map specification's RT_PictureMarkerSymbolHandle. As a symbol layer, RT_PictureMarkerSymbolLayerHandle can be combined with other symbol layers in a RT_MultilayerSymbolHandle, whereas RT_PictureMarkerSymbolHandle cannot. Since: 100.5.0
