member.summary: Returns a list representing the datum transformations suitable for projecting between spatial references without taking into account an area of interest.
member.remarks: The list is ordered in descending order by suitability, with the most suitable being first in the list. Some transformations require a supporting Projection Engine (PE) dataset to function correctly - see RT_GeographicTransformationStep_getProjectionEngineFilenames and RT_HorizontalVerticalTransformationStep_getProjectionEngineFilenames. The list may include grid-based transformations, whether or not these datasets can be located by the Runtime From version 100.9 onwards, if both inputSpatialReference and outputSpatialReference have a vertical coordinate system, this method returns a RT_HorizontalVerticalTransformationHandle instance. If either SpatialReference does not have a vertical coordinate system, a RT_GeographicTransformationHandle is returned. A geographic transformation is not needed when input and output spatial references have the same underlying geographic (horizontal) coordinate system. A vertical transformation is not needed if both datums (for ellipsoidal heights) or vertical datums (for gravity-related heights) are the same. If neither type of transformation is needed, an empty collection is returned. To replicate the former behavior, use the RT_TransformationCatalog_getTransformationsBySuitabilityWithAreaOfInterestAndIgnoreVertical method instead with 'ignoreVertical = true'. see RT_DatumTransformation_getIsMissingProjectionEngineFiles. Prior to version 100.9, this method only considered geographic coordinate systems, and the returned array of DatumTransformation objects were of the subtype RT_GeographicTransformationHandle. A geographic transformation is not required when input and output spatial references have the same underlying geographic coordinate system, in which case an empty list was returned.

member.name: T:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreTravelMode
member.summary: An object that represents a travel mode.
member.remarks: Travel modes on a network dataset define how a pedestrian, car, truck, or other medium of transportation moves through the network. A travel mode consists of a collection of network dataset settings that define actions that are allowed on the network and how the actions can be performed. Selecting a predefined travel mode allows you to efficiently and consistently set a number of properties that are appropriate for the mode of travel you intend to model. Since a travel mode is a collection of properties that work together it is recommended to have a full understanding of how these properties interact before altering them on the fly for a particular analysis. A best practice would be to create a new travel mode in the network dataset in ArcGIS Desktop or ArcGIS Pro that is fully tested to ensure that is returns the required solution. Since: 100.0.0

member.remarks: A unique value can have alternate symbols to the primary symbol. Alternate symbols allow you to tailor the visualization of unique value at different scales by selecting different symbol for different scales. Alternate symbols are supported only when unique value's primary symbol and other symbols in alternate symbol list are of type RT_MultilayerSymbolHandle and have RT_SymbolReferencePropertiesHandle defining valid min max scales at which the symbol becomes visible. Renderer will pick only one symbol at a given map scale. If primary symbol's scale range falls within the map's scale, primary symbol is used. If not, then symbols in alternate symbols list are iterated through and first symbol matching the current map scale is picked for rendering. A symbol becomes visible if the map scale is less than or equal to symbol's minimum scale and greater than symbol's maximum scale. For more information on Scale-based symbol classes and alternate symbols see the following documentation: https://pro.arcgis.com/en/pro-app/latest/help/mapping/layer-properties/scale- based-symbol-classes.htm Since: 100.13.0

member.name: T:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreUnit
member.summary: Defines a unit of measurement.
member.remarks:
The unit is a common base class for different types of measurement (linear, angular, and area) used throughout ArcGIS Runtime. Many function parameters only accept specific types of measurement to reduce the chance of accidental use of inappropriate values, but some generic functions accept all unit types e.g. for translation from ID to text description. RT_LinearUnitHandle - Projected coordinate systems define coordinates using linear measurements, for example using meters or miles. They are also used to return distance measurements, for example by some members of RT_GeometryEngineHandle. RT_AngularUnitHandle - Geographic coordinate systems define coordinates using angular measurements, for example using degrees or radians.
RT_AreaUnitHandle - Projected coordinate systems define area units for two dimensional measurements such as the area enclosed by a ring, for example in acres or square kilometers.
Linear, angular, and area units can be defined by using enumerations of the most common units of measurement. They can also be defined by Well-Known ID (WKID) or Well-Known Text (WKText). Create the unit instances using the Unit base class or the subtype, passing in the enumeration for a specific unit of measurement.
Construction of related units are also supported so that if, for instance, the LinearUnit (e.g. METERS) is known, then the corresponding AreaUnit (e.g. SQUARE_METERS) can be created based on the LinearUnit.
Custom unit implementations are not supported.
Each instance of the various units types has properties for the unit name (singular, plural, and abbreviated) and provides methods for unit conversion between different units of measurement in the same category of measurement.
All unit names and abbreviations are returned in the English language. Instances of unit are immutable. Client: DOTNET JAVA KOTLIN OBJECTIVE_C PRO QT RUST SWIFT UNITY UNREAL Since: 100.0.0

member.name: T:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreUSNGGrid
member.summary: A class that represents the display of the United States National Grid (USNG) on the map view.
member.remarks: The United States National Grid (USNG) is a point reference system of grid references commonly used in the United States. It provides a nationally consistent language of location in a user friendly format. It is similar in design to the national grid reference systems used throughout other nations. The USNG was developed by the Federal Geographic Data Committee. To display the USNG grid, create a USNGGrid and set it as the grid property within the MapView. USNGGrid inherits from Grid and adds a property for the label unit to use. Since: 100.0.0

member.name: M:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreUSNGGrid.#ctor
member.summary: Constructs an USNG grid for displaying on a map view.
member.remarks: The grid is supported in spatial references which are continuously pannable or some polar spatial references. You can check the RT_SpatialReference_getIsPannable property is true on your spatial reference. Examples of continuously pannable spatial references include WGS84 (WKID 4326) and Web Mercator Auxiliary Sphere (WKID 102113, 102100, or 3857). The following polar spatial references are also supported: North pole Azimuthal Equidistant (WKID 102016) North pole gnomic (WKID 102034) North pole Lambert equal area (WKID 102017) North pole orthographic (WKID 102035) North pole stereographic (WKID 102018) NSIDE EASE North (WKID 3408) NSIDC Sea Ice polar stereographic north (WKID 3411) WGS 1984 NSIDC Sea Ice Polar Stereographic North (WKID 3413) UPS North (WKID 32661) South pole Azimuthal Equidistant (WKID 102019) South pole gnomic (WKID 102036) South pole Lambert equal area (WKID 102020) South pole orthographic (WKID 102037) South pole stereographic (WKID 102021) NSIDE EASE South (WKID 3409) NSIDC Sea Ice polar stereographic South (WKID 3412) UPS South (WKID 32761) *- WGS1984 Antarctic polar stereographic (WKID 3031) Since: 100.0.0

member.name: T:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreUtilityAssociation
member.summary: A connectivity, containment, or structural attachment association.
member.remarks: Associations are an integral part of network topology. Connectivity associations allow connectivity between two junctions that don't have geometric coincidence (are not in the same location). Structural attachment associations allow modeling equipment attached to structures. Containment associations allow modeling containment of features within other features. Network traces make use of associations. Associations are defined using two RT_UtilityElementHandle objects. Since: 100.7.0

member.summary: Gets the relative location along the non-spatial edge where the junction is (logically) located.
member.remarks: If this is a junction to a non-spatial edge connectivity association, this property represents how far the junction is located along the non-spatial edge, from 0.0 (the edge's start point) and 1.0 (the edge's end point). If this association represents RT_UtilityAssociationType_junctionEdgeObjectConnectivityToSide, the value will be 0.0, if RT_UtilityAssociationType_junctionEdgeObjectConnectivityMidspan, the value will be between 0.0 and 1.0, and if RT_UtilityAssociationType_junctionEdgeObjectConnectivityFromSide, the value will be 1.0. The default value is 0.0. Since: 100.10.0
member.value: The relative location along the non-spatial edge where the junction is (logically) located.

member.name: P:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreUtilityElement.IsValid
member.summary: Gets a value indicating whether or not the RT_UtilityElementHandle has complete data available.
member.remarks:
When taking a RT_UtilityNetworkHandle offline, some of the data can be filtered out to limit the size of the data. This may leave some elements in an incomplete state. For example, one element of an association may be included in the offline dataset while the other element may not. When an element is incomplete, the following properties should not be used: RT_UtilityElement_getAssetGroup RT_UtilityElement_getAssetType RT_UtilityElement_getObjectId RT_UtilityElement_getTerminal
When RT_UtilityElement_getIsValid is false, the RT_UtilityAssetTypeHandle is assumed to have a RT_UtilityAssociationDeletionSemantics of RT_UtilityAssociationDeletionSemantics_restricted. Since: 100.11.0
member.value: Indicates whether or not the RT_UtilityElementHandle has complete data available.

member.name: P:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreUtilityNetwork.Geodatabase
member.summary: Gets the RT_GeodatabaseHandle that contains this RT_UtilityNetworkHandle.
member.remarks:
The RT_GeodatabaseHandle that contains this RT_UtilityNetworkHandle and is also used by the RT_GeodatabaseFeatureTableHandle in RT_UtilityNetworkDefinition_getNetworkSources. Use this property to manage transactions, sync edits, or access tables participating in this RT_UtilityNetworkHandle. This property has a value when the RT_UtilityNetworkHandle is retrieved from a RT_GeodatabaseHandle; otherwise, when created using any of the constructors, this property is null.
Note that calling RT_Geodatabase_close on a RT_GeodatabaseHandle that contains this RT_UtilityNetworkHandle will render this RT_UtilityNetworkHandle unusable. An attempt to create an element, get associations, get features from elements, or perform a trace after this RT_GeodatabaseHandle is closed will fail with RT_ErrorType_geodatabaseDatabaseClosed. Since: 100.11.0
member.value: The RT_GeodatabaseHandle that contains this RT_UtilityNetworkHandle.

member.name: P:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreUtilityNetwork.ServiceGeodatabase
member.summary: Gets the RT_ServiceGeodatabaseHandle of the RT_UtilityNetworkHandle.
member.remarks:
The RT_ServiceGeodatabaseHandle used by the RT_ServiceFeatureTableHandle in RT_UtilityNetworkDefinition_getNetworkSources. Use this property to switch to a branch version, manage edits, or query related records of tables participating in this RT_UtilityNetworkHandle. This property is null until the RT_UtilityNetworkHandle is loaded. The RT_MapHandle that was used to create this RT_UtilityNetworkHandle provides this RT_ServiceGeodatabaseHandle. When no matching RT_ServiceGeodatabaseHandle is found in the RT_MapHandle, this RT_UtilityNetworkHandle will create and load a RT_ServiceGeodatabaseHandle connected to the default version in RT_FeatureServiceSessionType_transient mode.
This property is also null when the RT_UtilityNetworkHandle is retrieved from a RT_GeodatabaseHandle.
Note that calling RT_ServiceGeodatabase_closeAsync on a RT_ServiceGeodatabaseHandle that is used by a RT_UtilityNetworkHandle will render this RT_UtilityNetworkHandle unusable. An attempt to create an element, get associations, get features from elements, or perform a trace after this RT_ServiceGeodatabaseHandle is closed will fail with RT_ErrorType_geodatabaseDatabaseClosed. Since: 100.10.0
member.value: The RT_ServiceGeodatabaseHandle of the RT_UtilityNetworkHandle.

member.name: T:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreUtilityNetworkAttribute
member.summary: A network attribute in a utility network.
member.remarks: A Network Attribute is an attribute that is copied and stored in the topological index. The utility network tracing task can read and make decisions using network attributes that are stored directly in the topological index. The network attributes in a topological index are limited to specific data types and aggregate size. Since: 100.6.0

member.name: T:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreUtilityPropagator
member.summary: Propagator objects allow a subset of RT_UtilityNetworkAttributeHandle values to propagate through a network while executing a trace.
member.remarks:
The propagated RT_UtilityNetworkAttributeHandle values can be tested to allow or disallow further traversal. In the example of phase propagation, open devices along the network will restrict some phases from continuing along the trace. Propagators only apply to subnetwork-based traces (RT_UtilityTraceType_upstream, RT_UtilityTraceType_downstream, and so on).
RT_UtilityPropagatorHandle is set in the RT_UtilityTraceConfigurationHandle. Since: 100.7.0

member.name: F:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreUtilityTierType.Hierarchical
member.summary: Tiers within this domain network are hierarchical.
member.remarks: In hierarchical domain networks, tiers are nested within one another, so features existing in subnetworks for a lower tier naturally participate in all higher tiers. For example, in a gas network, a valve isolation zone is within a pressure zone, which in turn exists within a system zone. A feature in the isolation zone also exists in the pressure zone and in the system zone. Since: 100.7.0

member.summary: Tiers within this domain network are partitioned.

member.name: P:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreUtilityTraceConfiguration.IgnoreBarriersAtStartingPoints
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether to ignore barriers at starting points.
member.remarks: The default is False. One example of how this can be used is with an upstream protective device trace. The first call to the trace will return the first upstream device that meets the protective device criteria. To find the next device upstream, you would set a starting point on the device returned by the first trace. With IgnoreBarriersAtStartingPoints set to False, this second trace would immediately stop at the starting point, since it meets the trace termination criteria. Setting this option to True will allow the trace to ignore the starting point, and continue to the subsequent device upstream. Since: 100.7.0
member.value: Indicates whether to ignore barriers at starting points.

member.name: P:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreUtilityTraceConfiguration.OutputAssetTypes
member.summary: Gets or sets a collection of RT_UtilityAssetTypeHandle objects which specifies what to include in the trace results.
member.remarks: Only elements that belong to this RT_UtilityAssetTypeHandle are included in the trace result. This property is independent of asset types in the RT_UtilityTraceConfiguration_getFilter. This is applied after all other tracing calculations, including traversal, filters, and function calculation. If this is empty and RT_UtilityTraceConfiguration_getOutputCondition is null, all elements are returned. Otherwise, elements which match either of these criteria are returned. Since: 100.9.0
member.value: A collection of RT_UtilityAssetTypeHandle objects which specifies what to include in the trace results.

member.name: P:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreUtilityTraceConfiguration.OutputCondition
member.summary: Gets or sets a condition object which specifies what to include in the trace results.
member.remarks: Only elements that satisfy this RT_UtilityTraceConditionHandle are included in the trace result. This condition may perform comparisons against network attributes (RT_UtilityNetworkAttributeComparisonHandle) and categories (RT_UtilityCategoryComparisonHandle), or both (RT_UtilityTraceAndConditionHandle, RT_UtilityTraceOrConditionHandle). This property is independent of barriers in the RT_UtilityTraceConfiguration_getTraversability or RT_UtilityTraceConfiguration_getFilter. This is applied after all other tracing calculations, including traversal, filters, and function calculation. If this is null and RT_UtilityTraceConfiguration_getOutputAssetTypes is empty, all elements are returned. Otherwise, elements which match either of these criteria are returned. Since: 100.9.0
member.value: A condition object which specifies what to include in the trace results.

member.name: P:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreUtilityTraceConfiguration.Propagators
member.summary: Gets or sets a collection of RT_UtilityPropagatorHandle objects to execute while performing the trace.
member.remarks: Propagator objects allow a subset of RT_UtilityNetworkAttributeHandle values to propagate through a network while executing a trace. For example, in phase propagation, open devices along the network will restrict some phases from continuing along the trace. Propagators only apply to subnetwork-based traces. (RT_UtilityTraceType_upstream, RT_UtilityTraceType_downstream, and so on). Since: 100.7.0
member.value: A collection of RT_UtilityPropagatorHandle objects to execute while performing the trace.

member.name: P:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreUtilityTraceConfiguration.ShortestPathNetworkAttribute
member.summary: Gets or sets the RT_UtilityNetworkAttributeHandle used to calculate the shortest path.
member.remarks: The shortest path may depend on some other numeric weight, such as cost or difficulty, rather than the shortest distance calculated from shape length. Since: 100.9.0
member.value: The RT_UtilityNetworkAttributeHandle used to calculate the shortest path.

member.name: P:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreUtilityTraceConfiguration.SourceTier
member.summary: Gets or sets the RT_UtilityTierHandle that is used as the start of the trace.
member.remarks: This property is only used with subnetwork-based traces (subnetwork upstream, etc.). If RT_UtilityTraceConfiguration_getDomainNetwork represents a partitioned network, this property is optional. If not null, the Trace routines will perform an additional check to validate that the starting points and barriers belong to this tier. If RT_UtilityTraceConfiguration_getDomainNetwork represents a hierarchical network, this property is required. Since rows in hierarchical networks can belong to multiple tiers, this property tells the subnetwork tracer which tier to use for tracing. Since: 100.7.0
member.value: The RT_UtilityTierHandle that is used as the start of the trace.

member.name: T:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreUtilityTraceFilter
member.summary: A mechanism to stop tracing when returning results. RT_UtilityTraceFilterHandle objects do not stop traversability to the controller.
member.remarks: Consider an upstream protective device trace. At first, you might try defining a RT_UtilityCategoryComparisonHandle that looks for a Protective Device category and assigning this to RT_UtilityTraversability_getBarriers. When you try to run an upstream trace using this configuration, it will probably fail. This is because traversability will stop at the first protective device, and the trace will be unable to find the subnetwork controller. The correct way to implement this trace is to assign RT_UtilityCategoryComparisonHandle to the filter. RT_UtilityTraceFilterHandle is set in the RT_UtilityTraceConfigurationHandle Since: 100.8.0

member.name: P:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreUtilityTraceParameters.FilterBarriers
member.summary: Gets or sets the collection of filter barriers.
member.remarks: A regular barrier, specified by RT_UtilityTraceParameters_getBarriers, prevents traversal which, when used with subnetwork-based traces, can prevent traversal to the subnetwork controller. Like RT_UtilityTraceConfiguration_getFilter, filter barriers are evaluated in the second pass of a trace. Therefore, it can restrict the result set without impacting the ability to find subnetwork controllers from starting points. One example of where filter barriers can be used is in the gas distribution domain. Filter barriers can be used to simulate the location of a squeeze-off when executing a valve isolation trace. The user can place a filter barrier at the proposed location of the squeeze-off and then verify its impact using a trace. Since: 100.10.0
member.value: The collection of filter barriers.

member.name: T:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreUTMConversionMode
member.summary: Determines how latitude is designated in UTM notation.
member.remarks: Within a single longitudinal zone within the UTM system, two points share the same grid position: one in the northern hemisphere and one in the south. Two schemes are used to resolve this ambiguity. In the first, the point is designated a latitude band, identified with letters C through X (omitting I and O). In the second, in place of the latitude band, a hemisphere indicator (N or S) is used. Client: DOTNET JAVA KOTLIN OBJECTIVE_C PRO QT RUST SWIFT UNITY UNREAL Since: 100.1.0

member.summary: The letter after the UTM zone number represents a latitudinal band (C through X, omitting I and O).

member.name: T:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreUTMGrid
member.summary: A class that represents the display of the Universal Transverse Mercator (UTM) coordinate system grid on the map view.
member.remarks: The Universal Transverse Mercator (UTM) conformal projection uses a 2-dimensional Cartesian coordinate system to give locations on the surface of the Earth. Like the traditional method of latitude and longitude, it is a horizontal position representation, i.e. it is used to identify locations on the Earth independently of vertical position. However, it differs from that method in several respects. The UTM system is not a single map projection. The system instead divides the Earth into sixty zones, each being a six-degree band of longitude, and uses a secant transverse Mercator projection in each zone. To display the UTM grid, create a UTMGrid and set it as the grid property within the MapView. Since: 100.0.0

member.name: T:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreVector
member.summary: *Internal Use* Defines a dynamic array that provides callbacks when elements are added or removed.
member.remarks:
The vector holds RT_ElementHandle objects. Use RT_Vector_getValueType to determine what type of RT_ElementHandle objects are being stored in the vector. A RT_ElementHandle that has been retrieved from the vector can be converted to its underlying type by calling (for example) int32_t int_value = RT_Element_getValueAsInt32(element_handle, error_handler); There are a couple of performance optimizations to consider with the generic collection type: The RT_ElementHandle object can be reused for multiple calls while adding/inserting/updating values within the collection. So you can instantiate one RT_ElementHandle and iteratively change it's value and call add/update/insert on the collection to modify the values of the collection.
If the overhead of creating these RT_ElementHandle does become too much for a specific value type, then consider subclassing the collection type and provide "overloaded" methods that would accept that value type directly. This would eliminate the overhead of instantiating these RT_ElementHandle objects. Internal Use This should not be exposed to external Esri developers. member.name: T:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreVectorMarkerSymbolElement
member.summary: The RT_VectorMarkerSymbolElementHandle represents a component of a vector marker. A single RT_VectorMarkerSymbolElementHandle is a combination of a symbol and a geometry.
member.remarks: The symbol held by the RT_VectorMarkerSymbolElementHandle is itself a RT_MultilayerSymbolHandle. The geometry of the RT_VectorMarkerSymbolElementHandle does not pertain to the geography of the Map or Scene. Rather, the geometry property describes the shape of the Multilayer_symbol held by the RT_VectorMarkerSymbolElementHandle. The coordinate values defining the geometry are in points. This behavior facilitates creating a custom RT_VectorMarkerSymbolElementHandle of custom shape and symbol, then combining it with zero or more other elements to form a vector marker. To create a red square, for example, construct a RT_VectorMarkerSymbolElementHandle with a RT_MultilayerPolygonSymbolHandle that contains a red RT_SolidFillSymbolLayerHandle and a square geometry. When combined in a RT_VectorMarkerSymbolElementHandle and placed in a RT_VectorMarkerSymbolLayerHandle a red square displays. The symbol and geometry properties must create a meaningful combination to have a visual effect. For example, a RT_MultilayerPolygonSymbolHandle does not draw anything if the corresponding geometry is a point, but does draw if the geometry is a polygon. Since: 100.5.0

member.name: T:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreVectorTileCache
member.summary: Metadata for a local cache of vector map tiles that can be used to create a layer.
member.remarks: Local tile caches are ideal for providing basemaps or less frequently changing contextual layers, where network access is limited or non-existent. They can be created and downloaded onto a device by using an RT_ExportVectorTilesJobHandle, or alternatively can be provisioned directly to local storage. Currently the only supported type of cache is: Vector tile package (.vtpk) - a map and the tile cache of the data contained within it, packaged into one convenient, portable file, ideal for offline sharing or complete map documents in a disconnected environment or via a portal. A VectorTileCache is often used as a basemap, but can also be used to create an RT_ArcGISVectorTiledLayerHandle that is added to a map as an operational layer. Since: 100.2.0

member.summary: Loads the metadata for the object asynchronously.
member.remarks: Loads the metadata if the object is not loaded and always calls RT_Loadable_setDoneLoadingCallback. DOCUMENTATION FOR THE ArcGISFeature IMPLEMENTATION OF Loadable.load ONLY An ArcGISFeature is loadable. Depending on a ServiceFeatureTable's feature request mode, queries on the table can return ArcGISFeature objects which have the minimum set of attributes required for rendering and labeling (and geometries do not include m-values). See RT_ServiceFeatureTable_queryFeaturesWithFieldOptions, RT_FeatureRequestMode_onInteractionCache, and RT_FeatureRequestMode_onInteractionNoCache. To access all attributes in the returned ArcGISFeatures, call this method on each feature. For alternative ways to load all attributes in the returned features, see RT_ServiceFeatureTable_loadOrRefreshFeatures or RT_ServiceFeatureTable_queryFeaturesWithFieldOptions. Since: 100.2.0

member.summary: Gets or sets the horizontal angle of the observer's field of vision.

member.name: P:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreViewshed.MinDistance

member.remarks: The minimum distance allows you to exclude obstacles close to the observer (the corner of a building, for example). member.summary: A layer that requests images from a tiled image server based on a URL template.
member.remarks:
It provides a simple way to integrate non-ArcGIS Services as a layer in a map. The URL template usually follows a pattern similar to https://{subDomain}.server.org/path/{level}/{col}/{row}.png, where: "subDomain" is one of the strings in the subDomains list "level" corresponds to a zoom level "col" represents the column of the tile "row" represents the row of the tile The URL should be arranged to reflect how the tiles are organized in the cache or on the server, and can point to a web server ( https:// ) or to a local file cache ( file:// ).
The tiles retrieved by this class are accessed directly by URL. Because the service is only providing images, you are responsible for manually setting the attribution text on the map or scene view.
To create a custom service tiled layer whose URL follows the above pattern (or a similar pattern), you can extend this class. Alternatively, you can extend the super class RT_ServiceImageTiledLayerHandle, in which you implement a required method to set the request information for a given LOD, column, and row. Extending RT_WebTiledLayerHandle, however, has no such requirement.
A RT_ErrorType_commonInvalidArgument exception will be thrown when attempting to load a layer with invalid template URI.
If RT_TileInfoHandle is not specified, tiles are assumed to be in the OpenStreetMap tiling scheme, with 256x256 PNG tiles at 96 DPI, the WebMercator projection, and a FullExtent of [-180, -85.0511, 180, 85.051].
Functional characteristics Tiles are fetched on demand using the specified URL template. Tiles are typically pre-rendered (cached) on the server but may be generated on demand by some services. Web tiled layers do not support identify, query, selection, or time.
Tiles are fetched on demand using the specified URL template. Tiles are typically prerendered (cached) on the server but may be generated on demand by some services. Web tiled layers do not support identify, query, selection, or time.
Specifying subdomains from which the layer will request tiles allows the load to be more evenly distributed among servers.
Performance characteristics
Web tiled layer requires a connection to the service at all times. Performance is similar to other raster tile layers. Since: 100.1.0

member.name: P:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreWFSFeatureTable.AxisOrder
member.summary: Gets or sets the axis order, which defines how coordinates are interpreted.
member.remarks: Some WFS services return coordinates in (X,Y) order, while others use (Y,X). Setting this property to RT_OGCAxisOrder_swap will result in all coordinates in geometries being swapped from what was sent by the server. Setting to RT_OGCAxisOrder_noSwap will cause coordinates to be interpreted as-is. AxisOrder can be changed on an already-loaded table, but that change will only affect future calls to populateFromService. Features that are already in the table will not be modified. Defaults to RT_OGCAxisOrder_auto. In this mode, Runtime will make its best guess using heuristics that are optimized for good results with most popular WFS servers. Since: 100.5.0
member.value: The axis order, which defines how coordinates are interpreted.

member.value: The mode defining when features are requested from the service.

member.remarks: Some WFS services expect coordinates to be sent in (X,Y) order, while others use (Y,X). Use RT_OGCAxisOrder_swap to send coordinates in (Y,X) order. Use RT_OGCAxisOrder_noSwap to send coordinates in (X,Y) order. Defaults to RT_OGCAxisOrder_auto. Since: 100.5.0

member.summary: Populate the table using a query.
member.remarks: Use the default (empty) QueryParameters to get all features from the service. Specifying null or an empty RT_VectorHandle for outfields will result in the default set of outfields being used. WFS is only compatible with a subset of possible queries defined by QueryParameters. Non-overloaded method: PopulateFromService Since: 100.5.0

member.name: T:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreWMSLayer
member.summary: Displays data from a WMS service.
member.remarks:
The service may be hosted in the cloud on ArcGIS Online, on a third party server, or on-premises with ArcGIS Server. Web Map Service (WMS) is an Open Geospatial Consortium (OGC) standard for delivering map images from an online service. WMS layer displays data from a web service that provides maps in the form of server-rendered images. ArcGIS Runtime supports WMS versions 1.1.0, 1.1.1, and 1.3.0. The service may be hosted in the cloud on ArcGIS Online, on a third party server, or on-premises ArcGIS Server. Functional characteristics A WMS service can contain multiple layers in a hierarchy. A Wms layer can be constructed directly with a URL to a service and the uniquely identifying name of the desired layer. Alternatively, a RT_WMSServiceHandle can be used to programmatically explore the available layers and allow the user to choose layers at run time.
The maps provided by a WMS service use predefined symbology defined by the server. As a result, it is not possible to apply custom renderers or to visualize feature selection. WMS layers can have multiple style options. Your app can choose from the available styles.
Some layers can be marked as opaque, which means that they cover most of the map area and are good candidates for use as a basemap.
WMS layers support identify and time. They do not support selection or query. Note that due to the nature of WMS, it is not possible to retrieve feature geometry from WMS identify results. WMS layers support custom parameters, which can be specified for the service or an individual layer.
Performance characteristics WMS servers render map images on demand, which can require more server resources than a similar tiled service. WMS requires a service connection at all times. Since: 100.2.0

member.name: T:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.CoreWMTSLayer
member.summary: Displays data from a WMTS service by using pre-generated tiles.
member.remarks:
Web Map Tile Service (WMTS) is an Open GeospatialConsortium (OGC) standard for delivering geographic data via raster tiles. ArcGIS Runtime supports WMTS 1.0.0. The service may be hosted in the cloud on ArcGIS Online, on a third party server, or on-premises with ArcGIS Server. A WMTS layer uses pre-generated tiles to create a map instead of dynamically generating map images. Functional characteristics The maps provided by a WMTS service use predefined symbology defined by the server. As a result, it is not possible to apply custom renderers or to visualize feature selection.
A WMTS service can contain multiple layers in a hierarchy. A WMTS layer can be constructed directly with a URL to a service and the uniquely identifying name of the desired layer. Alternatively, a WMTS service can be used to programmatically explore the available layers and allow the user to choose layers at run time.
Performance characteristics WMTS layer consumes raster tiles that were prerendered by a server. WMTS requires fewer server resources than WMS because the images are rendered and cached ahead of time. WMTS layer requires a connection to the service at all times.
Creating a WMTS layer from URL For some WMTS services it may be necessary to provide a direct URI to the getCapabilities resource, by appending either /1.0.0/WMTSCapabilities.xml or ?service=wmts&request=getCapabilities&version=1.0.0 to the root WMTS URI. Since: 100.1.0

member.name: P:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.ICoreAPIKeyResource.APIKey
member.summary: Gets or sets the API key to access API key enabled services and resources in ArcGIS Online.
member.remarks: An API key is a unique key used to authorize access to specific services and resources in ArcGIS Online. It is also used to monitor access to those services. An API key is created and managed in the ArcGIS developer dashboard and is tied to a specific ArcGIS account. In addition to setting an API key at a global level for your application using the RT_ArcGISRuntimeEnvironment_getAPIKey property, you can set an RT_APIKeyResource_getAPIKey property on any ArcGIS Runtime class that implements RT_APIKeyResourceInterface. When you set an individual RT_APIKeyResource_getAPIKey property on an RT_APIKeyResourceInterface it will override the default key at the global level (on the RT_ArcGISRuntimeEnvironment_getAPIKey property, in other words), enabling more granular usage telemetry and management for ArcGIS Online resources used by your app. Classes that expose an API key property by implementing RT_APIKeyResourceInterface include: RT_BasemapHandle RT_ArcGISSceneLayerHandle RT_ArcGISTiledLayerHandle RT_ArcGISVectorTiledLayerHandle RT_ServiceFeatureTableHandle RT_ExportVectorTilesTaskHandle RT_LocatorTaskHandle RT_GeodatabaseSyncTaskHandle RT_ClosestFacilityTaskHandle RT_RouteTaskHandle RT_ServiceAreaTaskHandle RT_ExportTileCacheTaskHandle Since: 100.10.0
member.value: The API key to access API key enabled services and resources in ArcGIS Online.

member.name: T:RuntimeCoreNet.GeneratedWrappers.ICoreJSONSerializable
member.summary: A interface for reading and writing JSON.
member.remarks: This interface will be used when an Object needs to be read or written to JSON. These methods return a specific object and not the interface RT_JSONSerializableInterface. Objects implementing this interface have the ability to persist custom data to the JSON output. This custom data is stored as a RT_DictionaryHandle where the keys are strings that represent properties on the Object, and the values are strings that represent the JSON value for that corresponding property. Any custom data that causes malformed JSON when the Object is persisted will not be included in the JSON output. For example, if a key from the custom data matches a property on the Object and both were written out to JSON, it would result in malformed JSON. So in this example, the key in the custom data causing the malformed JSON would not be persisted. Since: 100.0.0
